title: Alibaba's AI Engine Is Roaring, but US Chip Curbs Threaten to Hit the Brakes
description:
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (NYSE:BABA) stock rose Thursday after the Chinese e-commerce giant reported mixed second-quarter results.
The technology giant is increasingly relying on artificial intelligence and cloud computing to drive growth. However, weaker e-commerce demand, rising capital spending and tighter U.S. chip restrictions are clouding its outlook.
Alibaba shares have fallen about 40% this year.
Earnings Snapshot
Alibaba reported quarterly revenue of $40.498 billion, up 10% year over year and above the $40.410 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted diluted earnings per American depositary share (ADS) rose 86% to $1.21, missing analyst expectations of $1.64.
Adjusted net income climbed 92% to $2.969 billion, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes and amortization (EBITA) surged 260% to $4.868 billion.
Net income jumped 213% to $9.608 billion, primarily driven by higher net investment income and stronger operating results.
AI Cloud Boom Offsets E-Commerce Weakness
AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue jumped 53% to $9.094 billion, driven by strong demand for AI and cloud computing services.
Revenue from external cloud customers climbed 64%, while recurring revenue from those customers rose 67%. The segment’s adjusted EBITA surged 121%, with its EBITA margin reaching 14.5%.
AI-related product revenue reached $2.673 billion, marking the 13th consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year growth.
However, Alibaba’s traditional e-commerce businesses faced challenges. Revenue from its China e-commerce business fell 5% to $14.691 billion amid weak consumer spending.
International e-commerce revenue declined 8% to $3.837 billion, primarily reflecting the impact of European Union customs reforms on AliExpress. Revenue growth at Trendyol partly offset the decline.
Despite those challenges, overall Alibaba E-commerce Group revenue rose 2% to $29.419 billion. China quick-commerce revenue grew 22% to $8.764 billion.
The broader e-commerce group’s adjusted EBITA surged 243% to $5.795 billion, driven by improved operating performance across its commerce businesses, including Taobao Instant Commerce.
US Chip Curbs Threaten Data Center Expansion
CEO Eddie Wu warned during the earnings call that new U.S. restrictions on China’s access to advanced computing chips could disrupt Alibaba’s data center expansion.
The restrictions could force Alibaba to scale back its previous goal of more than 20 gigawatts of global data center capacity by 2032, Bloomberg reported Thursday.
"Certainly the construction of data centers will experience some impact," Wu said, adding that the restrictions could also affect Alibaba’s overall capital spending plans.
However, management expects its proprietary chips to help cushion the impact. Alibaba is already training a next-generation Qwen AI model using its T-Head chips. Meanwhile, the company expects its Zhenwu V900 processor to enter mass production in early 2027.
Wu said cloud revenue growth could slow to between 30% and 45% in 2027, with a potential rebound to 50% or higher in calendar 2028 as domestic computing capacity improves.
AI Spending Drains Cash
Alibaba’s capital expenditures rose 60% to 50.477 billion yuan, reflecting continued investment in AI infrastructure. Free cash outflow widened to 34.472 billion yuan from 21.840 billion yuan a year earlier.
Meanwhile, Alibaba’s AI Labs and Applications segment recorded an adjusted EBITA loss of $1.567 billion, widening 206% year over year. The company attributed the increase to greater investment in AI capabilities and higher inference costs related to its Qwen app.
Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Robert Lea and Jasmine Lyu said heavy AI spending could continue to weigh on investment returns. They expect Alibaba’s AI business to generate cash losses over the next three years.
Alibaba’s outlook hinges on whether strong cloud demand and its domestic chip strategy can offset U.S. export restrictions, mounting investment costs and weakness in its core e-commerce business.
Alibaba Sticks to $100 Billion Cloud Revenue Goal
Despite the challenges, Wu reaffirmed Alibaba’s goal of reaching $100 billion in external cloud revenue by 2030, with an EBITDA margin of 20%.
Executives expect the proposed U.S. computing chip export controls to affect products and services in 2027. However, China’s domestic computing capacity has developed faster than management initially expected.
Management said it remains too early to assess the full impact of the new U.S. rules. Alibaba also said it has obtained and used computing resources in compliance with applicable laws and regulations and will continue to do so.
Executives expect computing resources to be most scarce in the Chinese domestic market in 2027 and 2028.
During that period, Alibaba expects its proprietary domestic chips to provide cost advantages and support gross margins in its cloud computing business.
BABA Price Action: Alibaba shares were up 2.95% at $86.86 at the time of publication on Thursday. The stock is trading near its 52-week low of $84.22, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Anthropic CEO addresses AI safety before ringing the Nasdaq opening bell
description:
Anthropic (ANT)  priced its IPO at $83 per share, ahead of its trading debut today. That's above earlier estimates of $80. The outlet previously reported that shares were oversubscribed by as much as 6x.
Anthropic, which Yahoo Finance named its Company of the Year for 2026, reported in its most recent amended S-1 that its third-quarter  revenue climbed to $17 billion, a 12x year over year increase.
For the nine months that ended Sept. 30, Anthropic's sales eclipsed $33 billion. It brought in $2.5 billion in all of 2025 and just $41 million in 2023.
Anthropic's sales continue to improve. Its number of customers spending more than $100,000 has increased from roughly 1,500 in December 2025 to more than 11,900 as of Sept. 30. Its computing efficiency has also jumped, meaning it's seeing more revenue per dollar spent on computing infrastructure.
"There's no real historical analogy for a company that has been this successful this fast," NYU Stern School of Business professor Arun Sundararajan told Yahoo Finance.
Anthropic's public debut also comes amid a wave of upheaval in the AI industry, ranging from market jitters to questions about the technology's impact on jobs.
It also faces plenty of competition from rival OpenAI (OPAI.PVT), as well as heavy hitters like Google (GOOG, GOOGL) and Meta (META).
Now the market will determine how that risk factors into the company's future prospects.


This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/live/anthropic-ipo-live-company-said-to-price-stock-at-83-begin-trading-thursday-212656452.html

title: Important Cardano News and ADA Price Update: November 19
description: Here's what has been making waves in the Cardano ecosystem lately.
fullContent:
Cardano remains in the spotlight thanks to several important ecosystem developments.

Meanwhile, its native token ADA continues to feel the pressure of the broader market downturn, plunging by 11% in the past week.

Goodbye DJED

One of the latest announcements coming from the Cardano ecosystem concerns DJED, the network’s overcollateralized stablecoin. The team revealed that the product and the reserve token SHEN will be shut down on December 31, 2026.

Users have been advised to redeem their holdings before the deadline, while those providing liquidity or using the assets in lending protocols should withdraw them beforehand. The protocol will continue operating and processing redemptions until the shutdown date.

DJED launched on the Cardano mainnet in January 2023 following a partnership between Input Output Global (IOG) and COTI.

Midnight’s Advancement

Cardano’s privacy-focused sister chain, Midnight, also made headlines after teaming up with CD Security.

The collaboration aims to secure elliptic-curve cryptography within a zero-knowledge (ZK) circuit, a key component of privacy-preserving blockchain applications.

Midnight has been presented as a next-generation network focused on protecting sensitive personal and business data, and the partnership represents another step toward strengthening its technological foundations.

Meanwhile, NIGHT (the chain’s native token) is among the few posting price gains over the past month. It currently trades near $0.04 (per CoinGecko), up 16% on a 30-day basis.

Hoskinson’s Reaction

Cardano’s founder Charles Hoskinson recently pushed back against claims that the project has reached the end of its road. The discussion emerged after some community members interpreted his remarks about completing the entity’s original roadmap as a sign that development was winding down.

Hoskinson clarified on X that he had “never once said Cardano is finished.” Instead, he suggested that the project is entering a new phase focused on fresh initiatives, technological improvements, and broader adoption.

ADA Price Outlook

Cardano’s native token is currently worth roughly $0.15, representing a 50% collapse from the local peak of around $0.30 in early October and an 11% weekly plunge. Its market capitalization dropped to approximately $5.8 billion, making ADA the 18th-largest cryptocurrency.

The most obvious reason for the downtrend appears to be broader market weakness, with Bitcoin (BTC) briefly tumbling below $62,000, Ethereum (ETH) slipping under $1,800, and Ripple (XRP) losing the $1 psychological level.

Volatility remains high due to Anthropic’s highly anticipated Nasdaq debut scheduled for today (November 19), so ADA and the rest of the market may endure additional short-term turbulence.

title: Bitcoin Reclaims $64K as Anthropic IPO Sparks Tech Market Recovery
description: Bitcoin reclaims $64K on Thursday after briefly approaching $62,000 overnight, as renewed optimism surrounding Anthropic’s record-breaking stock market debut helped lift technology shares and improve sentiment across financial markets. The recovery followed several difficult sessions for cryptocurrencies and technology stocks. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence chatbot, priced its expanded IPO and private […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin reclaims $64K on Thursday after briefly approaching $62,000 overnight, as renewed optimism surrounding Anthropic’s record-breaking stock market debut helped lift technology shares and improve sentiment across financial markets.

The recovery followed several difficult sessions for cryptocurrencies and technology stocks. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence chatbot, priced its expanded IPO and private placement at a combined $107 billion. Trading in the unofficial gray market suggested that its shares could open as much as 24% above the offering price when they begin trading on Nasdaq.

The development helped push Nasdaq 100 futures up nearly 2%, while the S&P 500 appeared positioned for its first daily advance in six sessions. Bitcoin gained alongside the improving mood, although concerns about further Federal Reserve rate increases continued to limit the recovery.

Anthropic’s Record IPO Lifts Technology Market Sentiment

Investor attention has shifted toward Anthropic’s highly anticipated Nasdaq debut, with the company’s offering attracting substantial interest ahead of its first official trading session.

The AI company priced its shares at $83, above the original proposed range of $70 to $78. Gray market activity, which allows investors to trade expectations before an official listing, indicated that shares could begin trading approximately 24% higher than the offering price.

The strong indication helped revive demand for technology exposure after several weeks of losses across the sector. Nasdaq 100 futures advanced almost 2%, while broader U.S. equity futures also improved. Alex Kuptsikevich, chief market analyst at FxPro, suggested that the IPO could eventually have a positive effect on cryptocurrency markets as well.

He previously identified Anthropic’s listing as a potential destination for risk-seeking capital. If investors had temporarily moved money into the offering, some of that capital could return to cryptocurrencies once the listing process progresses.

Anthropic shares are scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with quotations expected around 9:50 a.m. ET and trading anticipated to start approximately 10 a.m. ET on Thursday.

Bitcoin Faces Seventh Consecutive Weekly Decline

Despite Thursday’s rebound, Bitcoin remains under considerable pressure following weeks of losses.

The cryptocurrency dropped close to $62,000 overnight before recovering toward $64,000 during the early U.S. trading session. The move provided some relief after a prolonged downturn, but BTC remains on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

If the streak continues, it would become Bitcoin’s second-longest run of weekly losses on record, behind the nine-week decline recorded in 2022. Between weeks 40 and 46, Bitcoin fell from approximately $87,500 to a low near $62,000, highlighting the scale of the recent correction.

Another technical concern is Bitcoin’s position relative to its 200-week moving average, a long-term trend indicator that has historically attracted attention during major market downturns.

BTC was trading more than 7% below this average, marking its deepest move beneath the indicator in three years, according to Kuptsikevich. The analyst attributed the market’s weakness partly to concerns about a more aggressive Federal Reserve policy outlook.

Federal Reserve Rate-Hike Concerns Continue to Weigh on Crypto

Although Anthropic’s IPO improved sentiment across technology markets, monetary policy remains a significant obstacle for Bitcoin and other risk-sensitive assets.

Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s latest meeting indicated that some policymakers were prepared to support interest-rate increases larger than the usual 25-basis-point adjustment.

That possibility has raised concerns about additional tightening and its potential impact on financial conditions. Higher interest rates can reduce appetite for speculative investments by making cash and fixed-income assets more attractive. Kuptsikevich described the market as being unsettled by the possibility of a double rate hike and the risk of further aggressive tightening.

This uncertainty helps explain why Bitcoin’s recovery has remained relatively modest despite the improvement in U.S. stock futures. Other major cryptocurrencies showed limited movement during the same period. Ether held near $1,800, XRP slipped approximately 1% and remained below $1, while TRX gained around 1%.

Can Anthropic’s record-breaking Nasdaq debut help restore demand for Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies? Will BTC manage to break its seven-week losing streak, or will expectations of further Fed tightening continue to pressure prices?

title: Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage
Coinbase opened crypto spot margin trading in the U.S. with up to 10x leverage, but only for eligible contract participants with more than $10 million invested.
This post Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Coinbase Launches U.S. Spot Margin Trading With Up to 10x Leverage

Coinbase (COIN) has opened crypto spot margin trading to U.S. customers, letting eligible traders borrow to go long or short with up to 10x leverage, the exchange announced Wednesday, though access is limited to investors with more than $10 million invested.

“Crypto spot margin is now available in the US for eligible traders,” Coinbase wrote on X. Traders borrow at the moment they place an order, rather than setting up a loan first.

The eligibility bar is high. In a follow-up post, Coinbase said margin trading is open only to people who qualify as “eligible contract participants” under the Commodity Exchange Act. For an individual, that generally means more than $10 million in assets invested on a discretionary basis.

The product is also not available in all states, and the loans are for commercial or business purposes only, the company said. Coinbase did not list eligible states or assets in the posts.

The limit tracks how U.S. law treats leverage. Under the Commodity Exchange Act, leveraged retail commodity trades generally have to run through a regulated futures exchange, so off-exchange margin products like this one are often reserved for eligible contract participants.

How spot margin works

Coinbase first described spot margin in October. Eligible traders can borrow against collateral to increase their buying power on spot markets, with leverage of up to 10x on selected major assets and up to 5x on other supported assets.

Collateral can be posted in more than 15 supported assets and stays on Coinbase throughout. Loan balances, collateral levels and margin health appear in real time, and spot positions sit in the same margin portfolio as a trader’s derivatives.

Trump leaves China after historic talks with Xi and 'friend' Putin
description:
President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin sat down together in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in a rare face-to-face encounter for the leaders of three of the world's most powerful countries, but there appeared to be little concrete to show for the meeting in terms of resolving any of the crises facing the world.
The leaders offered a joint statement after their roughly hour-and-a-half-long meeting. Mr. Trump immediately left for his return flight to the U.S. without speaking to journalists on the ground.
The presidents discussed Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine, which Mr. Trump has wanted to bring to a negotiated end. But the only significant statement on the conflict came after the meeting from Putin, who ruled out any direct negotiations with Ukraine, citing a major strike earlier this week by Ukrainian forces on a key bridge in Russian-held Crimea.  
Putin's senior aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the meeting that the atmosphere had been good, and the Kremlin quickly released what it called a joint statement from all three leaders characterizing the talks. The White House later provided the same statement.

The three men "exchanged views in detail on the current international situation and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security," the readout said, adding that as permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, they had "reaffirmed their commitment to reforming the UN so that it can more effectively respond to global challenges and fulfill its fundamental mission in the area of international peace and security."
They also committed to increasing gas and oil production "for the benefit of all countries," agreed on the "fundamental importance" of "the principle of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials," and said the "International Criminal Court and other similar bodies should not abuse their powers."
Finally, the leaders "reaffirmed that there can be no winners in a nuclear war, and that it should never be unleashed."
The White House indicated that Mr. Trump might speak with reporters on Air Force One during the flight back to the U.S.
"A great relationship"
The Kremlin shared a short video on social media, via Russian state media, showing Xi accompanying Putin as they walked out of the meeting to Putin's waiting motorcade. Before they exit the building, Putin is seen shaking Xi's hand, thanking him for hosting the gathering and telling him, according to Russian state media, that nobody had expected it to go so well. 
Before the meeting, Mr. Trump met separately with Putin on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, and then with Xi.
"We've had a great relationship for many years," Mr. Trump said, standing alongside his Russian counterpart. "I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start."
As Mr. Trump approached Putin for a handshake, he said, "Who is that?" before laughing and saying, "He's my friend."
Focus on Ukraine
Russia's TASS news agency said the war in Ukraine was the main topic discussed by the two leaders, and that Putin left the meeting in "an excellent mood."
After the trilateral talks Thursday, Putin told reporters that Ukraine and Europe were "not yet ready" to make the compromises necessary to resolve the war, according to Russian media. 
"We will not negotiate after the attacks on the Crimean bridge," he declared, referring to this week's Ukrainian strike on the highly symbolic Kerch Bridge, which links Russia with Ukraine's Russian-occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Putin said Kyiv and Europe would eventually come to understand that it is better to make compromises than to face "realities." 
Ukraine and its European partners have long feared that the White House appears willing to offer Putin too much — including the prospect of major energy deals — with no significant concessions from Russia  in return, while putting pressure on Kyiv to make major territorial concessions without any concrete security guarantees. 
Mr. Trump then met for about an hour with Xi ahead of the three-way meeting. As the Trump-Xi session began, Xi told Mr. Trump relations between China and the United States were "stable and improved."
Mr. Trump told reporters he had spoken with Xi for two hours on Wednesday, with trade and tariffs being the main topics. He also said he would be asking China to "do some more" for American farmers, because China has an "insatiable appetite."     
Mr. Trump said previously that he planned to talk about denuclearization with his fellow leaders. Russia and the United States are by far the world's largest holders of nuclear weapons, with stockpiles estimated at well over 5,000 warheads, while China is believed to be a distant third, with about 600 weapons. 
Putin has made denuclearization a key talking point for decades, but both he and Mr. Trump have allowed previous treaties intended to limit nuclear proliferation to lapse in recent years. China, which has been building up its nuclear program, ruled out taking part in any denuclearization talks with the U.S. and Russia as recently as last year.
China's state-run Xinhua news agency quoted Xi, however, as saying ahead of the trilateral meeting on Thursday that nuclear weapons were a "sword of Damocles hanging over humanity," and calling for them to be "completely banned and completely destroyed, leading to a world free of nuclear weapons."
The Kremlin said in its readout of the three-way meeting that it would "continue dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons" with China and the U.S.
A range of other global challenges lingered in the background of the trilateral meeting, including the war in Iran and tension over trade and artificial intelligence.

Global trade and AI
The summit took place in the capital of the Chinese tech industry, a sector that has drawn intense scrutiny in recent weeks amid worries that advanced U.S. computer chips are surreptitiously reaching China. The scandal was sparked by allegations that now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman and suspected Chinese intelligence asset, Alice Huang, whose company is accused of diverting Nvidia's coveted AI chips to China. Beijing has dismissed claims that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy as "groundless speculation" and "nothing more than an attempt to smear China."
Mr. Trump — an ally of Jensen Huang's — had previously told reporters he may bring up the businesswoman during his meetings in China, though he said, "I don't know that she is a spy." Her firm, Megaspeed, is under Justice Department investigation. It has denied wrongdoing. 
Shortly after the concerns about Jensen Huang surfaced, the Trump administration issued a new rule aimed at curbing China and other countries' ability to remotely access advanced AI chips. China and the U.S. have also discussed broader AI policy issues in recent months, including setting up a communication channel to share information when AI systems go haywire.
Mr. Trump brought up AI during a speech at the APEC forum earlier in the day, vowing to block any "globalist regulation" of artificial intelligence.
"We do not want to do anything to destroy the tremendous potential of this technology," he said. "We have to watch it, we have to be careful, we have to cherish it. It's almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements, so we have to be very careful in managing those bad elements."
Beyond AI, the U.S. and China have sought to stabilize their economic relationship over the last year, following a tit-for-tat trade war that sent tariffs above 100% in 2025. A tariff truce between the two countries is set to expire on Jan. 10 of next year.
Mr. Trump said in his APEC speech the U.S. is committed to "growth and stability" in the Asia-Pacific region, and argued the American economy is "thriving like it has never thrived before." He also said the U.S. is negotiating "numerous trade agreements" and expects to sign some agreements with APEC members in the near future.
During Xi's remarks earlier in the session, the Chinese leader called on countries in the region to "look out for each other" and "expand our shared interests," including on free trade and economic growth.

Foreign conflicts loomed large during the Trump-Putin-Xi talks. Iran is one contentious area, given China's status as one of the largest customers of Iranian oil, and Russia's ties with Iran.
The White House previously said the war in Ukraine would not be a topic of discussion since no Ukrainian representatives will be present. But on Monday, Mr. Trump said he expected the issue to come up, calling it "my favorite subject."
Taiwan is another frequent discussion topic between the U.S. and China. During the U.S. president's visit to Beijing in the spring, Xi reportedly delivered a stern warning about the island, which he has long vowed to reintegrate with mainland China, floating potential "clashes and even conflicts" if the issue isn't "handled properly."
And Mr. Trump was expected to press Xi to release two detained Americans during his visit to China, CBS News has reported. Beijing has resisted repeated U.S. calls for their release.
This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-xi-putin-china-apec-summit/

title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4 million after row over its Nazi history
description:
Watch: Moment Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m (£144.8m)

Auction house Sotheby's has sold a painting by Vincent van Gogh for a record $190.4m (£144.8m).
The sale of Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom") shatters the renowned artist's previous auction record of $117.2 million set in 2022.
The historic sale in New York on Wednesday comes after an eleventh-hour agreement was reached to resolve a dispute regarding claims the art piece was previously sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.
Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Van Gogh's life. It is considered one of the most important works of art from that period to remain in private hands, according to Sotheby's.

Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
It was not immediately clear who purchased the painting. The BBC has contacted Sotheby's for comment.
The oil painting, which was estimated to carry a value of $180m (£136m) prior to the sale, was put up for auction as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.
Sotheby's announced in the hours before the auction that it had resolved a dispute between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - regarding the sale.
Representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family had claimed the painting may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.
A lawyer for the family's heirs reportedly wrote to Sotheby's on their behalf, telling the auction house that the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment. 
"In recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution and the work will be sold pursuant to their agreement," Sotheby's said on Wednesday.
Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890.
It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it in 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934.
The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotheby's said.
Four other owners then had the painting.
The Blaquier family acquired it in 1975 and owned it for more than half a century before the latest sale, the auction house said.


Sotheby's staff handle the "Châtaigniers en fleurs" painting by Vincent van Gogh at an auction preview in Hong Kong last month [Getty Images]

title: Anthropic’s IPO Deal Surpasses SpaceX as Bitcoin and Tech Stocks Rebound
description: Anthropic’s IPO deal is preparing for a major Nasdaq debut after pricing its initial public offering at $83 per share, putting the artificial intelligence company behind Claude at the center of one of the largest capital raises in financial market history. Combined with a planned $26 billion private placement, the transaction is expected to reach […]
fullContent:
Anthropic’s IPO deal is preparing for a major Nasdaq debut after pricing its initial public offering at $83 per share, putting the artificial intelligence company behind Claude at the center of one of the largest capital raises in financial market history.

Combined with a planned $26 billion private placement, the transaction is expected to reach approximately $107 billion, exceeding the $86 billion raised by SpaceX in its June listing. The offering arrives at a challenging moment for technology stocks. Concerns about AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the sustainability of the sector’s growth have weighed on major companies in recent weeks. However, investor interest in Anthropic’s listing helped lift market sentiment ahead of its Thursday debut.

Bitcoin also showed signs of recovering, trading just below $64,000 after gaining more than 1% over the previous 24 hours.

Anthropic’s $107 Billion Deal Sets a New IPO Benchmark

Anthropic priced its shares at $83, exceeding the upper end of its original $70–$78 offering range. The company and its shareholders sold a combined 980 million shares, generating approximately $81 billion through Anthropic’s ipo deal.

A separate $26 billion private placement involving strategic investors, including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, brings the total transaction to roughly $107 billion. That figure puts Anthropic ahead of SpaceX’s $86 billion IPO haul, which included the underwriters’ additional share option.

The offering values Anthropic at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, while its basic market capitalization stands just above $1 trillion. Underwriters also have the option to sell another 147 million shares, potentially adding around $12 billion to the public offering.

The company is scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Tokenized versions of its shares are also expected to become available through blockchain-based platforms. BNB Chain is set to support offerings through bStocks, Ondo and xStocks, while Backpack Securities plans to issue a version on Solana.

AI Stocks Remain Under Pressure Despite Anthropic’s Strong Debut

Anthropic’s listing comes as the broader technology sector continues to face a significant correction. The Nasdaq 100 remains approximately 14% below its October record, while the S&P 500 is down around 7% from its peak.

Several companies exposed to AI infrastructure have suffered particularly steep losses. Shares of cloud-computing providers such as CoreWeave, Cipher Digital and IREN have fallen by as much as 70% from their highs. Meanwhile, chipmakers including Sandisk, Micron Technology and Marvell Technology have lost approximately half their value.

The pressure reflects growing concerns about the enormous costs associated with expanding AI infrastructure and whether future demand will justify current valuations.

Nvidia’s removal of CEO Jensen Huang has added another source of uncertainty. Huang played a major role in the AI boom through the company’s chip business, investments and partnerships, making the leadership development particularly relevant to investors assessing the sector’s direction.

Despite the recent declines, Anthropic’s pricing above its initial range points to substantial demand for exposure to leading AI companies. Its first trading sessions could therefore offer an important indication of whether investors remain willing to commit capital to the sector.

Bitcoin Approaches $64,000 as Market Sentiment Improves

Bitcoin entered Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut after an extended period of weakness. The cryptocurrency was heading toward its seventh consecutive weekly decline, a losing streak that would be surpassed only by its nine-week run of losses in 2022. BTC remained approximately 27% below its September high near $87,000, highlighting the pressure that has continued to affect the broader crypto market.

However, markets showed signs of stabilizing ahead of Thursday’s opening bell. Nasdaq 100 futures advanced more than 2% in premarket trading, while Bitcoin and gold each gained over 1% during the preceding 24 hours. Bitcoin was changing hands just below $64,000 at the time of reporting.

The recovery suggests that investors were becoming more willing to take on market exposure following several weeks of selling. Still, one strong trading session does not necessarily signal that the broader correction has ended.

Anthropic’s debut could provide a useful test of investor appetite for high-growth technology companies, while Bitcoin’s ability to hold its recent recovery will remain an important indicator of sentiment across risk assets.

Will Anthropic’s record-breaking debut restore confidence in AI and technology stocks? Can Bitcoin extend its recovery toward higher levels, or will persistent market uncertainty trigger another round of selling?

title: Walmart's Weight-Loss Drug Windfall Is Losing Steam
description:
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) stock fell in Thursday’s premarket session despite the retail giant reporting better-than-expected third-quarter fiscal 2027 results and raising its full-year outlook again.
Earnings Snapshot
Adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share exceeded analyst expectations of 64 cents. The figure excludes an after-tax loss of 3 cents per share related to equity and other investments.
Revenue rose 5.2% year over year to $188.835 billion, topping the consensus estimate of $187.271 billion. On a constant-currency basis, revenue increased 4.5%.
Global e-commerce net sales increased 17%, accounting for 24% of total net sales. Membership and other income grew 20%, driven by a 17% increase in global membership fee revenue and higher miscellaneous income.
The gross profit rate expanded 28 basis points to 24.5%, reflecting a more favorable business and merchandise mix at Walmart U.S.
The timing of Flipkart’s Big Billion Days sales event also benefited Walmart International’s gross profit rate. However, lower fuel margins at Sam’s Club U.S. partially offset those gains.
On a constant-currency basis, adjusted operating income increased 5.5% year over year, outpacing net sales growth of 4.4%.
Stronger sales, higher gross margins, global membership growth and additional miscellaneous income drove the increase. However, expenses growing faster than sales limited those gains.
During Thursday’s earnings call, a Walmart executive warned that elevated diesel prices could prolong fuel and transportation cost pressures.
“We’ve had some cost pressures throughout the year on fuel and transportation. I think some of those will remain true as long as diesel fuel remains elevated,” the executive said.
Global inventory increased 8.1%, reflecting strategic initiatives, the timing of seasonal events and inflation-related cost increases.
Walmart repurchased $2.7 billion in shares during the quarter, leaving $22.4 billion under its share repurchase authorization.
Walmart U.S. Performance
Walmart U.S. net sales rose 3.6% year over year to $125 billion, while e-commerce sales increased 23%.
Excluding fuel, comparable sales grew 2.9%, driven by a 1.5% increase in transactions and a 1.4% rise in average transaction value.
Pharmacy deflation created a net headwind of approximately 70 basis points to comparable sales growth. Like-for-like inflation stood at 1.2%.
Store-fulfilled delivery grew more than 40%, supporting e-commerce growth. Meanwhile, marketplace sales jumped 49%, and the advertising business grew 37%.
Membership and other income surged 43%, reflecting double-digit Walmart+ membership revenue growth and higher miscellaneous income. The increase also included fees from the company’s bundled membership offering.
Walmart introduced a new $120 annual membership package in the U.S., combining Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus.
Walmart International Performance
Walmart International net sales increased 3.3% year over year to $34.7 billion on a constant-currency basis. Higher unit volumes and customer transactions drove growth across markets.
However, the timing of Flipkart’s Big Billion Days sales event reduced growth by approximately 500 basis points. Walmart expects a corresponding benefit in the fourth quarter.
E-commerce sales declined 2%, primarily due to the event’s timing.
Membership fee revenue jumped 29%, contributing to a 16.4% increase in membership and other income. Favorable currency movements boosted reported sales by $1.2 billion.
Walmart Raises Full-Year Outlook
Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings forecast to $2.84-$2.89 per share from $2.80-$2.87. Analysts expect earnings of $2.88 per share.
The retailer also lifted its full-year revenue forecast to $741.01 billion-$743.13 billion from $734.66 billion-$741.72 billion. However, the revised range remains below the analyst consensus estimate of $752.65 billion.
Walmart expects fiscal 2027 net sales to increase 4.9% to 5.2% year over year.
Walmart forecast fourth-quarter sales of $199.236 billion to $201.142 billion, compared with the analyst consensus estimate of $200.106 billion.
GLP-1 Sales Benefit Narrows
Walmart’s weight-loss drug windfall is losing steam despite rising prescription volumes. 
The retailer expects GLP-1 medications to deliver a 40% smaller boost to U.S. comparable sales growth this fiscal year than in each of the previous two years, as unfavorable pricing and shifts in product mix erode their sales contribution.
It expects GLP-1 medications to contribute approximately 60 basis points to fiscal 2027 U.S. comparable sales growth, excluding fuel. That compares with approximately 100 basis points in both fiscal 2025 and 2026.
Unfavorable pricing and product mix more than offset prescription volume growth, reducing the contribution from GLP-1 medications.
During the third quarter, pharmacy deflation and shifts from brand-name to generic prescriptions related to maximum fair price regulation created a headwind of approximately 125 basis points. Growth primarily from GLP-1 medications partially offset that pressure.
WMT Price Action: Walmart shares were down 1.04% at $126.03 during premarket trading on Thursday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

The offering is one of the most closely watched listings of the year and has drawn strong interest from crypto platforms, several of which are offering tokenized access to the stock around the debut.

For crypto traders, tokenized stocks offer a way to follow companies like Anthropic without leaving the crypto ecosystem, using stablecoins and the same accounts they already use for digital assets.

What Is ANTx

ANTx is a tokenized stock from xStocks that tracks the price of Anthropic shares. According to information published for the launch, each ANTx token is backed 1:1 by Anthropic shares held in custody by Backed Assets (JE) Limited. ANTx holders gain price exposure to Anthropic, but do not receive shareholder or voting rights.

On Bitrue, ANTx trades on the spot market against USDT.

Bitrue’s Anthropic Product Lineup

With the ANTx listing, Bitrue now offers three ways to trade Anthropic-related products:

  • ANTx spot trading (xStocks): spot trading of the tokenized Anthropic stock against USDT, available from day one.
  • ANT/USDT perpetual futures: a USDT-settled perpetual futures contract tracking Anthropic, live on Bitrue Futures since Nov. 17. This product is separate from xStocks and is supported by Bitrue’s RWA trading event.
  • ANT3L and ANT3S leveraged tokens: leveraged long and short tokens linked to Anthropic, expected to list on Nov. 20. These are also separate from xStocks.

Together, the three products let traders choose how they follow Anthropic, from spot exposure through a tokenized stock to futures and leveraged tokens.

Trade & Earn: 20,000 USDT Prize Pool

To mark the ANTx listing, Bitrue is running a Trade & Earn campaign for ANTx spot trading:

  • Prize pool: 20,000 USDT shared among eligible traders.
  • Per-person cap: up to 1,250 USDT per participant.
  • How to join: register through the campaign page and trade ANTx on the Bitrue spot market during the campaign period.

Full campaign rules, including the campaign period and eligibility, are available on the campaign page.

“Anthropic’s public debut is one of the biggest moments of the year at the intersection of AI and markets, and our users want to be part of it,” Bitrue said in a statement. “By supporting ANTx from day one, alongside ANT futures and leveraged tokens, we are giving our users several ways to follow Anthropic from the same account they use for crypto.”

Part of Bitrue’s Growing RWA Range

The ANTx listing adds to Bitrue’s growing range of real-world asset markets. Bitrue users can already trade USDT-settled products linked to gold, well-known US technology stocks and other traditional assets, with recent additions including MercadoLibre (MELI), NuScale Power (SMR) and the iShares MSCI Brazil Small-Cap ETF (EWZS). The full range is available on Bitrue’s RWA & TradFi page.

ANTx, ANT/USDT perpetual futures and ANT3L/ANT3S leveraged tokens do not represent ownership of Anthropic shares and do not carry shareholder rights. Perpetual futures and leveraged tokens are complex products with significant risk, and leveraged tokens can lose value quickly in volatile markets. Availability depends on the user’s jurisdiction. title: Trump Signs Thailand Trade Deal: Which Stocks Will Benefit?
description:
Thailand says the US will cut its forced-labor tariff to 10%. See which tariffs change and which stocks could benefit.
The post Trump Signs Thailand Trade Deal: Which Stocks Will Benefit? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Donald Trump has announced a major trade deal with Thailand, promising lower US tariffs in exchange for greater access to the Thai market. But the agreement could create very different outcomes for investors.

Some Thai companies stand to gain from cheaper imports, while American exporters could win new business.

On Tuesday, Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint statement in Manila. Thailand subsequently announced that Washington had agreed to reduce its additional forced-labor tariff from 12.5% to 10%.

The reduction would bring Thailand in line with Malaysia and Indonesia. However, it has no implementation date, and the final agreement remains unfinished.

Which Stocks Could Benefit From Trump’s Thailand Deal?

The tariff cut could help Thai food and rubber exporters. However, computers, hard drives and semiconductors were already exempt.

In July, Kasikorn Securities identified Thai Union (TU), Sri Trang Agro-Industry (STA), KCE Electronics and Delta Electronics (DELTA) as potential beneficiaries.

Its latest assessment is more cautious, rating the deal neutral for Thailand’s stock market.

Still, the brokerage identified several potential winners:

  • CPF, BTG and GFPT: Cheaper American corn could increase earnings by 1%–3%.
  • BDMS, Bumrungrad (BH) and Praram 9 (PR9): Lower import costs for American medicines and medical equipment could improve margins.

American agricultural exporters also stand to benefit from Thailand’s proposed $2.6 billion in annual purchases. 

Boeing could benefit from an earlier commitment to purchase 80 US aircraft worth $18.8 billion.

Why Investors Remain Cautious

Trump declared:

“Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports.”

Thai officials say existing tariffs remain until the agreement takes effect. Domestic farmers also face potential competition from American imports.

Meanwhile, Thailand’s SET Index fell 1.66% on Tuesday, amid concerns over separate US chip export restrictions.

Investors now await the final tariff schedule and details of Thailand’s import commitments. A separate US investigation into excess manufacturing capacity could introduce further tariffs, leaving exporters facing additional uncertainty.

The post Trump Signs Thailand Trade Deal: Which Stocks Will Benefit? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

The rally also follows heightened concerns about digital infrastructure security, growing demand for AI protection and NVIDIA Corp.’s (NASDAQ:NVDA) quarterly earnings beat.

Palo Alto Earnings Beat Signals Strong Cybersecurity Demand

Palo Alto reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $3.45 billion, up 39% year over year and above estimates of $3.31 billion. Adjusted EPS of $1.05 also topped expectations.

Next-generation security annual recurring revenue surged 66% to $9.73 billion, while remaining performance obligations reached $21 billion.

Chairman and CEO Nikesh Arora said companies were tapping "emergency funds" for AI defense.

"You’ll see cyber budgets rise, I’m sure, in the next two years," Arora said, adding that critical and severe vulnerabilities were being discovered at nearly seven times last year’s monthly average.

Technology Outages Put Cybersecurity Stocks in Focus

Recent outages affecting Microsoft systems and critical infrastructure have drawn attention to digital resilience, although the disruptions have not been established as connected cyberattacks.

The countdown is on: Zscaler is set to report earnings on December 2, 2026 (confirmed).

title: Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin
A Bank of Russia official said retail investors will be able to trade crypto on margin up to 300,000 rubles, with the first crypto funds for qualified investors expected in 2027.
This post Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin

Russia’s central bank plans to let ordinary investors trade bitcoin and other crypto on margin, capped at 300,000 rubles with a broker, a senior Bank of Russia official said this week, days after retail buying became legal.

Olga Shishlyannikova, director of the central bank’s department of investment financial intermediaries, outlined the plan at the Ural Conference hosted by NAUFOR, the national association of securities market participants, RBC Investments reported. She said the margin rule and two other acts are under review at Russia’s Justice Ministry, and the regulator expects them to be registered by the end of 2026.

It is not yet clear whether the 300,000-ruble margin limit for non-qualified investors will be shared with the existing cap on crypto purchases or counted separately.

The central bank first published draft margin rules in July. Under that draft, brokers could accept cryptocurrencies as collateral for margin positions, and their clients could sell short. Both qualified and non-qualified investors would be able to trade on margin, with retail crypto trades subject to limits set by the Bank of Russia.

The draft also added crypto to the risk-coverage ratios brokers use to police leveraged trades. Those ratios set how far a broker can lend against a client’s portfolio and when positions are forcibly closed.

Crypto funds expected in 2027

Shishlyannikova also said the central bank expects the first Russian mutual funds that hold crypto directly to appear in 2027. Professional market participants have already filed applications to register such funds, she said.

“Yes, we are considering the possibility next year of amending the relevant regulations to allow funds intended for qualified investors to buy cryptocurrency,” Shishlyannikova said. The regulator is not considering the same access for funds sold to non-qualified investors, she added.

In late September, the central bank allowed fund managers to invest qualified investors’ money in cash-settled instruments tied to crypto prices, in a directive registered with the Justice Ministry. The proposed change would let those funds hold the coins themselves.

Futures for retail can wait

Retail access to crypto futures will take longer. Deputy Governor Philipp Gabunia told reporters on Thursday that the Bank of Russia could let non-qualified investors trade crypto-linked futures once the spot market is running, if it sees no risks, Interfax reported.

“For non-qualified investors, this could be a very sensitive story. Let’s launch, and now we’ll see how it starts to work,” Gabunia said. “If we don’t see risks, we’ll allow it. Non-qualified investors will have to be a little patient.”

Gabunia said the market’s shape could still shift, including which coins are admitted and which derivatives are offered on them. “Legislation is now changing this configuration a lot,” he said.

He said the central bank does not expect “super-large” turnover on Russia’s crypto market. Qualified investors can already trade futures tied to bitcoin, ether, Solana, XRP and Tron on Russian exchanges. Gabunia did not give a timeline for retail access.

Russia’s law on digital currencies took effect Sept. 1, setting up rules for crypto trading through exchanges, brokers and trust managers, plus new crypto exchange offices and digital depositories. Qualified investors were cleared to buy crypto from that date.

The comments fill in the next steps on a calendar that has moved quickly this month. Since Nov. 17, non-qualified investors in Russia have been able to buy bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT through brokers and crypto exchange offices, capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary, or roughly $3,600.

A separate central bank ordinance lets exchanges open organized crypto trading from Nov. 22, once the regulator approves their trading rules. Moscow Exchange, which is under U.S. sanctions, has said it plans to list bitcoin on Dec. 1, initially as a pilot.

This post Russia’s Central Bank to Let Retail Investors Trade Bitcoin on Margin first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Gate Security Academy | Gate & GoPlus: How to Read Audit Reports and Identify Smart Contract Vulnerabilities
description:
Gate has published the second edition of Gate Security Academy, produced together with Web3 security provider GoPlus Security. This edition examines what smart contract audits can and cannot establish, and how users can assess a project’s security beyond an audit report. Gate Security Academy is a series dedicated to the different types of security issues
The post Gate Security Academy | Gate & GoPlus: How to Read Audit Reports and Identify Smart Contract Vulnerabilities appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Gate has published the second edition of Gate Security Academy, produced together with Web3 security provider GoPlus Security.

This edition examines what smart contract audits can and cannot establish, and how users can assess a project’s security beyond an audit report. Gate Security Academy is a series dedicated to the different types of security issues in the crypto industry, drawing on real cases that users may encounter in everyday life and bringing together insights from both the platform and the security provider perspective.

Security is a dynamic state, not a certificate on a piece of paper.

Many projects that suffered hacks this year had already undergone security audits. Some had even been audited multiple times. This does not mean audits are worthless. It simply means that the questions an audit can answer are far narrower than most people assume.

An audit report describes a particular version of a project, reviewed by a particular team, at a particular point in time. But contracts can be upgraded, permissions can change, and the oracles and cross-chain bridges that projects depend on can change as well. New attack techniques emerge every week.

The moment an audit report is delivered, it begins to become outdated.

Even more concerning are older contracts that were deployed years ago and successfully passed audits at the time. These contracts are now being scanned again in large batches. Deep vulnerabilities in contracts that have been live for years can sometimes be discovered in just over ten minutes.

In this edition, GoPlus Security and the Gate Security Team discuss smart contract audits and vulnerability detection from the perspectives of both a security provider and a trading platform.

Why do audited projects still get hacked? How should users read an audit report? What checks do trading platforms perform before and after listing a token? And how can ordinary users conduct their own checks before signing a transaction?

Guest Introductions

Adam, Partner at GoPlus: Adam is a Partner at GoPlus and Head of its Security Research Institute.

GoPlus Security is building the first decentralized security layer for Web3 and AI. By combining blockchain technology with cutting-edge AI security solutions, it provides users with intelligent, efficient, and decentralized security products and services.

Since 2022, GoPlus has grown to 30 million API calls per day and helping users prevent nearly $100 billion in potential losses.

Gate Security Team: Gate’s security department is responsible for building and maintaining the platform’s account, trading, and asset security systems. The team also regularly handles user appeals involving suspicious account activity and requests for assistance with investigations.

Founded in 2013, Gate was one of the first major exchanges to commit to 100% proof of reserves and currently serves more than 63 million users worldwide. Security is the foundation that makes this business possible. Through Gate Security Academy, Gate aims to explain the common mechanisms behind the real security risks users may encounter.

Q1. Why do so many projects still get hacked or experience abuse of privileges even after passing security audits?

Adam, Partner at GoPlus:

A one-time audit does not mean a project will remain secure forever. Traditional smart contract auditing services now face four structural limitations.

Snapshot-based reviews. An audit is essentially a semi-manual inspection conducted by security engineers at a particular point in time. Its effectiveness depends on the quality of the tools, the expertise of the individual auditors, and their working conditions. But contract code can be upgraded, administrative permissions can change, and configuration parameters can be adjusted. From the moment a one-time audit report is delivered, it starts becoming outdated.

Inability to predict future threats. New vulnerability types and attack techniques continue to emerge. Historical audits cannot cover risks that have not yet appeared.

Uncontrolled external dependencies. Projects commonly rely on oracles, cross-chain bridges, and third-party protocols. Changes in the risks associated with these dependencies fall outside the scope of traditional audits.

Vulnerabilities emerging in older contracts. Contracts deployed several years ago that passed audits at the time are now being scanned in batches using automated tools, uncovering previously undetected vulnerabilities. Examples include deep vulnerabilities in established DeFi protocols that remained undiscovered for years after their official launches.

As for the abuse of privileges, it occurs more often during the operational stage than in the contract code itself.

Common causes include excessive owner privileges, such as the ability to mint tokens at will, blacklist addresses, or pause trading; compromised administrator private keys; improper multisignature management; malicious proposals; and governance attacks.

These are all security issues that can arise during ongoing operations.

Even if an audit report identifies permission-related risks, who monitors those permissions afterward? And who determines whether subsequent actions are secure and reasonable? A traditional audit cannot answer these questions.

Launching a contract after an audit is only the beginning of security work, not the end.

What projects need is continuous security throughout the entire contract lifecycle, rather than a one-time audit report.

Gate Security Team:

An audit can tell users what the code is capable of doing, but it cannot tell them what the project team intends to do.

This is one of the most important lessons we have learned from years of token listing reviews.

Many incidents are rooted in the intentions of the project team.

A contract can be technically compliant, with owner permissions designed within normal parameters, yet the project team can still choose a particular moment to exercise those permissions: changing trading rules, enabling blacklists, or minting additional tokens.

From a code perspective, these actions are entirely legitimate. An audit report will not necessarily flag them as vulnerabilities because they are part of the contract’s intended design.

That is why technical audits need an additional layer of safeguards.

At Gate, we conduct strict project screening and reviews during the token listing process. We also require project teams to sign declarations committing not to engage in malicious conduct, and we monitor their compliance with those commitments.

This additional layer is intended to address what audits cannot: the absence of code vulnerabilities does not guarantee that a project team will never make decisions that harm users.

For projects that have already been listed, we conduct regular security audits and use on-chain event monitoring to track contract status.

Users can also check the current risk indicators of a particular contract at any time.

Q2. If a one-time audit does not guarantee lasting security, how should project teams and the industry adapt?

Gate Security Team:

The crypto industry has a structural characteristic: a large portion of its business, especially DeFi, operates much like modular finance.

Different platforms are built from shared components, including contracts, software libraries, wallets, price oracles, cross-chain bridges, connectivity providers, web interfaces, and systems used to distribute updates.

That means the question is not only whether a project’s own contracts are secure, but whether every component it depends on remains reliable.

If an upstream component fails, losses can spread down the entire chain of dependencies.

Looking back at major attacks, the problem often originated somewhere outside the protocol’s core logic: a supplier, a development tool, the way software reached users, or the process through which users approved transfers.

Adam, Partner at GoPlus:

A new attack model has already taken shape and is spreading rapidly: hackers use automated tools to discover vulnerabilities efficiently.

Attacks have evolved from manual research conducted by specialists into an assembly-line process.

If the industry’s approach remains limited to hiring an audit firm to produce a report before launch, or calling a security company only after a problem has been discovered, it is like trying to fight a machine gun with a bow and arrow.

The only effective way forward is to counter these attacks with tools that are equally efficient.

At the industry level, the necessary shift is from one-time audits or reactive expert intervention to continuous security throughout the entire lifecycle.

Take GoPlus DeepScan’s three-part smart contract security solution as an example. It provides a practical, closed-loop approach.

Before launch — Token security self-check: Quickly identify potential backdoor risks within minutes, including honeypot tokens, malicious minting functions, blacklists, abnormal transaction taxes, and excessive owner privileges.

At launch — AI smart contract auditing: Conduct in-depth analysis of source code, permission management, and business logic; scan for vulnerabilities at both the syntax and business logic levels; and deliver a structured audit report.

After launch — Continuous security monitoring and regular checks: Track newly discovered vulnerabilities, attack incidents, and risks involving external dependencies such as oracles, cross-chain bridges, and third-party protocols in real time. Continuously assess whether the project is affected, issue routine risk alerts, and conduct regular contract security checks and ongoing audits.

Q3. How has vulnerability discovery changed over the past two years? And how do the security models differ when the same assets are held on-chain versus on an exchange?

Adam, Partner at GoPlus:

Frankly speaking, in the short term, attackers now have more ways to discover vulnerabilities.

There are three reasons for this.

Automated tools have significantly lowered the barrier to vulnerability discovery. Work that previously required top security researchers several weeks can now be completed by automated attack pipelines in just a few minutes.

There is an enormous number of older contracts on-chain that passed audits years ago. For attackers, these contracts represent a vast gold mine of potential vulnerabilities.

Attackers only need one successful exploit. Finding a single vulnerability can be enough to steal funds, while defenders must protect against every possible vulnerability.

It may take hackers only a few minutes to exploit these vulnerabilities and steal funds. But defenders can also discover the same vulnerabilities in just a few minutes.

The difference comes down to whether the project team uses the right tools before the hackers do.

More importantly, defenders have three structural advantages that attackers do not.

First-mover advantage. Defenders can repeatedly review contracts before launch and throughout their operation. Attackers can only hope that defenders have not already performed those checks.

Cost advantage. AI audits can be purchased on a per-audit or annual subscription basis, making them affordable enough for routine and comprehensive use.

Compounding security knowledge. Security knowledge bases continue to evolve with every new attack. The more these defense systems are used, the stronger they become.

When comparing on-chain and off-chain models, both who protects your assets and the types of risks you face are completely different.

On-chain self-custody: Security = Private key security + Smart contract security.

You are solely responsible for security. If your private key is lost or stolen, there is no customer support team you can appeal to.

Every interaction also exposes you to on-chain risks, including approval vulnerabilities, phishing signatures, and honeypot tokens.

The advantage is that your assets do not depend on the creditworthiness of any platform.

Exchange custody: Security = Platform security + Account security.

Private keys are managed by the platform through mechanisms such as hot and cold wallet separation, multisignature controls, and risk management systems.

In effect, you are outsourcing technical security to the exchange.

However, you still need to protect your exchange account through secure passwords, two-factor authentication, phishing prevention, and proper API key management.

It is also essential to choose an exchange with a trustworthy reputation.

Overall, on-chain security is about private key protection and the risks of your own actions, while exchange security is about platform trust and security infrastructure.

The former tests your awareness of Web3 security. The latter tests both the exchange’s infrastructure and your own account security habits.

Q4. As a trading platform, what improvements has Gate made to strengthen security?

Gate Security Team:

First, we conduct regular security audits of listed projects and continuously monitor contract status through on-chain events.

Whether a contract has been upgraded, permissions have changed, or unusual large transactions have occurred are all things that need ongoing attention.

A security assessment conducted when a token was first listed has a limited shelf life, just like the audit reports Adam described.

Users can also check the current risk indicators of a particular contract at any time.

Now let’s talk about the platform itself.

Gate’s security bug bounty program remains open to security researchers around the world.

Anyone who discovers a vulnerability can submit it to us through three channels: sec@gate.com, support tickets, or the HackenProof platform.

We expect project teams to accept security scrutiny, and we must be willing to subject ourselves to the same scrutiny. Security requirements should not be one-sided.

Having discussed tokens and the platform, let’s turn to account security.

Our advice is not to search for a single “safest place” to store all your funds. It is more practical to separate assets according to how frequently you need to use them.

Funds used for frequent trading can remain in your spot account for easy access. Assets that you do not expect to move for six months or a year can be placed in Gate Vault.

Gate Vault uses MPC combined with a 2-of-3 signing mechanism.

The private key is divided into three shares, held separately by the user’s device, Gate, and an independent third party.

The complete private key is never reconstructed at any stage, and neither Gate nor the independent third party can initiate a transaction on its own.

All outgoing transfers are also subject to a 48-hour delay before completion.

These 48 hours serve as a security buffer for users, during which they can freeze the outgoing transfer at any time.

Even if something unexpected happens, the delay gives users time to discover the problem and stop the transfer.

Another improvement is the Gate Account Security Protection Plan.

This plan is based on the Security Score.

Previously, account security settings were scattered across different pages, including login verification, authenticator apps, two-factor authentication, passkeys, trading limits, and withdrawal limits.

Users often found it difficult to understand how much of their account security setup they had actually completed.

The Security Score brings these measures together into a score from 0 to 100.

Users can immediately see which protections they have enabled and which are still missing. When the score changes, the system also reminds users to strengthen their settings.

Users with a Security Score of 80 and an account in good standing can activate the protection plan.

Once activated, it provides an additional layer of protection after users have completed their own security measures.

During the coverage period, if assets are transferred out of an account without authorization, users may apply for compensation if the incident meets the applicable rules.

The current maximum coverage for a single incident is $200,000.

This limit will be increased, with tiered coverage based on VIP level reaching up to $1 million.

Applications must be submitted within 45 days of the incident through “My Protection” by contacting security customer support.

Required materials include a police report and records of the asset transfers.

Q5. What should a complete audit report include? How should security scores, key findings, and remediation recommendations be used?

Adam, Partner at GoPlus:

An audit report that can guide action, rather than simply be filed away, should contain at least four elements.

Security Score (Quantifiable Rating) — For Initial Screening, Not Final Conclusions

Project teams can use the score as a quantitative benchmark for internal security assessments and compare changes after each iteration.

Exchanges can use it for preliminary token listing reviews, filtering out projects that clearly fail to meet security requirements at the first stage.

Ordinary users can treat the score as an entry point: avoid projects with low scores, and examine the key findings of those with high scores.

Key Findings (High-Risk Issues and Core Conclusions) — For Decision-Making

This is the executive summary of the report.

It should identify which issues are severe enough to block a launch and must be fixed beforehand.

For managers without technical backgrounds and exchange listing review teams, understanding the key findings is often sufficient.

Issue Details (Vulnerability Evidence and Impact Analysis) — For Identifying Problems

This section is intended for technical teams.

It should include the precise vulnerability location, down to the contract, function, and line of code, as well as the vulnerability type, severity level, attack path, and root cause analysis.

Good issue descriptions should provide reproducible execution paths and triggering conditions, rather than simply listing problems.

Remediation Recommendations (Actionable Fixes) — For Closing the Loop

Recommendations must be specific, actionable, and detailed enough to implement at the code level.

After remediation, the contract should be rescanned and retested to verify the fixes.

Together, these steps form a complete closed loop: security scoring, key findings, issue details, remediation, and rescanning.

Gate Security Team:

Based on our experience developing contract auditing features, we would add three points.

First, the two sections most easily overlooked are often the ones that should come first: audit objectives and limitations, and the scope of the audit.

We have established nine dimensions for our reports: audit objectives and limitations, scope, severity matrix, priority assessment, vulnerability details, risk paths, threat modeling, key function analysis, and remediation recommendations.

But the first two determine whether readers will misunderstand the entire report.

If the limitations are not clearly stated, readers may assume the audit covers everything.

If the scope is unclear, readers cannot tell whether only the main contract was audited or whether the review also covered liquidity pools, strategy contracts, oracles, and external dependencies.

Many promotional materials simply say “Audited” without explaining what was actually audited.

Such a statement provides almost no useful information.

Second, when reviewing key findings, users should consider risks together, even if each individual feature does not qualify as a vulnerability.

Here is a common combination found in audit reports.

The contract owner can blacklist addresses and freeze assets.

Trading pairs can be reset, preventing ordinary users from transferring tokens.

Minimum holding requirements can prevent users from selling their entire balances.

A single owner can also change multiple critical rules at any time.

Viewed separately, these four features may all be considered normal design choices.

Taken together, however, they indicate that control over the contract is highly concentrated in the hands of one person.

Third, users should understand how the report was generated, because that determines the boundaries of its reliability.

Our contract auditing process has three stages.

The first is static analysis, which checks fundamental risks such as access control, reentrancy, price manipulation, flash loans, and logical consistency.

The second is business scenario modeling. We extract the contract’s core interaction scenarios, verify business paths and boundary conditions, and identify issues that rule-based scanning may miss.

The final stage is semantic verification. We examine critical business paths individually to confirm whether the risks identified in the first two stages are genuine.

The third stage is primarily intended to reduce false positives.

If an audit report is filled with false alarms, users quickly lose patience and may eventually skip the entire checking process.

That is why the false-positive rate directly determines whether a security tool will actually be used.

Q6. What practical security measures can ordinary users take right now?

Adam, Partner at GoPlus:

Check token security before trading.

Before buying a new token, examine its security risks.

Pay particular attention to potential backdoors such as honeypot tokens, malicious minting, blacklists, abnormal transaction taxes, and excessive owner privileges.

Regularly clean up contract approvals.

Revoke approvals granted to DApps you no longer use, especially unlimited approvals.

Many theft incidents originate from problems with contracts that users previously authorized.

Strengthen account security.

Use strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication.

Apply the principle of least privilege to API keys, and never grant withdrawal permissions to untrusted tools.

Make phishing prevention second nature.

Verify domain names before signing, avoid links sent through private messages, and be skeptical of airdrops, customer support messages, and promises of high staking returns.

Phishing content is becoming increasingly convincing, so users need to remain rational and alert at all times.

Separate assets according to their purpose.

Keep only small amounts needed for everyday use in hot wallets.

For substantial holdings, hardware wallets are recommended.

Do not put all your eggs in one basket.

Pay attention to a project’s approach to security, not just its audit reports.

Whether a project conducts continuous audits and maintains security monitoring mechanisms matters more than an audit report issued years ago.

Prioritize projects that take security seriously and are willing to disclose how their security systems are built and maintained.

Gate Security Team:

Adam’s six recommendations are already very comprehensive.

We would like to connect several of them with Gate’s tools and turn them into actions users can take immediately.

Check token security before trading.

Users can directly use Gate AI’s contract auditing feature.

Submit a contract address and receive a report within minutes.

Focus on four areas: owner privileges, blacklists and trading restrictions, minting permissions, and transaction taxes.

If any one of these four areas is flagged red, users should stop there. There is no need to look any further.

Strengthen account security by raising your Security Score above 80.

Fund passwords, authenticator apps, two-factor authentication, anti-phishing codes, passkeys, daily withdrawal limits, and withdrawal channel management are all included in the checklist.

Users simply need to follow the prompts and complete each item.

The greatest value of the Security Score is that it turns settings scattered across different pages into an organized checklist, so users do not have to decide for themselves which protection to enable first.

Reaching a score above 80 also allows eligible users to activate the Account Security Protection Plan, providing an additional layer of protection after they have strengthened their own account security.

Use two existing tools to protect against phishing.

If you receive a message claiming to be from Gate, first use our Official Verification Channel to check whether the domain or email address belongs to us.

All emails sent by Gate will include the Anti-Phishing Code you configured yourself. Any email missing that code should be treated as fake.

Check approval amounts carefully before signing.

A contract itself may be secure, but that does not mean the transaction a website asks you to sign is safe.

A legitimate DApp will usually request only the amount needed for a particular transaction.

If it immediately asks for unlimited approval, that alone is a reason to stop and think.

If a wallet pop-up displays nothing but a string of characters you cannot understand, refusing to sign is always safer than signing first and asking questions later.

Finally, it is worth emphasising that security is dynamic, not static.

Launching a project after an audit is only the beginning of security work.

For project teams, this means continuous monitoring after launch is more important than the audit report itself.

For trading platforms, it means that listing a token is only the beginning of the review process.

And for ordinary users, the few minutes spent checking a transaction before signing are among the lowest-cost security measures available, yet also among the easiest to overlook.

There is no such thing as a security certification that guarantees safety forever.

When every party takes one extra step, the balance shifts toward the defenders.
