However, ETH would still need stronger buying demand to translate these improvements into a lasting market recovery.

Investors should monitor whether network activity continues growing, whether institutional products attract additional capital, and whether transaction economics improve alongside adoption.

Is Ethereum’s Biggest Opportunity Still Ahead?

Ethereum’s $25.8 trillion milestone highlights a fundamental distinction between blockchain adoption and cryptocurrency market performance.

The network is processing more stablecoin transfers, supporting more transactions, and securing more ETH through staking than a year earlier.

Yet the market has not necessarily rewarded those developments through stronger ETH prices.

That divergence creates an interesting opportunity for investors willing to evaluate Ethereum beyond short-term market movements.

If institutional adoption continues expanding, Ethereum’s long-term investment case may increasingly depend on its position as financial infrastructure rather than speculation alone.

title: Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain
description:

The post Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Protocol 42 switched on Agentic Mining at 06:00 UTC on 19 November 2026. AI agents can now place real-fund trades across its 42 markets. The same window opened Agentic Pass. That BNB Chain NFT funds agent wallets and pays holders in points, not P&L.

What Agentic Mining Changes for AI Trading

Agents trade live capital on Creator Markets. They no longer wait on a human click for every order. Pass mint proceeds go into the agents' trading wallets. Holders receive starter points and a share of the weekly Agent Pool. They can also chase extra points on a Pass leaderboard. A wallet that still holds one Pass at the weekly snapshot gets a 1.7-times points multiplier. That boost covers all Protocol 42 trades for that week. Agent fills sit in public view after a short delay. Readers can check what the bots did.

How Agentic Pass Funds the Agent Wallets

Each NFT costs 200 USDT in the first mint wave. Three AI agents take that capital. The opening series issues 2,000 Passes per agent and 6,000 Passes in total. Mint money lands in a separate Safe 2-of-3 multisig for each agent. Each agent may spend at most 100 USDT on a single trade. It must hold a Creator Market position for at least one hour before it can sell. Trading pauses if the wallet balance falls sharply.

Pass buyers earn 42 Points rather than a claim on trading profit. The mint stake is not withdrawable or refundable. Agent gains stay in the trading float. Losses do not erase points already earned or the 1.7-times trade multiplier. Binance's Agentic Wallet is one of the main entry ramps. That wallet isolates agent funds from a user's main balance. Users can set spend limits and keep a bot running around the clock. Protocol 42 already sits inside the Binance Wallet stack through earlier Creator Market tools. Agentic Mining moves those rails from human-led clicks to agent-led books.

Why Public Agent Logs Matter for Thin Markets

Long-tail markets often starve when market makers refuse unhedgeable risk. Protocol 42 wants agents to quote and trade without a human maker on every tape. That is the core AI and blockchain stake in this launch. Public Agent Terminal logs show fills about 15 minutes after execution. The delay keeps the machine book from becoming a black box. It also blocks instant copy-trade signals.

The launch still does not prove the agents will make money. They may deepen thin markets, or they may only farm points. The 1.7-times Pass multiplier and the weekly Agent Pool reward participation first. They do not guarantee a profitable bot. Protocol 42 opened Agentic Mining with real funds, a BNB Chain Pass, and a public trade log. The next print that matters is whether the agents keep trading once the points heat cools.

title: KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity
description:
KR1 put its Venice DIEM to work. The firm is taking a page out of the productive-asset book. It now sells live DIEM AI inference capacity to paying third-party customers. How KR1 Sells DIEM AI Inference on Venice KR1 plc filed the launch on 19 November 2026. The LSE: KR1 announcement opens DIEM infrastructure operations. […]
The post KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
KR1 put its Venice DIEM to work. The firm is taking a page out of the productive-asset book. It now sells live DIEM AI inference capacity to paying third-party customers.

How KR1 Sells DIEM AI Inference on Venice

KR1 plc filed the launch on 19 November 2026. The LSE: KR1 announcement opens DIEM infrastructure operations. The filing builds on a Venice update from 12 November. DIEM is Venice’s inference token. Each staked DIEM supplies US$1 of daily credit to run AI models on Venice. The company holds 557 DIEM, bought separately from its VVV position. VVV is Venice’s native token. That stake equals about US$557 of daily model credit. KR1 can sell that credit rather than leave it idle.

In the 90 days to 16 November 2026, KR1 fulfilled about 1.92 million third-party requests through Surplus Intelligence. Those runs served 101.5 billion AI model tokens. On Surplus Intelligence, KR1 picks which models to list and sets the price. When the marketplace matches a buyer to one of those offers, Venice runs the model on KR1’s credits. KR1 is paid in USDC. KR1 also feeds DIEM into Diem Relay. That pool stakes supplier tokens on Venice and sells the resulting inference capacity. Suppliers take a share of the USDC proceeds in line with their stake, after fees.

What KR1’s October DIEM Yield Shows

October earnings pointed to a 5.45% annualised yield. The figure is estimated on the fair value of DIEM used to supply the marketplace at month-end. KR1 said that rate will move with inference and compute supply and demand. Proceeds arrive in USDC. Income may be reinvested into more productive holdings or used for operating costs. The stated aim is to lift the earning power behind each KR1 share.

Keld van Schreven explained the firm’s model in practice. He is Managing Director and Co-Founder of KR1 plc. Digital assets earn from AI demand while the company keeps the underlying tokens. He said the work goes past buying assets. Knowing which models customers and agents use, and what they pay, helps KR1 pick services, price capacity, and raise utilisation. The London-listed group frames the launch as Technology Infrastructure work. Onchain assets become rented AI capacity instead of a static treasury line. The open question is how durable that 5.45% October print stays. More suppliers may chase the same credits.

title: Trump, Xi and Putin Promise More Fuel, But Markets Are Not Convinced
description:
Trump, Xi and Putin pledged more fuel. His last diesel deal with Putin cut US prices by 32 cents. See what changed.
The post Trump, Xi and Putin Promise More Fuel, But Markets Are Not Convinced appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin have promised to increase global fuel supplies. Yet oil prices barely moved on Thursday, as investors remained focused on stubborn US inflation and the growing likelihood of another interest rate hike in December.

The three leaders made the announcement during a historic meeting in Shenzhen, China, on November 19.

According to their joint declaration, the countries agreed to increase supplies of refined petroleum products, including diesel and gasoline.

“The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations.”

However, the declaration offered no specific production targets, delivery dates, or details about how the additional fuel would reach consumers.

Trump’s Previous Fuel Promise Has Delivered Little Relief

This is not Trump’s first attempt to bring down fuel prices through an agreement with Russia.

On October 9, Trump announced a diesel supply deal with Putin, promising prices would come down “FAST!”

Six weeks later, the results remain disappointing.

According to AAA, US diesel still costs around $5.96 per gallon, down just 32 cents since that announcement and roughly 58% higher than a year ago.

Why Markets Are Still Worried About Inflation

Thursday’s oil market reaction showed little excitement over the latest promise.

Brent crude rose just 0.18%, while US crude gained 0.15%. The muted moves suggest traders are waiting for evidence of actual supply increases.

Meanwhile, the bigger economic problem remains unresolved.

The Federal Reserve’s latest minutes showed persistent inflation concerns. Markets now price a 92% probability of a quarter-point rate hike in December.

Higher interest rates are weighing on risk assets, including Bitcoin, while a stronger dollar is pressuring commodities such as gold.

For investors, the outlook remains difficult. Lower fuel prices could eventually ease inflation, but Thursday’s declaration offers no guarantee of relief.

Until actual supplies rise and inflation cools, markets have little reason to change their expectations.

title: Nicolas Cage's 'Madden' biopic fails the coach and the movie while Christian Bale's Al Davis steals the show
description: Nicolas Cage's Madden biopic falters as the actor plays the coach like Cage himself, while Christian Bale's Al Davis portrayal steals the film entirely.
fullContent:
The first thing you saw on Amazon Prime's streaming site Thursday was Nicolas Cage's face enlarged by prosthetics, adorned with fake eyebrows, and topped off by a bad hairpiece – unlike the believable ones he wears in real life – promising a John Madden biopic of a bigger-than-life figure.

That's what "Madden" was supposed to be.

It was billed as the story of a coach-turned-broadcaster-turned-EA video game maven who touched generations of NFL fans and affected the game very much for the better.

JOHN MADDEN ROLE PUSHES NICOLAS CAGE TO DRAMATIC PHYSICAL TRANSFORMATION WITH ‘BRUTAL’ DIET, PROSTHETICS

But the reality of this 110-minute feature is we come away understanding the film would have been better done as an Al Davis bio, because Christian Bale's portrayal of the since-deceased Oakland and Los Angeles Raiders owner was magnificent on every level while Cage was simply the wrong guy to play the great coach.

Quick aside that will cause some disagreement: The casting director or producer or whoever picked Cage as Madden obviously never saw Frank Caliendo impersonate Madden.

THE CAST OF 'MADDEN' HITS THE RED CARPET TO TALK ABOUT WHETHER THEY'VE CHOWED DOWN ON TURDUCKEN

Caliendo would have been an inspired choice to play the coach. And, yes, the height would have been a challenge, but we could have more easily forgiven elevator shoes than Cage sleepwalking through Madden as himself – with little effort to sound or act like the guy a generation of NFL fans watched broadcast games every season for decades.

The Rock (1996) and Family Man (2000) made Cage a generational star. But, sadly, Cage being one hundred percent Cage ruined this one for me.

It was easier buying former Seahawks running back Marshawn Lynch in his role as an EA Sports computer geek than Cage as Madden.

Not even Sienna Miller forcing us to watch her as Carol Davis because, well, Sienna Miller must be seen, or the football shots that were believable enough, or the nostalgic soundtrack, or Bale's outstanding performance could save this movie.

The football scenes, by the way, were cool in an odd sense. It was like watching NFL Films on 1970s hallucinogens.

I definitely bought in to Bale's work as Davis. The Oscar winner perfectly captured Davis in all his rebellious genius.

There were shots in which I actually believed I was watching Davis. Bale totally nailed the owner's Brooklyn accent, spiced with a bit of Southern inflection.

True story: The first time I met Al Davis was in the early 1990s at an NFL spring meeting in Orlando.

I was in the bathroom using one of the urinals when Davis, wearing white pants, white shoes, a white Raiders jacket, and silver-rimmed dark sunglasses, walked up to the adjacent wall fixture, looked over, and asked my name.

Then he asked who I worked for. And then he told me he couldn't wait to get "these damn meetings over with."

Afterward, when we'd both washed our hands, he shook my hand and actually said, "Good luck, kid. Just win, baby."

The man was a caricature of himself in real life and it was wonderful.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

One of the comical scenes in Madden happens during an offseason meeting between the coach and Davis in the late 1970s.

I just about fell out of my seat when Davis introduces his young son Mark Davis to Madden because the red-headed bowl cut the young Davis is wearing is just a slightly earlier version of his latter-day bowl cut he still wears as the current Raiders owner.

When this movie is over, you're left asking yourself whether you just saw a documentary or a drama or a comedy. Then you realize the film is none of the three. Because it fails at all three.

A friend of a friend who saw the movie on its first day put it this way:

"Just watched Madden. It is preposterously awful ... and yet I sort of loved it."

Well, that first part is accurate.

title: Republicans hold lone Alaska House seat despite losing Senate, governor races
description: Rep. Nick Begich won re-election to Alaska's lone House seat after ranked-choice tabulation, a rare Republican bright spot in a Democratic wave.
fullContent:
Rep. Nick Begich, R-Alaska, won re-election to Alaska’s lone House seat Wednesday, surviving a Democratic wave that flipped both the Senate seat and the governor’s mansion.

Begich, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump, defeated independent challenger Bill Hill, a commercial fisherman and retired teacher backed by the Alaska Democratic Party, following the state’s ranked-choice voting tabulation.

Begich’s victory, called at 9:27 p.m. ET on Wednesday – more than two weeks after Election Day – stood in sharp contrast to the rest of Alaska’s top-of-the-ticket results, where voters handed Democrats major breakthroughs despite Trump winning the state by 13% in 2024.

HUNDREDS OF SUBPOENAS FLY IN DOJ’S ‘DECOY DAN’ PROBE AS DEMOCRAT PELTOLA DECLARED WINNER IN ALASKA

The race was among the final House contests called nationally after the Nov. 3 general election, offering a rare bright spot for Republicans in a midterm cycle that saw Democrats seize control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats thus far hold a 257-172 majority in the House, having flipped 46 seats to just three for Republicans. There are three races that remain too close to call.

"This process requires engagement, and the perspectives brought forward during the campaign added value for Alaskans as they made important decisions about their vote in this race," Begich said in a statement after his victory.

Hill, who campaigned on lowering costs, curbing big money in politics and pushing back against billionaires, said he called Begich to concede and congratulate him.

"I wished him well as he continues representing Alaska in Congress, because all Alaskans have a stake in his success," Hill said in a statement.

ALASKA DEM PELTOLA DEFEATS SULLIVAN, FLIPPING 9TH GOP SENATE SEAT AFTER 'DECOY DAN' UPROAR

One day before Begich’s race was called, Democrat Mary Peltola unseated second-term Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska. Peltola — who previously represented Alaska in the U.S. House before losing to Begich in 2024 — became the first Alaska native elected to the Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate race in the state in nearly two decades. Her victory cemented a 56-44 Democratic Senate majority, the party's largest since 2009.

"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my career to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," Peltola wrote on X.

Democrats also secured the Alaska governor’s office for the first time in nearly 30 years, with Democrat Jonathan S. Kreiss-Tomkins winning the open-seat race to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

Throughout the House campaign, Begich pitched himself as an effective advocate aligned with Trump’s push to expand oil, gas and resource development in Alaska. But the final stretch of the race was overshadowed by controversy surrounding Democrat Eric Hafner, a perennial candidate with no ties to Alaska who is currently serving a sentence in a federal prison in New York following a 2022 conviction for threatening to kill judges, police officers and others.

PELTOLA SAYS ALASKA ‘VOTED FOR CHANGE’ IN SENATE RACE

Hafner, whose state election booklet biography made no mention of his incarceration, captured nearly 8% of the first-round vote. In the closing weeks of the race, Hill’s campaign distributed stickers and yard signs branding Hafner a "fake ‘Democrat,’" while state party officials spent thousands of dollars on text messages to clarify that Hill was the party’s endorsed candidate after mysterious, unsourced texts circulated promoting Hafner.

Hafner’s mother, Carol "Kitty" Hafner — who also lacks ties to Alaska and finished sixth in the state's August Senate primary — dismissed claims that her son was recruited as a spoiler, writing in an email to The Associated Press that his runs have been "entirely independent of any influencers" and adding, "Tell President Trump to Pardon Eric Hafner!"

Controversy over alleged ballot spoilers also marked the Senate race, where independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr. drew suspicion due to sharing a name with the Republican incumbent. Following reports that members of Peltola’s team helped recruit Sullivan Jr. into the race, the U.S. Justice Department opened a criminal investigation and Gov. Dunleavy ordered a state inquiry. Peltola has repeatedly denied any involvement.

"I personally know that I am innocent, so I don’t spend a lot of time hand-wringing" about it, Peltola said Wednesday.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Here's What Needs to Happen for Ethereum Price to Hit $2,200 as a Fool Writer Buys
description: A Motley Fool writer is buying Ether as RSI signals oversold conditions. ETH must clear resistance near $2,170 and its 50-day average to reach $2,200.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Investment writer Dominic Basulto said he is loading up on Ether, calling it extremely undervalued.
  • Daily momentum sits deep in oversold territory, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Bulls must first clear resistance just below $2,200 before the headline target comes into play.

Dominic Basulto, a Motley Fool investment writer, argues that Ethereum's lead in decentralized finance and Vitalik Buterin's roadmap make Ether cheap.

That long view runs into a weak chart. Ether trades under both of its main trend lines, and recent losses came fast. Traders now want to know whether stretched selling can turn into a real recovery or only a brief bounce.

A Fool Writer Calls ETH Extremely Undervalued and Buys

Dominic Basulto, an investment writer who holds Bitcoin, Ether and Solana, said on Nov 19, 2026 that he is "loading up" on ETH. He called the token "extremely undervalued" after a steep slide. By his count, ETH was down 40% for the year and 64% from its August 2025 high.

His case starts with scale. Ethereum carried a market value near $215 billion that day, against roughly $43 billion for Solana. The network also holds a 52.5% share of value locked in decentralized finance, and it leads in stablecoins and asset tokenization.

Basulto also pointed to Vitalik Buterin's roadmap. The Ethereum co-founder wants the chain to become "the cryptographic world computer." He is outlining a quantum-safe design and backs Ethereum as the top blockchain for AI.

Cycles form the last piece. The decline began more than 12 months ago. Basulto noted that ETH gained 472% in 2020 and 395% in 2021 after earlier slumps. He described ETF outflows as "a symptom" of the slump rather than its source. He expects a rebound as early as 2027.

Ethereum Trades Far Beneath Both Key Averages

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Charts tell a harder story than Basulto's thesis. Ether traded near $1,800 on the latest data. That leaves it well below both of the moving averages traders watch most closely.

A moving average smooths out daily noise by tracking the average closing price over a set number of days. The 50-day average sits near $2,210. The 200-day average is a bit higher, near $2,270. When price holds under both lines, the trend points down and those levels tend to act as ceilings.

The slide is recent and steep. ETH lost about 25% over the past month and roughly 13% in the last week alone. Sellers pressed hardest lately, a sign the selling may not be over.

Buyers did manage a small bounce of about 1% over the past 24 hours. That move barely registers against recent losses.

The gap matters for anyone eyeing a recovery. ETH would need to climb more than 20% just to touch the 50-day line. That is a long way for a market where sellers still set the pace.

That $2,200 goal sits almost exactly on the 50-day average. Reaching it would mean reclaiming the first key trend line that broke during this decline. Until price closes back above it, the downtrend stays intact.

Oversold Readings Hint at Seller Exhaustion

Momentum readings show how stretched the selloff has become. The Relative Strength Index (RSI), a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 26. Anything under 30 counts as oversold, meaning sellers have pushed price down faster than usual.

Oversold conditions often come before relief bounces. Short sellers take profits, and bargain hunters like Basulto step in. Those rallies can be sharp, yet they frequently fade without changing the bigger trend.

Other gauges still lean bearish. The MACD, which compares short and longer-term price averages, remains below its signal line, so momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings also show a real trend, and sellers lead it.

Sellers look tired, yet no reversal is confirmed. Buyers have not taken control.

$2,170 Stands Between Bulls and the $2,200 Target

The first real test for buyers comes before the headline target. Resistance sits near $2,170, a band where earlier selling stalled. Price would have to clear that zone before the 50-day line even comes into play.

A break above that level would open the path to the next band near $2,280. That ceiling sits just above the 200-day average. Clearing both would mark the first sign that the broader downtrend is losing its grip.

The picture below current prices looks less comfortable. Daily support sits far lower, near $1,200, with no other floor in between.

If ETH loses its current footing, the chart offers little to slow a decline. A slide could run a long way before buyers find a level with a history of holding.

Two Paths for the Next Three Days

  • Bullish: The oversold reading sparks a relief bounce, and ETH closes above $2,170. That would put the next ceiling near $2,280 in reach. A drop back under $1,800 would cancel this setup.
  • Bearish: Sellers reject price below $2,170, and ETH breaks under $1,800. With no floor in between, sellers could press toward $1,200. A close back above $2,170 would invalidate this view.

Long Thesis, Short Term Downtrend

Basulto's argument rests on years, and his case for Ethereum's network lead may hold up. Traders watching the next few weeks face a different test. The headline target only comes into view after ETH reclaims its 50-day average, and sellers still guard that line.

With no support mapped until far lower, buying too early could prove costly.

title: Stablecoin Market Loses Billions: Where Is Crypto’s Liquidity Going?
description:
The stablecoin market lost $16 billion in 30 days as USDT and USDC supply shrank. How does it compare with the 2022 crypto crash?
The post Stablecoin Market Loses Billions: Where Is Crypto’s Liquidity Going? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Crypto’s stablecoin market has shed $16 billion in a month, marking its sharpest contraction since the 2022 bear market. The retreat is hitting USDT and USDC hard, leaving fewer dollar-backed tokens circulating.

Total stablecoin market cap is now standing at $283 billion, plunges by more than 5% in just a month, losing $16.5 billion in just a month. The decline puts the market under pressure just as crypto struggles to recover, with investors showing little appetite for buying the dip.

USDT and USDC Lead the Stablecoin Market Exodus

Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC account for most of the latest contraction. USDT is holding a market cap of $175.02 billion, down 4.3% over 30 days, while USDC fell to $68.58 billion, losing 5% during the same period. Together, the two stablecoins represent 86% of the entire market.

Source, RWA.xyz

The contraction also extends beyond dollar-backed tokens. Sky Dollar’s USDS supply dropped 22.32% over 30 days, while Ethena’s USDe expanded 4.36%. The gap shows that some are still moving between stablecoin products.

The pressure is also visible in exchange reserves. A November 11 CryptoQuant’s data showing USDT market cap had fallen $6.6 billion over 60 days through November 7. It was more than twice the $3.2 billion decline recorded after FTX collapsed in December 2022.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

The 2022 Crypto Winter Offers a Warning

The current contraction brings back an ugly history. Stablecoin supply reached $161.5 billion in March 2022 before entering a prolonged decline. Terra’s UST collapse accelerated the withdrawal of capital, with nearly $30 billion disappearing from stablecoin supply in June alone.

That monthly decline was almost twice the latest $16.5 billion contraction this time. Back in 2022, the damage continued into the following year. By September 2023, aggregate stablecoin supply had fallen by 26% from its March 2022 peak, a contraction of $43 billion.

Bitcoin endured a similar period of weakness. After reaching nearly $69,000 in November 2021, BTC eventually plunged to around $15,500 in November 2022. Stablecoin supply continued shrinking even after the initial market shock initiated by Terra. Crypto’s liquidity problems then became a prolonged market condition.

Yet, in 2023, not every stablecoin experienced the same fate. We had a $13.3 billion increase in USDT supply from its November 2022 lows, while USDC lost $16.7 billion. During that period, investors were not simply abandoning every stablecoin. Some were moving toward Tether as the market reassessed issuers and available returns.

Where Is Crypto’s Liquidity Going?

This time, arguably, the stablecoin contraction is happening against a different market backdrop. Crypto traders have fewer reasons to keep large amounts of capital parked in stablecoins when Bitcoin and major altcoins struggle to attract buyers. Some holders may be redeeming their tokens for traditional dollars, while others are moving into interest-bearing assets outside crypto.

A shrinking stablecoin market does not mean every dollar has left digital assets. But the simultaneous decline in USDT and USDC supply makes the latest contraction harder to dismiss as simple rotation between issuers.

A crypto recovery needs buyers willing to commit fresh capital, and stablecoins have historically provided traders with an immediate way to enter the market.

title: Super Bowl champ Ben Watson speaks out on Christian Nigerian persecution, double-standards and Trump's impact
description: Super Bowl champion Benjamin Watson says he doesn't trust US leadership to protect persecuted Christians in Nigeria without public pressure on lawmakers.
fullContent:
Super Bowl champion Benjamin Watson called out "double standards" in human rights advocacy when asked about attention to Palestinians compared with persecuted Christians in Nigeria, and said he doesn’t trust US leadership to protect Christians in Nigeria without public pressure.

"I do think that there are double standards. I do think that, you know, we will exclude certain people from the same type of human dignity that we want for ourselves. I believe everybody deserves human dignity," Watson told Fox News Digital.

"I believe that the Palestinian deserves human dignity and respect. I believe that the Jew deserves human dignity and respect. I believe that those in Nigeria who are suffering deserve human dignity, and they have human dignity, and they deserve respect."

Watson, a former New England Patriots tight end, is working with Global Christian Relief on its Stand With Them campaign, which aims to raise $1 million for relief and rebuilding efforts in Nigeria.

Asked whether he trusted Trump to continue prioritizing the issue, Watson answered, "No, I don’t. I don’t," despite the fact that Trump has already ordered a military strike against those targeting Christians in the country.

"And so I don’t trust that he will keep pressing this. I do trust that any president or any representative will push what the people think is important," he said.

Watson urged Americans to contact lawmakers and discuss the crisis in their churches, homes and online. He also credited the administration’s willingness to engage.

JOHN CLEESE BLASTS WORLD'S SILENCE ON EASTER MASSACRE OF NIGERIAN CHRISTIANS BY ISLAMIST TERRORISTS

"The good thing, though, however, is that it’s very clear that the administration is open and is willing to engage," he said. "And I hope that that will continue. I would applaud any efforts and opportunity, you know, to engage with the administration on this issue."

Trump redesignated Nigeria a "country of particular concern" for religious freedom in October 2025. U.S. forces struck ISIS targets in Sokoto State on Christmas Day that year in coordination with Nigerian authorities, according to AFRICOM.

At a Nov. 12 congressional hearing, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs Frank Garcia acknowledged in written testimony that violence had continued despite diplomatic and security cooperation. He outlined police training, information-sharing and efforts against terrorist financing.

Watson also warned against assuming Americans’ religious freedoms will always be secure.

"And so what history would tell us is that at some point on this land, we may be facing, as believers, the decision to denounce our faith or to be killed," he said.

His warning, he explained, came from his reading of Scripture and world history rather than a particular event he had witnessed in the United States.

He also rejected treating Muslim identity as evidence of extremism, noting that wrongdoing has occurred in the names of both Christianity and Islam.

"It’s not an automatic that simply because someone is a professing Muslim, that there’s violence or that there’s evil or any of those things attached to them," he said.

USCIRF’s October Nigeria brief documents attacks on Christian communities, churches and clergy, as well as violence against Muslims and other religious groups. Perpetrators include extremist insurgents, criminal gangs and armed militants.

Open Doors’ 2026 World Watch List ranks Nigeria seventh for overall Christian persecution and identifies it as the country with the most Christians killed for their faith during the reporting period.

Asked what he would tell Trump to do next, Watson called for greater attention to the crisis and accountability for Nigeria’s government.

"It needs to be something that’s headline news. If these things were happening in other countries, if this was happening in Europe, we would hear about it. And the fact is it’s happening in Nigeria and we’re not hearing that much about it," he said.

STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION

Watson suggested presidential news conferences and conversations with people who have firsthand experience in Nigeria. He declined to prescribe a specific policy and emphasized respecting national sovereignty.

"But I do know that there are ways that we can hold governments accountable," he said.

Nigeria first received the U.S. religious freedom designation in 2020. The Biden administration did not renew it in 2021, drawing criticism from the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom.

Watson said the designation brings awareness, accountability and advocacy in Washington. But he declined to prejudge how Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January, would address the crisis.

"Neither, neither at this moment. They’re not in office yet. We haven’t seen how they respond to it," he said when asked whether the election result was encouraging or discouraging.

When asked about the possibility that incoming Democrats would prioritize Palestinians over Nigerian Christians, he cautioned against making assumptions.

"That’s projection. But my message is the same for a Democrat or Republican," he said.

"If you care about human dignity, if you care about the image of God in every person, if you care about human beings, then this is something that needs to be at the forefront of your agenda, needs to be at the forefront of your advocacy, forefront of your foreign policy."

Asked what he would tell Americans who care about persecuted Christians but oppose spending resources abroad, Watson said domestic needs and international compassion can both be addressed.

"And so what I would say to them is, yes, be involved locally, be involved in the United States, but understand that we live in a world house," he said.

Watson also supported admitting people fleeing persecution through the legal refugee process.

"Yeah, I think we have refugee law. I think we have immigration law. I’m a strong believer in those laws. I also believe in compassion," he said.

"And so, yes, I’ll be in favor of having people who are fleeing for their life, like we always have in this country, to open our doors while also understanding that we have a process that must be completed. And, and that process is important."

Trump’s fiscal 2027 refugee determination allows up to 17,500 admissions, primarily allocated to South African Afrikaners, while retaining broader restrictions and exceptions. Watson was not asked about that specific allocation.

Watson traced his interest in persecuted Christians to around 2010, when he was playing for the Cleveland Browns.

In December 2025, he joined a Sports Spectrum-coordinated letter to Trump and congressional leaders seeking action on religious persecution in Nigeria. Other signatories included Brock Purdy, C.J. Stroud and Tony Dungy.

He also pointed to Leah Sharibu, who was 14 when she was abducted from her school in Dapchi in February 2018. USCIRF identifies her as a captive held for refusing to renounce Christianity.

"She wasn’t released because she didn’t denounce Jesus Christ. And she is still to this day in captivity," Watson said.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Global Christian Relief says its campaign supports rebuilding churches and homes, assisting wounded and displaced people and educating children.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Watson urged fellow Christians to take responsibility for helping persecuted believers while welcoming participation from people of any faith.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"We invite everybody to get involved, whether you’re a person of faith or not," he said.

"Many of them are fearing for their lives, but yet even in that, they are still praising, they are still worshiping, they still have faith. Let’s advocate for them."

title: Hong Kong SFC Flags Hyperliquid as Suspicious Unlicensed Trading Platform
description:
Hong Kong's SFC added Hyperliquid to its suspicious platform alert list, joining UK and Singapore regulators in 2026.
The post Hong Kong SFC Flags Hyperliquid as Suspicious Unlicensed Trading Platform appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid to its alert list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The November 18 entry names the platform’s trading website and says its operator holds no SFC license.

The listing is a consumer warning, not a ban or enforcement action. Still, it marks Hyperliquid’s front end as an unlicensed venue courting Hong Kong traders, adding regulatory risk for holders of Hyperliquid (HYPE).

Why Did Hong Kong Flag Hyperliquid?

The regulator’s concern covers two scenarios. Either Hyperliquid runs a trading venue in the city, or it actively pitches its services to local residents.

The entry lists no physical address. Instead, it points only to the app.hyperliquid.xyz trading interface.

Note: No website block, asset freeze, or trading halt accompanied the listing. Hyperliquid had not publicly commented on the SFC entry at the time of writing.

HYPE price showed no visible sell-off after the SFC listing. The altcoin traded near $68.42 on Thursday, up 2.1% on the day.

The token is holding the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement level at $68.08, after a November 14 drop briefly tested the 0.618 level near $61.

Is Hyperliquid’s Regulatory Problem Going Global?

Hong Kong is the latest regulator to act, not the first. In May, the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) added Hyperliquid and the Hyper Foundation to its warning list.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) followed on June 26, placing the exchange on Singapore’s crypto warning list alongside Bybit, KuCoin, and Bitget.

At the time, Hyperliquid said it had never claimed MAS authorization and that the listing did not amount to enforcement. However, investor Kyle Samani argued the platform was not truly permissionless.

Taken together, the three alerts suggest regulators judge decentralized exchange front ends by who they serve, not by how trades settle.

The next test is whether Hyperliquid restricts access in these markets or maintains that warning lists change nothing.

The post Hong Kong SFC Flags Hyperliquid as Suspicious Unlicensed Trading Platform appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: 1inch Taps Hyperliquid to Bring Perpetual Futures Trading to Its Users
description: The integration gives 1inch users access to leveraged trading across cryptocurrencies and traditional assets as Hyperliquid continues expanding its footprint in decentralized finance.
fullContent:
One of the most popular and veteran decentralized exchange aggregators, 1inch, has expanded its services by integrating Hyperliquid’s perpetual futures markets. This would allow its users to trade derivatives directly through the platform.

The announcement came today, revealing that the integration is available through the 1inch decentralized application and Android wallet in supported regions. An iOS rollout is expected in the coming weeks.

The new feature is designed to provide exposure to perpetual contracts covering cryptocurrencies, but als equities, commodities, and even foreign exchange.

Users are able to fund their positions with tokens that they already hold on 1inch, which would automatically be converted into USDC before being deposited into Hyperliquid.

The integration is also intended to support market, limit, and time-weighted average price (TWAP) orders, alongside stop-loss and take-profit functionalities.

Hyperliquid’s Growing Dominance in the DeFi Sector

This particular development comes as Hyperliquid continues to attract substantial attention from major industry partners.

As CryptoPotato reported, the Intercontinental Exchange, which is the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, revealed plans to bring Hyperliquid-powered perpetual futures to the regulated US market.

Meanwhile, the platform itself has been expanding beyond cryptocurrencies through its HIP-3 infrastructure. This allows developers to create derivatives markets linked to traditional assets.

In other words, the latest 1inch integration represents but one step in that direction, potentially introducing Hyperliquid-powered trading infrastructure to a wider audience without requiring users to navigate a separate interface.

The post 1inch Taps Hyperliquid to Bring Perpetual Futures Trading to Its Users appeared first on CryptoPotato.

title: China blocks Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Putin-Xi meeting over question to Trump
description: Chinese officials barred Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern from the meeting of President Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin after her earlier question.
fullContent:
Chinese officials barred a Bloomberg reporter from a high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin after she asked a question during an earlier bilateral session.

The clash over press access unfolded on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, China, where the three leaders gathered for their first-ever three-way meeting to discuss nuclear arms control, trade and the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Despite a push from the White House to get her admitted, Chinese officials refused to budge on barring Bloomberg reporter Annmarie Hordern from the room.

Hordern was blocked after she called out a question to Trump during his earlier one-on-one meeting with Xi: "President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?"

CHINA'S XI SURPRISES TRUMP AT TARMAC, RECIPROCATING GESTURE SHOWN MONTHS AGO

A second reporter also started to ask a question during the bilateral session but was shushed by Chinese officials. Beijing subsequently passed along a message to the U.S. travel pool warning that yelling questions is considered "extremely rude" and that journalists would be pulled from the room if they did so.

A White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity surrounding the issue, said Chinese officials insisted Hordern not be allowed into the trilateral meeting even as the White House advocated for her inclusion.

TRUMP BRINGS TWO DIVIDED CABINET HEAVYWEIGHTS TO CHINA AS CONTROVERSY HANGS OVER HIGH-STAKES TALKS

The dispute over press rules stood out alongside the friendly tone Trump sought to project toward both leaders during the summit. Trump praised his friendship with Xi, who greeted Air Force One on the tarmac Wednesday with a one-armed hug and called Putin "my friend" ahead of a separate 40-minute sit-down.

Tensions over artificial intelligence, however, still hung over the meetings.

Trump's ally Jensen Huang resigned last week as the CEO of Nvidia after confessing to an extramarital affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whose company helped give China access to Nvidia's advanced computer chips used to develop AI models. Beijing has denied that Alice Huang was a Chinese government agent.

Fox News’ Kaitlin Sprague and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Probing Ethereum nodes using Sonar
description:
TL;DR
Sonar is a free tool from ProbeLab that probes a single Ethereum node on demand. Give it an ENR and it finds the node over discv5, dials every address the record advertises, runs the libp2p or devp2p handshake, and for consensus-layer nodes exchanges Status and MetaData. Each result is compared with the node’s own ENR and with what our discv5 crawler has recorded about it. Other node identifier formats are also accepted, such as libp2p peerID or enode URL. Sonar is in beta. We would like feedback from client teams and node operators on what else a probe should check.
Why probe a node from the outside
A node can look healthy in its own logs and still be hard for the rest of the network to reach. Common cases:
the ENR advertises an IP or port that is not reachable (NAT, a firewall rule, a public IP that changed)
only some transports work, for example TCP answers but QUIC does not
the ENR and the node’s Status/MetaData disagree (fork digest, attestation or sync-committee subnets, custody group count)
a beacon API or metrics port is open to the internet
The node only sees its own side of these problems. Sonar connects to it as an unknown peer would and shows what happened at each step.



How a probe works
Decode the ENR. Sonar shows every field: node ID, IPv4/IPv6 addresses and ports, the eth2 fork digest and next fork, attnets, syncnets, custody group count, and the eth field that marks an execution-layer node.
Look the node up over discv5. The lookup returns the latest version of the record, so an old ENR is refreshed before any dial.
Dial every advertised address, one at a time. IPv4 and IPv6, TCP and QUIC are dialed and reported separately.
Identify the node. Consensus-layer nodes go through libp2p identify (agent version, protocols, listen addresses). Execution-layer nodes go through the devp2p hello over RLPx (client name and capabilities).
Run the eth2 exchange (consensus-layer nodes only). Sonar requests Status and MetaData, collects the gossipsub topics the node subscribes to, and records any GOODBYE and its reason code.
Read the node’s discv5 routing table, bucket by bucket.
Check the API and metrics ports of the client the node runs.
A probe takes from a few seconds to about half a minute, depending on how many addresses the node advertises and how quickly it answers. Results stream into the page as each step finishes.
What the result shows
Reachability
One row per address: whether it connected, the connection setup time, the RTT, and the full error when a dial fails. The columns on the right show where each address came from: the ENR, libp2p identify, the discv5 lookup, or our crawl history. In the example the node answers on discv5 (UDP 9000), TCP 9000 and QUIC 9001. Identify also reported six private addresses, which Sonar lists but does not dial.



Consensus layer
This card appears only for consensus-layer nodes, the ones whose ENR carries an eth2 field. Any other discv5 participant, such as an execution-layer node or a node from another network that shares the DHT, still gets the reachability, routing table and port checks, but there is no eth2 exchange to run. For a consensus node, the card shows the values from Status and MetaData, next to the same fields in the ENR. The subnet grids compare what the ENR advertises with what the node reports it is subscribed to, for attestation subnets, sync-committee subnets and custody groups. Any mismatch is flagged. If the node sent a GOODBYE, the card shows the code and its meaning (for example 129, too many peers). A node that is full still tells us its GOODBYE reason, and some clients (Teku, for example) send their gossip topics before hanging up.



Routing table
How many peers sit in each bucket of the node’s discv5 routing table, how long the read took, and how many other nodes in our last crawl have this node in their own tables. Hovering a cell lists the peers in that bucket by ENR, and each one links to its own Sonar result, so you can walk from a node to its neighbours.
The bucket counts show how well the node itself is connected to the network: a table with most buckets filled means it can find peers and serve lookups, while a nearly empty one points to a node that is isolated or still starting. The “known by” count shows the other direction, how discoverable the node is: discv5 lookups only return nodes that sit in other nodes’ tables, so a node known by few peers is hard for new peers to find and gets fewer inbound connections, even when its own table looks healthy.



Port exposure
Admin ports usually have no authentication. Exposed to the internet, they let anyone read the node’s state, overload it with expensive queries or, on Prysm’s gRPC port, reach the interface a validator client uses. Metrics ports reveal the client version, which points attackers to known bugs, and can tie the node’s IP to the validators it runs. An exposed port causes no errors, so operators rarely notice it.
Sonar checks the API and metrics ports of the client the node runs, on the node’s public IP. Each port is rated by what it exposes: node control (high), node read (medium) or metrics (low). For a Lighthouse node that is the beacon API (5052) and metrics (5054); for Prysm it adds gRPC (4000), and so on per client. An open beacon API port is confirmed by calling /eth/v1/node/identity and comparing the peer ID with the probed node.



History
ProbeLab crawls the Ethereum discv5 network every two hours. Sonar lists the addresses and agent versions those crawls recorded for the node, so you can see when an address or a client version changed.
Next steps
Single vantage point. Probes run from one region of our infrastructure, so a result describes reachability from there. Nodes that rate-limit unknown peers can answer differently to their regular peers; geth, for example, throttles repeated inbound connections from one IP, so two quick probes of the same execution node can disagree. Future work could include probing from several regions and spread lookups across them, so a result can tell a node that is down apart from one that is unreachable from one place.
One-off probes. Each lookup runs once today. The next step is continuous monitoring: probing a node on a schedule and reporting when it becomes unreachable, when a transport stops answering, or when a new port opens. All this can be accompanied by daily/weekly/monthly reports, as well as the corresponding alerts. If that would help with nodes you run or depend on, tell us which checks matter and how often they should run.
We would like input from client teams and researchers on which behaviours are worth checking from outside a node: specific GOODBYE codes, req/resp methods, or Fulu custody and column fields. Replies on either of the two directions above are just as welcome.
Check Sonar at: Sonar: Inspect a PeerID, ENR or MultiAddress | ProbeLab Analytics and get in touch.

title: XMR at $500: The $455 Low Is the Line to Watch After a Clean zkSecurity Audit
description: Monero slipped below $500 even after zkSecurity found no serious flaws in FCMP++. Here is why the $455 low and the 200-day average now decide XMR's next move.
fullContent:
Monero's next privacy upgrade passed a key security test. Auditors at zkSecurity reviewed the code behind FCMP++ and found no serious flaws, and developers have fixed the minor ones.

The market shrugged. XMR slid back toward a level that once held as support. Traders now want to know whether buyers can hold the recent low before sellers push deeper.

Why Did Monero Fall Below $500 Despite Good Audit News?

Monero fell below $500 because sellers already controlled the market before the audit news arrived. The clean report landed after a failed run at the late-2025 highs, and traders were already locking in gains.

XMR swept those highs near $600 but never broke out above them. That kind of move often traps late buyers, and the selling that followed was sharp. Last week's drop closed the weekly candle under that key level.

The token now trades near $503, flat over the past 24 hours. The calm follows a rough stretch. XMR is down about 14% on the week and roughly 17% over the month. Buyers have paused the slide but have not reversed it.

What Did the zkSecurity Audit of Monero Find?

The audit found no serious flaws in the cryptography behind Monero's next privacy upgrade. MAGIC Grants, a non-profit crypto research and funding charity, hired zkSecurity to review the Generalized Bulletproofs code. That code underpins FCMP++, short for Full-Chain Membership Proofs.

Reviewers reported no high or medium severity issues. They flagged four low-severity issues and three informational findings, and developers have since addressed all of them.

zkSecurity said the protocol "is complete, zero-knowledge, and sound." In plain terms, honest proofs verify, they reveal nothing extra, and fake ones fail. The firm also wrote a machine-checked proof in the Lean theorem prover, which adds a formal layer beyond a manual review.

The result lowers the technical risk of shipping FCMP++. It did nothing to stop the selling, though.

Can XMR Hold the $455 Low?

Monero (XMR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

The short-term trend points down. XMR trades below its 50-day average near $555, so that line now acts as a ceiling. The 200-day average sits lower, around $474, and still works as a floor.

Buyers look fragile on the 4-hour chart. A sharp drop found a low there. The bounce stalled near $518, the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement, and price gave back that gain within a day.

Momentum sides with the sellers. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads 38. That reading is weak, though still above oversold territory. The MACD sits below its signal line, so momentum still points down. Trend strength readings confirm that sellers lead.

On the daily chart, the first resistance stands near $535, with $648 above it. A break of the $455 low would put the 200-day line in play. Below that sits the weekly demand zone between $390 and $440. Listed supports near $169 and $145 mark only a distant floor.

Is This Just a Reset in Monero's Uptrend?

It stays a reset if XMR holds its recent low and the 200-day line, then climbs back above first resistance. A daily close below both the 200-day average and the weekly demand zone would rule that reading out.

Bulls frame the drop as a reset within a multi-year uptrend. The long-term average still supports that view for now. Sellers control the short-term trend, though, so buyers need to defend that recent low first. The clean audit gives the upgrade case a firmer base. Price still has to confirm it.

title: Illia Polosukhin Says NEAR Intents Taps Real Markets as a Take-Two Token Goes Live
description: NEAR Protocol launched nTTWO, a Take-Two-linked token. NEAR trades near $3.39, and a close above the 50-day average near $3.89 would back the liquidity pitch.
fullContent:
NEAR Protocol has put a Take-Two-linked token live on its own platform. The company calls it the first stock issued natively on its blockchain.

The launch tests a bold claim about how NEAR Intents sources liquidity. Traders now want to know whether real volume follows, or whether the token stays a niche experiment.

A Take-Two Token Becomes NEAR's Test Case for Real Liquidity

NEAR Protocol said on Nov 18, 2026 that nTTWO, a token linked to Take-Two Interactive, is live on near.com. The company said the token supports confidential spot trading around the clock. NEAR called it "the first stock natively issued on the NEAR blockchain."

The token sits at the contract nttwo.rwa.assetize.near. Its launch gives NEAR a concrete product to back a broader pitch about how its trading layer works.

Co-founder Illia Polosukhin said NEAR Intents taps liquidity in the underlying markets instead of isolated pools. In plain terms, trades are meant to draw on the deep markets where Take-Two stock already changes hands.

The fine print matters. nTTWO is a limited-recourse debt certificate issued by Assetize Issuer PCC. Holders do not own Take-Two shares and have no claim against the company. They could also lose their entire investment.

A 12% Climb Stands Between NEAR and Its First Ceiling

NEAR trades near $3.39, and its first resistance sits around $3.81. Getting there takes a climb of about 12%. That is the nearest ceiling on the daily chart, where sellers have recently stepped in.

Even that move would repair only part of the damage. The token has lost about 31% over the past month. A rally to that ceiling would win back under a third of the slide.

The latest day offers a small start. NEAR rose about 3% in 24 hours, though it remains down roughly 6% on the week.

What Has to Go Right for the Intents Pitch

For the Intents pitch to lift NEAR, several parties have to come through at once.

  • Solvers: These market makers compete to fill swaps, but none is obliged to fill an order. If they step back, round-the-clock execution stalls and the liquidity claim looks thin.
  • Traders: NearBlocks shows a total supply of just 800 tokens, moving into and out of the Intents contract. Volume has to grow well past that for the product to matter.
  • Users outside the US: Signup promises "No email. No KYC," yet access varies by jurisdiction. US persons are excluded unless registered or exempt. Confidential Mode also offers limited privacy, since operator Intents Technology can disclose data.
  • near.com: Native issuance has to beat the Ondo stocks it added in September, which were issued on other chains.

Reclaiming the 50-Day Average Would Put the Call on Track

NEAR Protocol (NEAR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

NEAR now trades between its two key trend lines. The 50-day moving average, which tracks the average close over the past 50 sessions, sits near $3.89 and acts as a ceiling. The 200-day average, near $3.03, sits below price and acts as a floor for now.

Sellers still control the broader move. Trend strength readings point to a real downtrend.

Momentum has begun to turn. MACD, a gauge that compares short and long price averages, has crossed above its signal line. That suggests the selling pressure is easing.

RSI, a 0 to 100 measure of momentum, reads about 41. That sits in weak territory, below the neutral zone. Buyers have slowed the decline but have not taken over.

A daily close above the 50-day average would be the first real sign the call is working. If that holds, the next target is resistance near $4.28.

Where the Call Breaks

A daily close below support near $2.73 would break the call. It would mean the nTTWO launch failed to shift sentiment, and the next floor would sit around $2.21.

The test will play out over the coming weeks. A confirming signal would be NearBlocks showing nTTWO supply and transfers growing well beyond the current trickle. Flat volume would undo the liquidity pitch.

title: Bitcoin Price Edges Closer to a 9% Drop as ETF Outflows Top $1 Billion Again
description: Bitcoin trades near $64,000 after a second week of ETF outflows above $1 billion. RSI is oversold, but $58,000 is the floor traders are watching.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Spot Bitcoin funds logged another week of outflows above a billion dollars.
  • Daily momentum looks oversold, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • The nearest support floor sits about 9% below the current price, with little beneath it.

Investors pulled money from US spot Bitcoin ETFs for a second straight week. Corporate buying from Strategy Inc. has done little to offset the selling.

That matters because fund flows have driven much of this year's price action. Fear now grips the market, and a possible Fed rate hike looms in December. Traders want to know whether oversold conditions spark a bounce or the slide reaches the next floor.

Second Billion Dollar Week of ETF Exits Deepens the Slide

The funds shed about $1.07 billion between Nov 9 and 13, SoSoValue data show. Big funds are pulling money out faster than new buyers step in.

Strategy Inc. kept buying through the drop. The company added 485 BTC in the week to Nov 15, a purchase worth roughly $31 million. Its stash now stands at 850,849 BTC, bought at an average cost near $75,450. That leaves the firm sitting on about $10 billion in paper losses.

Mood across the market has soured. The Fear and Greed Index reads 22 out of 100, deep in fear territory. Bitcoin now trades about 50% below its October 2025 record near $126,000.

The Federal Reserve adds another worry. Markets expect a rate hike on December 9, which tends to hurt assets that pay no yield. Long-term holders see value at these prices. Short-term traders may wait until flows steady after the Fed decides.

Bitcoin Trades Far Beneath Both Averages After a 22% Monthly Slide

Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Bitcoin trades near $64,000, far below the levels where it spent most of the autumn. The daily chart shows a market that has stepped down in clear stages, with each bounce fading before it could build.

Moving averages smooth out daily noise and show the broader direction of price. The 50-day average sits around $75,000. The 200-day average is slightly higher, near $76,000. Bitcoin trades well under both lines. That gap confirms a downtrend on short and long time frames alike.

The two averages now act as a ceiling. Buyers who bought near those levels may sell to break even if price climbs back. That supply makes any recovery toward the mid-$70,000s harder to sustain.

Losses have also picked up speed. Bitcoin fell about 14% over the past week. Over the past month it dropped roughly 22%. More than half of the monthly decline came in the last seven days. Sellers grew more aggressive as November went on, which lines up with the heavy fund exits.

The last 24 hours brought a break from that pressure. Price finished the day roughly flat, with no fresh lows and no real bounce. Quiet days like this often follow a steep run lower as sellers catch their breath. Buyers have yet to take control, and one calm session does little to change the broader trend.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Sellers

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 24 on daily candles. Readings below 30 count as oversold. That tells traders the drop has run far and fast, and a relief bounce could come at any time.

Other signals still favor the bears. The MACD line remains below its signal line, so momentum keeps pointing down. Trend strength readings also show a real trend, and sellers are the ones driving it.

Oversold conditions can last for weeks when a downtrend is this firm. Price can keep sliding while RSI stays pinned low. A turn would need RSI to climb back above 30 and momentum to flip upward. Until then, the stretched reading signals exhaustion risk for sellers and offers no clear buy signal.

$58K Is the Floor Standing Between Bitcoin and Open Air

Nearest support sits near $58,000, the first real floor on the price chart. Buyers stepped in there before, so it should draw some demand on a retest.

The trouble lies beneath it. The data shows no clear next support if that level gives way. A clean break could leave price with little to slow the fall, and selling could speed up as stop orders trigger.

Any recovery faces its first test at the 50-day line, where the nearest resistance also sits. A push back to that zone would erase most of this week's damage. Sellers will likely defend it.

The bigger ceiling sits near $80,000. A daily close above that mark would show buyers back in charge. It would be the first sign the downtrend is turning.

What Flips the Next Three Days

  • Bullish: Oversold momentum sparks a relief rally that carries price back toward the 50-day line, where the first resistance sits. A daily close under that support floor would cancel this view and hand control back to sellers.
  • Bearish: Another week of heavy ETF exits drags Bitcoin down to retest the floor flagged above. A recovery above the 50-day line would undo this case and show the selling has run its course.

Stretched but Not Yet Bottomed

Sellers still set the pace. A lasting bottom likely needs fund flows to turn positive first. Until then, bounces may fade under the averages.

The Fed meeting is the main risk. A hike could push nervous holders to sell, and that pressure could crack the support floor.

title: DOGE ETF Assets Shrink to $9.74M as a Month Passes With No Flows at All
description: Spot Dogecoin ETFs have logged no flows for a month as assets fell to $9.74M. DOGE sits near its yearly low of $0.055, the level that decides the next move.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Spot Dogecoin ETFs have gone about a month without a single dollar moving in or out.
  • Selling momentum is fading on the daily chart, yet buyers have not stepped in to take over.
  • The yearly low near $0.055 is the line that decides whether the slide deepens.

Money has stopped moving through spot Dogecoin ETFs. The funds have logged no inflows or outflows for weeks, and their assets keep shrinking as the coin loses value.

That silence leaves DOGE without institutional support just as it trades near its weakest point of the year. Sellers look tired after a sharp autumn slide. Traders now want to know whether the recent low can hold without any fresh demand behind it.

Spot DOGE ETFs Sit Idle While Their Assets Nearly Halve

The funds have not recorded a single inflow or outflow since mid-October, fund-flow data from SoSoValue show. No new money has arrived, and no holder has pulled any out.

Their total net assets still shrank from about $17M in late September to roughly $9.74M. With flows frozen, that drop comes entirely from the falling price of the coin the funds hold.

That idle state matters. Institutional buyers are not stepping in to absorb the selling, so the funds offer no cushion under the market.

The weakness peaked on November 14. DOGE fell from $0.065 to $0.057 in a single day as volume jumped. Derivatives traders retreated too. Open interest slid from about $475M on November 11 to $362.5M, Coinalyze data show. Roughly a quarter of open bets vanished in a week. Funding rates turned negative during the crash and have only edged back above zero. Leveraged traders have barely returned.

A 44% Slide Leaves Dogecoin Far Below Both Key Averages

Dogecoin (DOGE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Dogecoin traded near $0.059 at last check, flat over the past 24 hours. The quiet day hides a deep slide. The coin sat above $0.10 in late September, so it has lost about 44% in less than two months.

The moving averages show how far the trend has turned. A moving average tracks the mean closing price over a set number of days and smooths out daily noise. DOGE now trades well below its 50-day average near $0.074. That line now acts as a ceiling, and rallies tend to stall beneath it.

Higher still, the 200-day average sits around $0.086. Price under both lines is the textbook picture of a downtrend. Long-term holders who bought this year are mostly underwater.

Recent losses came in steady steps. DOGE is down about 13% over the past week and roughly 25% over the past month. That pattern points to persistent selling rather than one bad session.

Buyers had one chance to change the tone after the mid-November crash. DOGE bounced to about $0.060, but the move failed to hold and price slipped back. Buyers showed little conviction, and sellers kept control of the trend.

Sellers Look Tired but Buyers Have Not Shown Up

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, shows how hard the selling has been. The daily reading sank close to 18 during the November crash, deep in oversold territory. It has since climbed back to about 31.

That rebound means the panic has eased. The reading still hovers near the oversold line, so buying pressure remains thin.

The MACD, another momentum gauge, still sits below its signal line, so momentum points down. Its red bars are shrinking, though, a sign that sellers are pushing with less force each day.

Trend-strength readings confirm a real downtrend, and sellers still lead it. Tired sellers can pause a decline without ending it. A reversal needs buyers to step in with conviction and volume, and so far they have stayed on the sidelines.

Why $0.055 Is the Floor That Cannot Crack

The key level sits just below the current price. DOGE briefly touched $0.055 during the November 14 crash, its lowest point of 2026. That wick now marks the only support on the chart.

The coin has no recent trading history lower down, so no obvious shelf of past buying exists. A daily close under that low would leave price searching for a floor in open space. Thin demand could make that search fast and painful.

Overhead, the first test sits near $0.072, just under the 50-day line. A move back above it would be the first sign of repair.

The next barrier waits around $0.078. Clearing both would ease pressure on the trend, though it would not reverse it.

Two Paths From the Edge of the Yearly Low

DOGE now sits close to its yearly low, and the next daily closes should pick a direction.

  • Bullish: Buyers defend the November low and push price through the first resistance under the 50-day line. That would open a run toward the next barrier above it. A close back under the November low would cancel this setup.
  • Bearish: A daily close below the yearly low extends the downtrend into uncharted ground with no support marked. A reclaim of the first resistance would invalidate this view and point to fading seller control.

Exhaustion Without Demand Leaves the Bottom Unconfirmed

Dogecoin looks worn out after its autumn slide, and the decline may still run further. No wave of buying has followed the tiring sellers. The burden stays on the bulls to prove demand.

The risk is lopsided. ETF money remains absent, and no support sits under the November low. A clean break there could move quickly.

title: Nike is Riding the GTA 6 Hype. Will Its Stock Price See Any Relief?
description:
Nike stock has lost more than 40% this year. Now Travis Scott, Rockstar and Nike drop GTA 6 Air Force 1 sneakers as the turnaround drags on.
The post Nike is Riding the GTA 6 Hype. Will Its Stock Price See Any Relief? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Nike is tapping into GTA 6 hype with a Travis Scott sneaker drop. The collaboration lands just as Nike tries to convince Wall Street that its turnaround can work.

The company’s stock has lost more than 40% this year.

Travis Scott Brings GTA 6 to the Air Force 1

The Travis Scott x Rockstar x Nike Air Force 1 Low comes in black and white. Instead of the usual AIR lettering, the midsole reads GTA. The black pair also carries a debossed map of the game.

Scott teased the collaboration with photos of a pink pair earlier this month, as a GTA fan account shared.

Sneaker release trackers list the pairs at $130 each, with London’s Selfridges first in line, followed by Nike’s SNKRS app and Scott’s Cactus Jack store. A separate friends-and-family edition will not go on public sale.

Resale demand is already strong. On StockX, the white pair lists for several times its $130 retail price ahead of the official drop.

The rapper also features on the game’s soundtrack and joins Rockstar’s Miami launch festival. On X, Scott congratulated the developers on launch eve, and Rockstar replied with a heart.

Crypto has tried the same playbook. Strategy released $250 Bitcoin Jordans earlier this year, as Nike stock kept sliding. However, buyers could not pay with crypto.

Turnaround Plan Leaves Wall Street Unconvinced

Hype alone will not fix the numbers. At its investor day, Nike unveiled its Full Stride Ahead strategy. The plan targets about $5 billion in extra revenue by fiscal 2031 and focuses on five sports and 23 priority countries.

Still, the company expects sales to keep falling before growth returns in fiscal 2029. Nike stock closed 6.3% lower on the day of the presentation.

The next test comes with quarterly earnings in December.

Meanwhile, GTA 6 itself is off to a record start. Sensor Tower estimates the game sold about 17 million copies for more than $1.65 billion by launch. Some analysts expect it to gross more than $3 billion in its first week.

The hype already left the PS5 Pro sold out at major US retailers, while near-perfect reviews lifted Take-Two stock.

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: What is a dirty bomb? Explosive terror threat explained
description: Iran's reported dirty bomb exploration puts new focus on a threat experts say could shut down a city and displace families even without mass casualties.
fullContent:
While no dirty bomb is known to have been successfully detonated in a terror attack, a reported Iranian effort to explore such an option has placed a new spotlight on long-standing fears of one — even as experts say the disruption could spread farther than the blast.

A dirty bomb is an explosive designed to spread radioactive material — but not in the way an atomic bomb like those dropped in World War II would.

"Anything involving radiation sounds frightening, but there’s a big difference between a dirty bomb and a nuclear weapon," said Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory special agent who at one point served as the Jackson Field Office's weapons of mass destruction coordinator.

Dirty bombs use a conventional blast to spread radioactive dust or a similar contaminant.

US REMOVES RADIOACTIVE CANCER-TREATMENT MATERIAL FROM CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRY OVER 'DIRTY BOMB' RISK

"The initial blast may pose the greatest immediate danger, but the contamination, fear and disruption afterward could be significant," Pack told Fox News Digital. "A dirty bomb doesn’t have to kill thousands of people to terrorize millions."

An attack could certainly be deadly. It would also shut down significant portions of a targeted city, he said, displacing families and businesses.

They're also risky to build, according to Pack. Bomb makers are at risk of exposing themselves to the same radioactive material they plan on using against the public, it's difficult to ensure the contaminants are dispersed in the explosion, and the terrorist would need to procure something to disperse to begin with.

"Just because somebody puts radioactive material with an explosive doesn’t mean they’re going to contaminate half a city," he said. "But even a relatively small incident could create tremendous fear, evacuations and disruption. That’s why we take these threats seriously."

The radioactive materials to make them can be gathered without the ability to produce nuclear power or weapons, according to Paul Mauro, a retired NYPD inspector and Fox News contributor. One potential source is medical waste, he said, such as byproducts of certain cancer treatments.

"That's why they call it dirty," he said. "It's waste."

The greatest danger of a dirty bomb is the blast itself, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, but radioactive material can spread and quietly cause dangerous health problems for people who unknowingly breathe it in.

"The radioactive materials used in a dirty bomb would probably not create enough radiation exposure to cause immediate serious illness, except to people who are very close to the blast site," according to the CDC.

Police departments are equipped with devices that can detect radiation, Mauro said — which are sensitive enough to flag medical radiation in a passing ambulance.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

CNN reported earlier this week that U.S. intelligence indicated Iran was developing potential plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a radiological device or chemical weapon, although sources described the effort as Iran exploring options rather than plotting an attack.

The issue came up again at a House Homeland Security Committee hearing Wednesday morning involving testimony from Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia.

IRGC OPERATIVE LANDS ON FBI’S MOST WANTED TERRORISTS LIST OVER ALLEGED PLOT TO KILL FORMER TRUMP ADVISOR

Clayton acknowledged that the threat of a dirty bomb attack has existed for years, but officials said they haven't seen evidence of an imminent plot.

"In the aftermath of September 11, 2001, there is heightened concern that terrorists may try to smuggle nuclear or radiological materials into the United States," the United States Government Accountability Office warned in a 2006 report. "These materials could be used to produce either an improvised nuclear device or a radiological dispersal device, known as a dirty bomb."

The GAO report cited a failed attack in Russia's capital in the mid-1990s as an example of the "capability and willingness" of terrorists to resort to such weapons of mass destruction.

Chechen separatists had placed a canister packed with cesium-137 and dynamite in a Moscow park, but it wasn't detonated.

The report included a summary of Department of Energy plans in place to scan for and detect sources of radiation that could be linked to terror plots or weapons smuggling and even locate material washed away in the wake of a natural disaster like Hurricane Katrina.

Now, the source of potential threats is believed to be Iran or its proxy militia group, Hezbollah.

"The best dirty bomb response is the one that you never hear about," said Pack, the retired FBI agent. "Because somebody stopped the plot before a bomb ever made it onto our streets."

SEND US A TIP

Radiation has no taste or smell, according to the CDC.

If you find yourself in the midst of a suspected dirty bomb attack, the CDC warns that you should cover your mouth and nose and try not to breathe it in. If you aren't already indoors, seek shelter. Remove your clothes and seal them in a bag, then shower up, making sure to thoroughly wash your hair to remove any potential contaminants. Indoors, close doors and windows and turn off fans that bring in outside air.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Monitor TV, radio or social media for official updates. Authorities will announce when it's safe to go outside again.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

"The good news is that it can be cleaned up," Mauro said of the dispersed material. "It would be expensive, time-consuming, a nightmare, sure."

Fox News' Krista Garvin and Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.
