fullContent:
Cryptocurrency exchange Bitunix has received the highest possible rating, AAA, from CER.live, an independent platform that evaluates the cybersecurity of crypto exchanges. The rating reflects the exchange’s performance in several areas of cybersecurity, including server security, user security, penetration testing and bug bounty management.

These assessments examine the measures exchanges have in place to protect their infrastructure, secure user accounts and identify potential vulnerabilities.

Perfect Scores in Four Security Areas Give Bitunix Users Stronger Protection

To reach an AAA rating, an exchange is judged on how well it protects its systems, how well it protects its users, and how actively it looks for weaknesses. CER.live groups these checks into four areas, and Bitunix scored 100 out of 100 in every one.

Server security. This area looks at how well an exchange protects the systems that run its platform. It checks whether those systems are set up safely and whether they can stand up to common attacks. A score of 100 means CER.live found no gaps in this area.

User security. This area looks at how well an exchange protects its customers’ accounts. It checks the tools that help keep accounts out of the wrong hands. A score of 100 shows that the exchange puts strong protections around the people who use it.

Penetration testing. A penetration test is a simulated attack carried out by security experts. Its goal is to find weak spots before real attackers do. This area measures how actively an exchange tests its own systems. A score of 100 shows that Bitunix looks for problems on its own and does not wait for them to appear.

Bug bounty management. A bug bounty program rewards outside researchers who find and report security flaws. This area measures how well an exchange runs that program and how it deals with the reports it receives. A score of 100 shows that Bitunix welcomes outside help and acts on what it learns.

Bitunix is also ISO 27001 certified, demonstrating its commitment to internationally recognized information security management standards. As an additional layer of financial protection, the exchange maintains a $50 million Care Fund, designed to provide an extra safeguard for user assets in any case scenario. Furthermore, the exchange is working toward CCSS certification.

Rising Crypto Hacks Put Exchange Security Back in the Spotlight

Security has become an increasingly important measure of trust in the cryptocurrency industry, particularly as exchanges continue to face sophisticated cyber threats. Recent incidents have reinforced these concerns, involving billions of dollars. These events highlight the importance of strong security infrastructure, independent testing, and continuous vulnerability monitoring.

In this environment, independent security assessments provide users with an additional way to evaluate the platforms they trust with their assets. Since 2018, CER.live has reviewed hundreds of exchanges, conducting security reviews of platforms across the industry. Its rating system has become an established reference for evaluating exchange security, helping millions of cryptocurrency users better understand the security measures and safeguards implemented by trading platforms.

CER.live ratings are publicly available, and Bitunix’s full results can be viewed on the CER.live exchange page.

About Bitunix

Bitunix is a global cryptocurrency derivatives exchange trusted by over 5 million users across more than 150 countries. Guided by its core principle of better liquidity, better trading, the platform is built for traders who expect more, committed to providing Ultra Trust, Ultra Products, and Ultra Experience. Bitunix offers a fast registration process and a user-friendly verification system to ensure safety and compliance. With global standards of protection through Proof of Reserves (POR) and the Bitunix Care Fund, the exchange prioritizes user trust and fund security. Industry-first innovations like Fixed Risk, TradingView-powered chart suite, along with indicator alerts, cloud-synced templates, provide both beginners and advanced traders with a seamless experience. Making Bitunix one of the most dynamic platforms on the market.

title: Woman who says abortion pills nearly killed her urges RFK Jr to act as group demands mail-order crackdown
description: Haile McAnally, who said she nearly died after taking abortion pills, says mailing mifepristone to doorsteps is reckless as she urges RFK Jr. to act.
fullContent:
FIRST ON FOX: A woman who said she nearly died after taking abortion pills is urging Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to crack down on mail-order access to the drugs, warning that shipping them directly to women's homes is "reckless" and could put more lives at risk.

Haile McAnally, who said she suffered severe bleeding and required a blood transfusion after taking abortion pills 14 years ago, is speaking out in response to a Nov. 6 letter from Susan B. Anthony (SBA) Pro-Life America. The letter called on Kennedy to immediately restore in-person dispensing requirements for mifepristone while the Food and Drug Administration conducts a safety review.

"Mailing them across the country to doorsteps just as easily as you could an Amazon package is not only reckless, it puts a lot of women's lives and safety at risk," McAnally told Fox News Digital.

EX-DEMOCRAT SHARES ABORTION PILL EXPERIENCE THAT LEFT HER 'HEMORRHAGING IN THE BATH'

McAnally, who serves as communications director for the Nebraska Republican Party and works with SBA Pro-Life America on legislation, recalled her harrowing experience that she previously shared with Fox News Digital in September.

"I had my own run-in with abortion pills 14 years ago," McAnally said. "When I took these pills at a clinic and ended up having severe side effects, I wound up alone in my bathtub, almost dying from these pills, needing a blood transfusion at the hospital."

The abortion pill mifepristone blocks progesterone, a hormone needed to sustain pregnancy, and is followed by misoprostol to complete the abortion process.

An April 2025 study conducted by conservative think tank the Ethics and Public Policy Center found that 10.93% of women "experience sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days following a mifepristone abortion."

In its letter, SBA argued that Kennedy has the legal authority to immediately suspend certain drug approvals if he determines they pose an imminent threat to public health.

McAnally said she is imploring Kennedy to have greater oversight of the drug.

FIRST ON FOX: TOP REPUBLICANS TAKE ABORTION PILL FIGHT TO SUPREME COURT, CITING COERCION AND SAFETY RISKS

"I just continue to urge the federal government, especially RFK Jr. and the senators … to make sure that we really think about the ramifications of letting this go through so easily," she said. "I think we really need to put women first, women's safety first and not be so callous about this issue because it's going to be huge. Life is precious. Women's lives are precious, and women's safety deserves the utmost importance when it comes to this issue."

The group points to a Justice Department filing earlier this year that it says confirms Kennedy could use that authority to reverse the Biden administration's 2023 changes allowing mifepristone to be dispensed by mail. The organization is urging Kennedy to reinstate the requirement that abortion pills be dispensed in person while the FDA completes its broader safety review of the drug.

"Secretary Kennedy, you possess clear statutory authority to protect women from this growing form of abuse," the letter reads. "Federal law authorizes the HHS Secretary to suspend the approval of a drug application (including a supplemental application) ‘immediately’ if the Secretary ‘finds that there is an imminent hazard to the public health.’ In a legal brief filed earlier this year on behalf of HHS and FDA, the Department of Justice confirmed with the federal district court your legal authority to immediately suspend supplemental drug approvals — which would include the Biden FDA’s 2023 changes to the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) for mifepristone."

TRUMP TO NOMINATE DR HEIDI OVERTON AS NEXT FDA COMMISSIONER

The Trump administration's reported decision to drop Heidi Overton's nomination adds complications to the debate over abortion pill regulations, as SBA presses Kennedy to act before the FDA completes its mifepristone safety review.

Erik Baptist, senior vice president of legal strategy at SBA Pro-Life America, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Now that the White House has pulled Heidi Overton’s nomination, we look forward to meeting with the administration’s new nominee for FDA Commissioner. We hope to secure two fundamental commitments on abortion-drug policy before the Senate proceeds with any confirmation vote."

Baptist continued, "The administration must immediately end the Biden FDA’s mail-order abortion-drug scheme and protect pregnant women from predators who coerce or poison women with these drugs. And the FDA must fix its flawed safety study by obtaining robust data, increasing real-time transparency, and inviting external experts to help with this study."

He added, "Confirmation is not a coronation. It is a time to vet nominees and seek commitments before they take office."

WOMAN HELD DOWN, FORCE-FED ABORTION PILLS AT HEART OF ‘HELL ON EARTH’ FIGHT OVER BIDEN-ERA POLICY

In the meantime, McAnally stressed the urgency of halting mail-order abortion pills while the FDA completes its safety review.

"We're asking that we put a stop to these mail-order abortion drugs and not only for more research into mifepristone and the side effects, but just because the recklessness and the side effects that these have," McAnally said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Kennedy and the White House for comment.

title: Bitcoin Could Soon Outperform US Treasury Bills Without A Price Rally — Here’s How
description: Bitcoin could become an increasingly attractive asset for institutional investors in 2027, even without a major price rally. According to a new forecast from Swiss digital asset bank Sygnum, Bitcoin carry trades could generate higher returns than short-term US government debt as derivatives markets recover. The prediction comes as institutional Bitcoin trading continues reshaping how […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin could become an increasingly attractive asset for institutional investors in 2027, even without a major price rally. According to a new forecast from Swiss digital asset bank Sygnum, Bitcoin carry trades could generate higher returns than short-term US government debt as derivatives markets recover. The prediction comes as institutional Bitcoin trading continues reshaping how professional investors approach the cryptocurrency market.

The forecast introduces an interesting possibility: Could Bitcoin become a competitive source of investment returns even when its price moves sideways?

Sygnum believes improving funding conditions and renewed institutional demand could make this possible, potentially opening another opportunity for professional investors seeking returns from cryptocurrency markets.

Sygnum Predicts A Major Bitcoin Carry Trade Recovery

In its November 19 2027 Sygnal Outlook, Sygnum predicted that Bitcoin carry trades could outperform US Treasury bills on average next year.

The strategy involves purchasing Bitcoin on the spot market while simultaneously opening a short position in Bitcoin futures.

This combination reduces direct exposure to BTC price movements while allowing investors to potentially capture the difference between spot and futures prices.

For institutional investors, the appeal is straightforward.

Instead of relying entirely on Bitcoin appreciation, traders can seek returns from the structure of the derivatives market.

Sygnum expects the annualized premium on three-month CME Bitcoin futures to average more than two percentage points above three-month Treasury bill yields in 2027.

The bank also expects open-interest-weighted Bitcoin funding rates to exceed Treasury bill yields by a similar margin.

These forecasts are conditional, and actual returns would depend on execution costs, funding changes, and market conditions.

Why Bitcoin Funding Rates Could Become Important Again

Bitcoin’s derivatives market experienced significant changes throughout 2026.

According to Sygnum, Bitcoin’s 30-day average funding rate remained negative for 67 consecutive days through May, representing its longest negative streak of the decade.

By August, the annualized CME Bitcoin futures basis had fallen to approximately 3%, below the 3.8% yield on two-year US Treasury securities.

This made traditional government debt comparatively attractive for investors seeking predictable returns.

However, conditions began improving toward the end of October.

Bitcoin funding rates recovered to approximately 8% annualized, suggesting that demand for leveraged exposure was returning.

The improvement could be important because positive funding conditions create opportunities for traders who hold Bitcoin while maintaining offsetting short positions in perpetual futures.

Nevertheless, funding rates can change rapidly, and a positive annualized snapshot does not guarantee sustained returns.

Why Institutional Investors Could Return To Bitcoin

The recovery in Bitcoin carry opportunities could also reflect changes in institutional positioning.

During previous periods, hedge funds frequently purchased spot Bitcoin ETFs while shorting CME futures to capture the futures premium.

As more investors entered the same trade, competition compressed potential returns.

Bitcoinist previously examined how Bitcoin ETF trading strategies can influence institutional positioning, including the importance of distinguishing directional selling from the unwinding of market-neutral positions.

Sygnum’s outlook suggests that reduced competition could eventually allow futures premiums to widen again.

The bank also points to expanding institutional adoption, tokenization, and Bitcoin’s growing role in investment portfolios as potential sources of demand.

Rather than treating BTC exclusively as a speculative asset, professional investors are increasingly examining how it can function within broader portfolio and derivatives strategies.

However, a carry trade is not equivalent to a directional Bitcoin investment. A fully hedged position may benefit from market premiums without benefiting directly from a BTC price rally.

Could Bitcoin Become More Attractive Than Traditional Assets?

Sygnum’s prediction suggests that Bitcoin derivatives could offer opportunities unavailable in conventional fixed-income markets.

However, comparing carry returns with Treasury yields requires considering their different risk profiles.

US Treasury bills offer government-backed repayment at maturity, while Bitcoin carry trades involve exchange exposure, collateral requirements, derivatives execution, and potentially significant margin risk.

A sudden market movement can force traders to provide additional collateral or unwind positions even when their overall strategy is intended to be market-neutral.

These risks are not merely theoretical. As Bitcoinist previously explored, Bitcoin basis-trade unwinding can amplify market volatility when leveraged institutional positions are rapidly closed.

Higher interest rates could also reduce the attractiveness of Bitcoin carry trades by increasing the return investors can obtain from government debt.

For Sygnum’s forecast to succeed, the improvement in Bitcoin funding conditions would need to persist beyond short-lived periods of leveraged speculation.

What Comes Next For Bitcoin In 2027?

Sygnum’s outlook provides two measurable indicators for evaluating the market.

First, the annualized three-month CME Bitcoin futures basis would need to average more than two percentage points above three-month Treasury bill yields.

Second, open-interest-weighted Bitcoin funding rates would need to maintain a similar advantage.

The bank considers its forecast invalidated if either measure remains below Treasury bill yields for two consecutive quarters.

For Bitcoin investors, the broader significance extends beyond the potential returns of a single trading strategy.

An expanding derivatives market could improve liquidity, attract additional institutional participants, and support Bitcoin’s integration into traditional financial portfolios.

If these developments continue, Bitcoin’s next stage of institutional adoption may depend not only on how high BTC can climb, but also on the financial opportunities created around the asset itself.

title: Ripple CEO Sees Crypto Comeback After Anthropic IPO: Is History About to Repeat?
description: Ripple's Brad Garlinghouse believes Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut could mark a turning point for cryptocurrencies, drawing comparisons to Bitcoin's recovery following the SpaceX IPO.
fullContent:
The CEO of Ripple, Brad Garlinghouse, gave an interesting explanation for the crypto market’s recent struggles, one that seems to be shared by quite a few experts.

He suggested that Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering has been attracting liquidity away from the market – one that otherwise might have flowed into digital assets.

Garlinghouse gave an interview for CNBC on November 19 and argued that investors are redirecting capital toward major public listings, with Anthropic’s record-breaking $81.3 billion offering attracting considerable attention.

Recall that the AI giant priced its shares at $83 a pop, securing a valuation of $1.5 trillion.

Ripple’s CEO thinks that once the IPO goes through, this could ease some of the pressure on crypto markets, potentially paving the way for a recovery.

Bitcoin’s Previous Comeback Offers Hope

As mentioned in the beginning, Ripple’s CEO isn’t the only one who’s drawing parallels with previous market cycles. As we recently reported, Bitcoin’s approximately 28% correction ahead of the AI giant’s public debut closely resembles its decline before SpaceX went public in June.

Back then, the cryptocurrency plunged toward $59K before staging an impressive comeback that eventually took it all the way above $80K.

Of course, history doesn’t necessarily repeat itself, but it oftentimes rhymes.

That said, the latest decline has also been fueled by persistent inflation cocnerns, expectations of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes, and substantial liquidations.

Moreover, XRP has experienced its very own difficulties, recently slipping below the psychological and technical barrier of $1 amid declining speculative activity.

This means that whether Anthropic’s IPO proves to be the actual catalyst for another crypto rally remains uncertain.

title: XRP on the Brink of a Major Breakout? Analyst Flags Key Resistance
description: XRP is approaching a third test of its 6-year support floor, a setup that compares with past 85% to 95% corrections before major breakouts.
fullContent:
XRP is approaching a 6-year ascending support level for a potential third retest, with the token recently falling below $1.

According to analyst ChartNerd, that area could provide a base for another major rally, although he warned that there are still several resistance levels in the way.

XRP’s Long-Term Support Comes Back Into Focus

The market watcher noted that XRP had spent the last 6 months moving closer to the long-term support floor, with the current setup looking like it could be the third time it tests it.

“Historically, 85-95% corrections have established the retests preceding major breakouts,” he added.

If that line holds, then the structure will be confirmed. However, he added that resistance sits between $1.03 and $1.14, where the daily 20-day EMA and other technical levels are converging.

Meanwhile, the 50-day EMA is near $1.20, with $1.25 marking a former support level that XRP lost during its fall. In the analyst’s estimation, a rejection in these areas could send the asset back to $0.89, with the possibility of it hitting $0.70 in the long term.

Furthermore, the chartist pointed to XRP’s 3-month Gaussian Channel, whose upper regression band has gone up to $0.84, a level only a few cents away from where recent price action took the token. Encounters with the band in the past, per ChartNerd’s analysis, have often coincided with periods of accumulation, although he cautioned that it didn’t identify exact market bottoms.

What the Market Shows

At the time of writing, the world’s 6th-largest cryptocurrency was back under $1, after suffering a 2% dip in 24 hours. The same weakness was evident on other timeframes, including a nearly 6% drop over the last seven days and much larger losses over two weeks and one month, at 25% and 24%, respectively.

XRP is also 54% lower than it was around the same time last year and remains 73% below its all-time high of $3.65, recorded in July 2025.

And spot XRP ETFs haven’t helped much either, with the last positive flows coming in late October. Since then, there have been 8 days of zero activity and 6 days that saw outflows ranging from just under $500,000 to about $10.4 million.

The post TSMC Stock Falls 5% on China Chip Pause: What Is at Risk? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
TSMC stock has fallen about 5% in Taipei since a new US export rule landed. The foundry has paused some China chip shipments, the Financial Times reported, yet China supplies 5% of its revenue.

Samsung Electronics paused deliveries too, and its shares are roughly flat over the same sessions. The sharper selling hit the Chinese companies that buy the chips.

Is TSMC Stock the Real Casualty?

Exchange data shows the decline measures Thursday’s Taipei close against Monday’s, the last session before the rule’s release.

Samsung ended Thursday almost exactly where it closed on Monday.

Alibaba lost about 8% in Hong Kong over those sessions.

Baidu’s stock also suffered as its Kunlun chip unit is a Samsung client, according to the FT.

Chinese technology companies were already short of components before the rule, the FT reported. The pause removes another source of supply.

Other catalysts hit chip stocks in those sessions, so the rule is not the sole driver.

What Does 5% of Revenue Look Like in Dollars?

Customers based in China supplied 5% of TSMC’s third-quarter net revenue, its management report shows. That equals roughly $2.3 billion.

The share was 8% a year earlier.

The rule covers only part of that sum. It comes from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department’s export regulator, and targets advanced logic chips.

Designers located or headquartered in China can no longer clear such chips through approved packaging firms. The foundry now needs a license.

Anyway, most of TSMC’s revenue comes from North American customers. If idled capacity shifts to them, the net loss could land below 5%.

That read fails if licenses stall and the affected lines cannot be refilled.

BIS applied a headquarters test to chip sellers through earlier BIS guidance this year. This rule moves that test onto the factories, and equity markets are charging the customers more than the foundry.

title: Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets
description:
A U.S. appellate court is upholding Maryland's right to enforce its sports wagering laws against Kalshi, marking another win for state oversight over federal preemption claims.
The post Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A U.S. appellate court is affirming Maryland’s authority to enforce its sports wagering laws against the prediction market platform Kalshi.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit says the Commodity Exchange Act does not clearly preempt the state’s gaming laws even for event contracts on a CFTC-regulated designated contract market.

Judge Gregory concurring emphasizes that the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power.

“Because the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power, I would not infer that Congress displaced Maryland’s concurrent authority absent a clear expression of its intent to do so.”

The decision rejects Kalshi’s preemption arguments and finds no impossibility or obstacle to federal objectives.

Maryland Attorney General Anthony G. Brown says the ruling requires Kalshi to meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.

“When betting platforms operate outside State oversight, Marylanders lose the protections that keep gambling fair and safe.”

“Today’s ruling means Kalshi must meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.”

The per curiam opinion in case No. 25-1892 was decided November 18, 2026, after arguments on May 7, 2026.

description:

The post Bitcoin Nears $62,862 Mining Cost: Will BTC Price Hold Above This Level or Break Below It? appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
CryptoQuant founder Ki Young Ju said Noted that Bitcoin (BTC USD) has fallen to the price it costs to mine one Bitcoin. His chart, built from MARA Holdings’ filings, puts the miner’s average cost at $62,862 per coin in the third quarter. Bitcoin dipped to $62,063 on Wednesday and trades near $63,900 on Thursday.

“A break below could pressure public miners and their institutional backers,” Ki wrote on X. Below that price, a miner spends more to produce a coin than the coin is worth.

We checked how that line held up before. Bitcoin closed below $62,862 on 18 days since January 2025, all between June and August of this year. Each time, it was back above the line within a month.

This time, though, two forces push the other way: MARA is selling its Bitcoin, and ETF investors are pulling money out.

BTC USD Below Mining Cost: What Happened the Last Six Times

We compared Binance’s daily BTC USD closes since January 2025 with the $62,862 line. Bitcoin dropped below it in six separate stretches, all this summer.

  • Short dips: five of the six stretches lasted one or two days, in early June, July and on August 1.
  • The long one: from June 23 to July 3, Bitcoin closed below cost 11 days in a row. It hit $57,800 on July 1, its lowest price of the past year.
  • The recovery: 30 days after each stretch ended, Bitcoin was back above the line, but only by 1% to 3% in five cases. The exception was August 1, which was followed by a 25% rally to over $78,000.

So the mining cost has acted as a floor, but a soft one. It stopped the falls without starting a rally, until August.

The cost line also moves. MARA’s cost was close to $60,000 in the second quarter, so this summer’s dips were tested against a slightly lower bar than today’s.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $62K: Did Mara’s $1B BTC Sale Cause It?

MARA Is Selling, and ETF Investors Are Leaving

Two groups that usually support the price are selling instead.

  • MARA: the largest listed miner sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion over six weeks, at an average of about $81,000, roughly 29% above its own mining cost. It said it would keep selling to fund AI data centers. At today’s price, that margin has shrunk to about 2%.
  • Spot Bitcoin ETFs: these funds, which hold the coin itself, lost a net $239.9 million on Monday, November 17, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $209.5 million. That came a day after IBIT’s first inflow in 11 sessions. Early figures point to another $306 million out on Tuesday.

The miners aren’t giving up, though. The network’s hashrate, the total computing power securing Bitcoin, averaged about 1,015 exahashes per second over the past 30 days. That’s 9% below its November 2025 peak but 13% above its August low. Miners are still adding machines, a sign they expect higher prices later.

DISCOVER: 20+ Next Crypto to Explode in 2026

BTC USD Price Analysis: The Mining Cost and $62,300 Sit Together

On the daily chart, BTC USD trades at $63,879. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,252, and its 200-day EMA at $75,625.

  • Support: $62,300, just below the $62,862 mining cost. Bitcoin bounced near it on Sunday and Wednesday, after it also held in February, June, July and August. Below it, $57,800, the July low.
  • Resistance: $65,500, a level Bitcoin bounced from in early 2026 and was turned back from in June, July and August. Above that, $74,300.

BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

Path What has to happen Next stop
Bullish A daily close above $65,500 as ETF outflows stop $74,300, the March-September level
Sideways Price holds between $62,300 and $65,500 A range near the mining cost
Bearish A daily close below $62,300 and the mining cost $57,800, the July low

BTC USD has climbed back above the mining cost after all six dips this year. This time, miners are sellers and ETF money is leaving, so another recovery needs buyers to show up, not just sellers to stop.

title: HYPE Price Escapes One Trap, Walks Into Another
description:
Key Takeaways HYPE has left its late-October downtrend channel Two key resistance levels overlap near $70 Momentum still leans toward […]
The post HYPE Price Escapes One Trap, Walks Into Another appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • HYPE has left its late-October downtrend channel
  • Two key resistance levels overlap near $70
  • Momentum still leans toward sellers
  • Team token unlocks begin November 29

The slide has hit a token that public companies have been accumulating: Hyperliquid Strategies (Nasdaq: PURR) reported spending $785 million on 9.1 million HYPE between July and September, lifting its treasury to 38.5 million tokens.

How HYPE Got Here

HYPE’s decline began in late October and followed a steep descending channel, a downward-sloping corridor formed by two parallel lines that contained almost every daily candle for the next three weeks. The heaviest trading volume of the period came at the start of that slide and again in mid-November, when sellers were most active.

The mid-November leg did the most damage. It pushed HYPE below its 200-day simple moving average (SMA), the average closing price of the past 200 days and a line many traders treat as the boundary between a healthy and a weakening trend. Until then, HYPE had stayed above that average for months. The same sell-off dragged the 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI), a momentum gauge running from 0 to 100, down toward the 30 mark that traders read as oversold.

The Rebound So Far

Since that low, HYPE has climbed out of the channel. On the daily chart it trades around $69, above the corridor’s upper line, which shows sellers can no longer push the price down at the pace they managed earlier in the month.

The bounce has been cautious, though. RSI has recovered to about 38, only slightly above its signal line near 37 and still well short of the 50 mark associated with buyers taking control.

Why the Rally Stalls Just Below $70

Traders often map pullbacks with Fibonacci retracement levels, horizontal lines drawn at set percentages between a major low and high. Measured from HYPE’s late-July swing low to the spike high near $100 on this chart, the 0.618 retracement, one of the most closely watched, sits close to $70.

The 200-day SMA also runs at about $70, within a fraction of a dollar of that Fibonacci level. Before mid-November, this zone acted as a floor under HYPE. Now price is testing it from below, the position in which old support often turns into resistance. The last few sessions show that contest: one candle’s high poked above the zone, the next closed back near $67, and today’s session bounced from a low around $66.

What the Next Daily Close Would Signal

A single intraday spike in either direction says little. A daily close on either side of the $70 zone carries more weight.

If buyers break through

A decisive daily close above $70 would put HYPE back over both the 0.618 level and the 200-day SMA. If the zone then holds as support on a retest, the channel escape would become a reversal setup, with room opening toward the 0.5 Fibonacci level around $75.

If sellers hold the line

A push into the $70 zone followed by a close back below it would confirm the area has flipped to resistance. HYPE would then risk sliding back toward or inside the channel, with the 0.786 Fibonacci level near $61 in view, an area the mid-November low briefly dipped under.

Bigger Hurdles Further Up

Even a clean break above $70 leaves heavier resistance overhead. The 50-day SMA has been falling since early November and now sits just under the 100-day SMA, with both near $80 on the live candle. A daily close at those readings would confirm that the faster average has crossed below the slower one, a shift traders read as medium-term weakness.

The supply calendar adds another factor. FalconX research notes that HYPE’s first team token unlocks begin on November 29, bringing newly released tokens to market while price is still working through these levels.

fullContent:
After a much anticipated retail step, HSBC opened an HSBC RedCoin tokenised fund path for Hong Kong clients. Eligible customers can spend HSBC RedCoin in the HSBC HK App. They buy Class SD units of HSBC Global Money Funds – Hong Kong Dollar. Interestingly, the offer lands while RedCoin still sits early on PayMe rails and bank apps.

HSBC RedCoin Tokenised Fund Draws Orders Despite Token Rails

HSBC Global Asset Management set the Class SD public launch date at 18 November 2026. According to the October 2026 product brochure, one token represents one Class SD unit. Ownership sits on a permissioned blockchain. Meanwhile, the mutual funds page lists tokenised funds as now available on the HSBC HK App. The same page sets the entry at HKD100, funded with RCHKD100. According to the Guide to Tokenised Funds, subscription and settlement use HSBC RedCoin. Class SD Units can only be subscribed and redeemed through Eligible Distributors. The manager appoints those distributors.

The fund itself launched on 1 March 1991. According to HSBC Asset Management, fund size was HKD 20,774 million as of 30 September 2026. That is about HK$20.8 billion in short-term HKD deposits and money market paper. Weighted average maturity was 32 days on that date. Class SD carries a 0.30% management fee. Fitch rates the fund AAAmmf. Dividends declared on each business day reinvest into Class SD the same day. Cash dividend payouts are not available on that class. Capital preservation is not guaranteed. According to the firm, Class SD is a new share class on the same fund, not a new fund. It keeps the same underlying money market exposure as the older share classes. Dealing is daily on every dealing day. Switching out of the tokenised class is not permitted.

Meanwhile, RedCoin (RCHKD) is the licensed HKD stablecoin HSBC put on PayMe on 23 October 2026, after an early user ramp. The launch note said a tokenised money market share class would follow on the HSBC HK App. That rail is now live for the Class SD window. The brochure says Eligible Distributors must be SFC-licensed for dealing in securities or virtual asset trading. Tokenisation adds blockchain, custody, and distributor risks. Those sit beside ordinary money market risk. According to HSBC, buying units is not placing a bank deposit. The units are not under Hong Kong Monetary Authority deposit supervision. After a much anticipated wait, eligible Hong Kong clients can now clear a HKD money market order with RedCoin inside the banking app.

The post PDAX Lets Stablecoins Fund Philippine Retail Dollar Bonds appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
After a much anticipated Retail Dollar Bonds Tranche 3 window, Philippine Digital Asset Exchange opened a PDAX stablecoin Philippine bonds funding path. Eligible USD stablecoins can fund those bond orders on the live public offer. Interestingly, the window lands while Manila still seeks at least $200 million from three-year onshore dollar notes due 2029.

PDAX Stablecoin Philippine Bonds Draw Orders Despite Friction

The Bureau of the Treasury set the public offer from November 19 to November 24. The issue date is November 27. According to The Philippine Star, citing the Treasury notice of offering, the minimum purchase is $200. The ceiling per order is the dollar equivalent of P500,000. Meanwhile, the final coupon is set through a Dutch auction among Government Securities Eligible Dealers. According to the same report, GCash GBonds and bank channels also take orders beside PDAX.

PDAX users fund the RDB3/USD pair after they hold enough USD. According to PDAX support, eligible USD stablecoins convert to USD in the FX tab at the live rate during set periods. According to Solana, the tokens accepted on the Solana network for this path include PYUSD, USDG, and USDPT. PHP cash-in and direct USD deposits also create USD. Meanwhile, PDAX Securities acts as the broker-dealer. Holdings sit in the investor's National Registry of Scripless Securities account.

PDAX is a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas-supervised exchange that already sells Philippine government bonds in its app. Bank branches still take dollar retail orders. PDAX routes the same BTr paper through an in-app FX* balance that can start as a stablecoin. According to founder and CEO Nichel Gaba, Filipinos can buy the bonds through the PDAX app from $200. He said they do not need deep wealth or a private banker to reach that dollar paper.

The Offer Terms on the Table

Interestingly, the stablecoin conversion is not an open-ended tap. According to PDAX support, that option runs only in specified periods, and the live pairs sit in the app. Meanwhile, the Treasury can close the offer early or adjust the window. The bonds pay interest in USD on a quarterly schedule after issuance. Principal returns in USD at maturity. PDAX said it charges no primary-offer fees on the RDB 3 window. According to The Philippine Star, this is the third Retail Dollar Bond sale. The prior RDB 2 raise brought in $1.26 billion in October 2023. The maiden sale raised $1.6 billion in 2021. After a much anticipated wait, that stablecoin funding door now clears into the same sovereign paper.

title: World's top court rules Myanmar acted with 'genocidal intent' against Rohingya
description:
The United Nations’ top court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya population.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) at The Hague delivered its judgement on Thursday about the military crackdown that drove more than 730,000 mainly Muslim Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.
ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said the court, in a 9-6 decision, found that Myanmar “has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention”.
It is the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide at the court. The ruling marked only the fourth time since the Nazi Holocaust that an international court ruled that the crime had been committed.
The case was brought by the West African nation of The Gambia, which in 2019 accused Myanmar of seeking to destroy the Rohingya people. It asked the ICJ to rule that Myanmar breached the 1948 Genocide Convention, order it to end any illegal activities targeting the Rohingya and ensure those responsible for genocide are punished.
Myanmar claimed its crackdown was in response to attacks on police posts by fighters from the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA).
Evidence shows Myanmar forces killed 10,000 Rohingya, Iwasawa said during a three-hour readout of the verdict.
“The Court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya ⁠⁠civilians, perpetrated widespread acts ⁠⁠of sexual violence as well as acts of ⁠⁠extreme violence against children and ⁠⁠attacked fleeing Rohingya ⁠⁠as they sought to flee in large numbers to ‌‌Bangladesh,” he added.
In specific cases that he referred to, he said Myanmar had acted with “genocidal intent”.
The ICJ said that the “only reasonable inference” from evidence of widespread atrocities by Myanmar security forces is that they had the intent to destroy a “substantial part” of the Rohingya minority.
It said Myanmar should have known that there was a risk of genocide when armed civilians participated in the military campaign. “Myanmar thus violated its obligation to prevent genocide,” it added.
Myanmar is now obliged to provide reparations and restitution “as a result of Myanmar’s wrongful acts”, Iwasawa said.
The court said appropriate restitution by Myanmar would include: Facilitating the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya; returning or replacing all collective property damaged; facilitating the search for the disappeared and ensuring proper burials; providing for the physical and psychological rehabilitation of those mentally injured; and ensuring the population’s protection from persecution.
		

						 					



						
‘Waiting’ years for justice
The court established that at least four genocidal acts have been proven, said Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen, reporting from the Hague. They are the mass killing of civilians; the forced displacement of hundreds of thousands of people; serious harm inflicted upon the group; and the prevention of birth.
The Rohingya have long been treated as second-class citizens, well before 2017, according to the judge, Vaessen said. They were also forced to take part in a birth control programme, she added.
“So the judge really saw this as a very strong explanation that … a genocidal act was committed there.”
The verdict is “extremely important for the Rohingya,” our correspondent said. “They’ve been waiting for 10 years for any kind of justice, but it’s also important for the whole international community because genocide is such a difficult act to prove.”
The hardest part of any genocide case is proving specific intent to destroy a group in whole or in part – an extremely high bar – said Toby Cadman, an international human rights lawyer. He noted that the ICJ had never before ruled that a state has specific intent to commit genocide.
“The court is guided by the genocide convention and what the genocide convention states and it is a high threshold,” Cadman told Al Jazeera.
Human rights organisations welcomed the judgement. “We hope this ruling marks the beginning of a long overdue process of accountability in Myanmar,” Amnesty International said in a statement. It added that all crimes under international law “must be effectively investigated and those suspected of responsibility brought to justice”.
Cadman said that the situation does not come to an end with the ICJ’s ruling and a lot will depend on what comes next. This includes whether the issue goes before the UN Security Council and whether there are sanctions, or other remedies that the court can order to ensure it is enforced.
More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced across South and Southeast Asia, including 1.2 million in sprawling refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh, according to the UN. Conflict, shrinking humanitarian aid and dangerous sea crossings continue to leave many members of the community displaced and vulnerable.
		

						 					



						
This article originally appeared on Al Jazeera at https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/19/un-top-court-finds-myanmar-killed-10000-rohingya-as-it-rules-on-genocide

Myanmar claimed its crackdown was in response to attacks on police posts by fighters from the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA).

Evidence shows Myanmar forces killed 10,000 Rohingya, Iwasawa said during a three-hour readout of the verdict.

“The Court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya ⁠⁠civilians, perpetrated widespread acts ⁠⁠of sexual violence as well as acts of ⁠⁠extreme violence against children and ⁠⁠attacked fleeing Rohingya ⁠⁠as they sought to flee in large numbers to ‌‌Bangladesh,” he added.

In specific cases that he referred to, he said Myanmar had acted with “genocidal intent”.

The ICJ said that the “only reasonable inference” from evidence of widespread atrocities by Myanmar security forces is that they had the intent to destroy a “substantial part” of the Rohingya minority.

It said Myanmar should have known that there was a risk of genocide when armed civilians participated in the military campaign. “Myanmar thus violated its obligation to prevent genocide,” it added.

Myanmar is now obliged to provide reparations and restitution “as a result of Myanmar’s wrongful acts”, Iwasawa said.

The court said appropriate restitution by Myanmar would include: Facilitating the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya; returning or replacing all collective property damaged; facilitating the search for the disappeared and ensuring proper burials; providing for the physical and psychological rehabilitation of those mentally injured; and ensuring the population’s protection from persecution.


‘Waiting’ years for justice

The court established that at least four genocidal acts have been proven, said Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen, reporting from the Hague. They are the mass killing of civilians; the forced displacement of hundreds of thousands of people; serious harm inflicted upon the group; and the prevention of birth.

The Rohingya have long been treated as second-class citizens, well before 2017, according to the judge, Vaessen said. They were also forced to take part in a birth control programme, she added.

“So the judge really saw this as a very strong explanation that … a genocidal act was committed there.”

The verdict is “extremely important for the Rohingya,” our correspondent said. “They’ve been waiting for 10 years for any kind of justice, but it’s also important for the whole international community because genocide is such a difficult act to prove.”

The hardest part of any genocide case is proving specific intent to destroy a group in whole or in part – an extremely high bar – said Toby Cadman, an international human rights lawyer. He noted that the ICJ had never before ruled that a state has specific intent to commit genocide.

“The court is guided by the genocide convention and what the genocide convention states and it is a high threshold,” Cadman told Al Jazeera.

Human rights organisations welcomed the judgement. “We hope this ruling marks the beginning of a long overdue process of accountability in Myanmar,” Amnesty International said in a statement. It added that all crimes under international law “must be effectively investigated and those suspected of responsibility brought to justice”.

Cadman said that the situation does not come to an end with the ICJ’s ruling and a lot will depend on what comes next. This includes whether the issue goes before the UN Security Council and whether there are sanctions, or other remedies that the court can order to ensure it is enforced.

More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced across South and Southeast Asia, including 1.2 million in sprawling refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh, according to the UN. Conflict, shrinking humanitarian aid and dangerous sea crossings continue to leave many members of the community displaced and vulnerable.

title: LBank’s IN SYNC Initiative Takes Its Youthful Brand Strategy Beyond Crypto
description: LBank’s IN SYNC Initiative Takes Its Youthful Brand Strategy Beyond Crypto
fullContent:
Singapore, Singapore, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

Crypto exchanges have spent years competing on trading fees, token listings, liquidity, and product features. But as the market matures and platforms increasingly offer similar trading experiences, another contest is taking shape: who can stay relevant when users are not trading? LBank is approaching that question through gaming, internet culture and community-led campaigns, with its latest collaboration bringing the exchange, SHIB and Grand Theft Auto-inspired themes into a Thanksgiving campaign offering up to 150,000 USDT in rewards.

The campaign is part of a broader direction LBank has been developing around cultural engagement rather than treating marketing as a series of isolated trading promotions. Following its October 26 brand upgrade, the exchange introduced a new positioning, “Your Go-To Crypto Plug,” intended to reflect a brand that connects users with crypto opportunities, communities and experiences beyond the trading screen. The subsequent launch of IN SYNC formalizes that direction into a longer-term initiative spanning gaming, esports, anime, music, creative content and other interest-based communities.

Gaming is a natural entry point for that strategy. GTA has become more than a game franchise, with its online conversation, memes, anticipation and surrounding internet culture reaching far beyond its core player base. By combining GTA-related hype with SHIB and a Thanksgiving campaign, LBank is looking to place its brand within conversations users are already having, rather than relying exclusively on crypto-native channels to attract attention. The campaign reflects a wider shift in how exchanges approach user acquisition: cultural relevance can help introduce a brand to audiences who may not actively follow market news, token launches or trading competitions.

IN SYNC is designed to extend that approach beyond individual collaborations. One of its recurring formats, LBank Wednesday, turns Wednesdays into a regular community touchpoint through creative challenges, interactive content, gaming-inspired activities and rewards. Instead of depending on occasional large campaigns to generate engagement, the weekly format creates a consistent reason for users to return, participate and share. The idea is closer to a recurring internet content series than a conventional exchange promotion, giving LBank a more regular presence in users’ online routines.

The initiative also extends into education and talent development through NEXT-GEN TRADER LAB, a program under LBank Labs that will bring simulated trading competitions and campus engagement initiatives to universities. Participants will be able to explore crypto market dynamics through simulated trading rather than putting real capital at risk, while the program is also expected to include campus ambassador opportunities. Together, LBank Wednesday and NEXT-GEN TRADER LAB address two different sides of the same strategy: building cultural familiarity through participation while introducing younger audiences to the market through structured learning.

The new initiative builds on LBank’s previous IP collaborations, including partnerships and campaigns involving Pudgy Penguins, YETI, PONKE and Nobody Sausage. These projects have brought different communities, visual identities and internet-native characters into the exchange’s marketing. The approach points toward what LBank describes as “IP Liquidity”—the ability to connect the attention, community energy and cultural recognition surrounding an IP with a platform’s broader brand and user ecosystem. Rather than simply borrowing an IP’s popularity for a short-lived promotion, the challenge is to create experiences that give both communities a reason to interact and make the collaboration feel relevant beyond the campaign itself.

That distinction may become increasingly important in a market where exchanges are competing for users in a more crowded environment. Product depth, trading infrastructure and liquidity remain essential, but they may not always be enough to establish a distinct brand identity when competitors are offering increasingly similar services. LBank’s strategy suggests that cultural participation could become another layer of differentiation—one built through recurring content, creative collaborations and communities that extend beyond crypto. Its positioning as “Your Go-To Crypto Plug” is ultimately a test of whether an exchange can become part of users’ wider digital lives, not just a place they visit when markets move. IN SYNC is LBank’s attempt to build that connection over time, with gaming culture, IP collaborations and community participation serving as the starting point.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Drops Under $64K, Pi Network (PI) Falls to New ATL: Market Watch
description: The total crypto market capitalization currently hovers slightly above $2.2 trillion.
fullContent:
The cryptocurrency market experienced another correction over the past 24 hours, with BTC briefly slipping to around $62,000.

Popular altcoins like Pi Network’s PI, ASTER, and SKY posted even larger declines, while certain AI-related digital assets are among the few in the green today (November 19).

BTC Under Pressure Again

The primary cryptocurrency, which spent most of the week consolidating around $64,000-$65,000, suffered another pullback. Several hours ago, it headed south, and the bulls managed to stop the free fall at approximately $62K.

They even attempted to reclaim some of the lost ground, and BTC currently trades near $63,800, down 2% on a daily basis and 14% over the past week.

One potential reason for the latest decline is the upcoming IPO of AI giant Anthropic, whose shares are expected to begin trading later today. Some market observers believe the event could temporarily divert capital from risk assets like Bitcoin as investors reposition funds to gain exposure to one of the year’s most anticipated public listings. As a result, heightened interest in Anthropic’s debut on Nasdaq may add further pressure on BTC during an already fragile period for the crypto market.

A similar pattern was observed earlier this year ahead of SpaceX’s IPO. Back then, BTC suffered a sharp correction in the weeks leading up to the listing as some investors supposedly rotated capital into the highly anticipated stock offering. However, once the IPO hype faded, BTC managed to regain a significant portion of its losses.

Following the recent pullback, the asset’s market capitalization dropped to around $1.28 trillion, while its dominance over the altcoins plunged to 59%.

New Historical Bottom for PI

Numerous altcoins followed BTC’s lead and also headed south over the last 24 hours. SKY is the worst-performing top 100 cryptocurrency today, posting a 12% daily loss, followed by ASTER (-6%). For its part, Pi Network’s native token tumbled by 5%, thus slipping to a new all-time low of around $0.057.

Among the few gainers are AI-related tokens, including PEARL (+23%), PIEVERSE (+21%), and VVV (+10%). Meanwhile, Bitway (BTW), which fell sharply last week, rebounded 32% today.

The total market capitalization is down 0.9% for the day and is currently around $2.21 trillion.

title: GTA 6 Flu Is Here: The Impact on Crypto Markets
description:
GTA 6 is taking over workplaces and social media as crypto markets go quiet. Could the gaming frenzy pull retail traders away from crypto?
The post GTA 6 Flu Is Here: The Impact on Crypto Markets appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
GTA 6 has finally arrived, and millions of gamers are putting everything else on hold, including crypto portfolios.

After 13 years of waiting, Rockstar’s blockbuster release is already disrupting workplaces, dominating social media, and pulling gamers away from their usual routines. Even our newsroom is feeling the impact, with maybe 30% of employees taking days off.

Could GTA 6 be stealing retail’s attention just as digital asset markets struggle to bring individual investors back?

GTA 6 Could Be Taking Retail Attention Away From Crypto

The scale of the launch is hard to ignore. GTA 6 sold around 17.1 million copies before its worldwide release. The game also carries expectations of $1.85 billion in revenue during its first three days.

Workers are making room for it, too. UKG data covering two million US employees showed time-off requests for launch day running about 20% above normal levels. A separate Zety survey found 22% of Gen Z workers planned around the release.

That is a sizeable chunk of the demographic that crypto platforms have spent years trying to attract. The overlap of both gaming and crypto competes for online attention, particularly among younger audiences who spend hours on streaming platforms, social media and digital communities.

For us, checking Bitcoin prices, chasing the latest meme coin and following market-moving posts can easily become part of the daily routine. But GTA 6 offers something considerably more entertaining than watching another sideways trading session.

The launch is also driving enormous engagement across YouTube and Reddit. Sensor Tower estimates point to more than 50 million additional visits to food delivery and restaurant apps in the US over 30 days.

Crypto’s social media ecosystem could find itself competing for a much smaller share of that attention.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Crypto Retail Activity Was Already Losing Steam

There is another reason the timing is interesting. Retail crypto trading has been weakening even as the broader market has attracted fresh capital.

Data reported from eToro clients placed 62% fewer crypto trades in October than a year earlier. Robinhood’s crypto trading volume also fell 48% year over year in the third quarter, while Coinbase consumer spot volume dropped 59%.

The figures show that rising market valuations have not translated into the same level of retail trading activity seen during previous cycles.

This leaves crypto exposed to competition for speculative attention. Institutional investors can continue trading through market cycles, but retail often depends on excitement, momentum, and whatever narrative is dominating the internet.

But GTA 6 has all three. The game could temporarily pull casual traders away from exchanges, particularly those who spend their evenings chasing small-cap tokens and following crypto KOLs. Meme coins could be especially vulnerable if their usual audience spends the next several days exploring Vice City instead.

There is also an ironic possibility that GTA 6 could create fresh opportunities for crypto speculation. Gaming-themed tokens and GTA-related meme coins could attract traders looking to profit from the launch itself.

Bitcoin does not need gamers watching charts every minute to keep trading. But an industry built around speculation, online communities, and retail enthusiasm cannot afford to ignore where that attention goes.

His arrest was one of five in Florida tied to fraud schemes linked to more than $54 million in losses at over 65 financial institutions nationwide.

The operation involved FBI offices in Miami, Nashville, New York, Columbia, Houston and Omaha.

Four suspects were arrested in South Florida while a fifth South Florida resident was arrested in Central Florida.

title: DECOM Invests in AmericanFortress™  to Back Private, Post-Quantum Payments on Existing Blockchains
description: The Swiss venture capital and digital asset firm backs the company behind FortressName™, the name people send crypto to instead of a wallet address, ahead of the $AF token launch.
fullContent:
The Swiss venture capital and digital asset firm backs the company behind FortressName™, the name people send crypto to instead of a wallet address, ahead of the $AF token launch.

Switzerland AG, a Swiss investment firm specializing in asset management and digital assets, and AmericanFortress, the privacy and post-quantum layer for existing blockchains, today announced DECOM’s investment in AmericanFortress. 

The investment comes as AmericanFortress prepares its token generation event on Dec 1st 2026 and the production launch of the AmericanFortress Wallet. It adds a Swiss institutional investor to a group that includes Selini Capital, 0G Foundation and SAVA Digital Asset Fund. Beyond the capital, DECOM will introduce AmericanFortress’s technology to its Swiss network.

"We back infrastructure our own investors will need. Privacy that keeps investors inside regulated markets, and protection against quantum attacks, are both on that list," said Henok Teweld, Managing Partner at DECOM Switzerland AG. "AmericanFortress delivers both on existing blockchains, with patents behind it. That is why we invested."

DECOM invests at Seed to Series A in blockchain infrastructure, DeFi, AI and emerging Web3 technologies, and manages and custodies digital assets for private and high-net-worth investors. Its portfolio includes 0G, where the $AF token deploys and which is itself an AmericanFortress investor.

DECOM's clients face the problem AmericanFortress was built to remove: on a public blockchain, paying someone can expose who else you deal with and what you hold. The usual alternatives are mixers, which cut users off from regulated venues, or moving funds to a separate privacy chain.

AmericanFortress does neither. It works on the blockchains people already use, without asking a chain to change and without mixing.

"Asset managers understand the problem better than anyone. Their clients cannot run a business on a ledger that shows every counterparty to every competitor, and they cannot touch a mixer," said Michal Pospieszalski, CEO and CTO of AmericanFortress. "DECOM has been investing in and managing digital assets since 2017. Having a Swiss firm with that record invest in us says the market wants privacy that works with regulation, on the chains it already uses."

A FortressName™ is a human-readable name, such as @alice, that replaces the long wallet address. People send crypto to the name, and one name works across the 13 blockchains AmericanFortress supports. Each sender gets their own private address for that name, one only the sender and the recipient can compute. A counterparty who pays you does not see who else has paid you or what you hold. The technology is patented.

Paid names include FortressID™, a verified identity powered by Sumsub. The holder can prove who they are to a counterparty or a regulator, and choose what to disclose, field by field.

AmericanFortress also addresses the quantum threat to today's wallets. Its zero-knowledge proof, ZK-POSP, protects funds against a quantum attacker and is going to be deployed in the AmericanFortress Wallet and SDK.

About AmericanFortress

AmericanFortress (MatterFi, Inc. d/b/a AmericanFortress) is a privacy and post-quantum layer for existing blockchains. It does not ask a chain to change, does not require users to move funds to a privacy chain, and does not mix. FortressNames let users send crypto to a name instead of an address across 13 chains, with each pair of users getting a private address space only they can compute. The company holds a portfolio of 16 patents, including two granted, covering 30+ inventions. Partners include Brinks, the Litecoin Foundation, 0G Network, Tron and Arbitrum. More at americanfortress.io.

About DECOM Switzerland AG

DECOM Switzerland AG, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Sursee, Switzerland, is a Swiss investment firm specializing in venture capital, asset management and digital assets. The firm combines early-stage investments in blockchain and Web3 companies, primarily Seed to Series A, with professional digital asset management and custody for private and high-net-worth investors. Portfolio investments include Bitway (formerly Side Protocol), Orochi Network, Lumio, 0G and OptimAI. DECOM is a Swiss financial intermediary affiliated with VQF, a FINMA-recognized self-regulatory organization, and is subject to applicable Swiss anti-money laundering regulations. More at decom.ch.

title: Critics have gone wild for 'GTA 6' — and say it's about way more than crime and chaos
description:
The much-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here, and critics who have spent weeks playing it before the public say it's worth the hype.
The open-world format of GTA 6 allows gamers to explore Vice City, the sun-drenched fictional Miami-like metropolis in the Florida-like state of Leonida, as the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like criminal duo Jason and Lucia.
"Rockstar's Vice City is a masterpiece I never want to leave," PC Mag's Jordan Minor wrote in his review. "Grand Theft Auto VI is simply one of the best-looking video games I've ever seen."
He wasn't alone.
"Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable," declared IGN's Luke Reilly. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played."

  
 
  
 


 

 View this post on Instagram

 
 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 



Same for the Guardian's Keza MacDonald, who gave it a glowing review.
"In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen," MacDonald wrote, adding: "Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start."
Here's what other top gaming critics are saying about GTA VI.
Lucia and Jason in a scene from Grand Theft Auto VI.
Rockstar Games

Yussef Cole, the New York Times:

This is a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful.
The surprising depth to which these themes are explored makes for a memorable and endearing experience in Grand Theft Auto VI, which largely lives up to its sky-high expectations by inverting the series's reputation for destruction.

Zack Zwiezen, Kotaku:

The best part of Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't what I expected. It's not the crime, or the action, or the massive world to explore, though all of those parts are excellent and better than ever. The real standout of GTA 6, the part of the game that kept me hooked and which I won't forget anytime soon, is its central duo, Jason and Lucia.
Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstar's most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters.


  
 
  
 


 

 View this post on Instagram

 
 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 



Giovanni Colantonio, Polygon:

Through Jason and Lucia's genuine chemistry, GTA 6 gives you a better reason to work through Leonida's daily grind. Yes, there's always another bank to rob or car to steal, but that's not the reason you wake up in the morning. It's to prove that love can survive in a cruel culture that tries so hard to beat it out of people. So be it if you have to play dirty to keep pace with the cold-hearted crooks who make their fortune from someone else's pain. It shouldn't be this hard to settle down with your lover and enjoy a sunset together in the rotten social climate that Rockstar has been eager to lampoon for decades at this point.
People will hem and haw about Grand Theft Auto's purported glamorization of lawlessness. They always have; they always will. But it will be different this time. GTA 6's empathy is bound to be the most controversial thing about it.
Lucia and Jason in another scene from "Grand Theft Auto VI."
Rockstar Games

Kyle Orland, ArsTechnica:

The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you'd expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.
But it's the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.
Taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game's two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content. Grand Theft Auto VI never lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it's all the better for it.
Running from the law is, of course, part of "GTA 6."
Rockstar Games

Gene Park, The Washington Post:

After enough years of playing games, you know what to expect. You recognize the tricks, anticipate the limits and learn which doors will never open. Other games are still immensely entertaining, but you stop wondering.
"Grand Theft Auto VI" brings the wonder back. I wanted to speak to everyone, follow every street and open every door. My experience with games kept telling me where the possibilities could end. Then "GTA VI" would do something that would shock and delight. Writing about this game feels like sending dispatches from the future. I've been desperate to tell people what happened there, as if I've returned from a new life.

Tamoor Hussain, GameSpot:

Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realizing [of] such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutiae both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. 
GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I'd wager won't be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.


  
 
  
 


 

 View this post on Instagram

title: Ripple CEO Predicts Utility-Driven Crypto Will Win — Could XRP Be The Biggest Beneficiary?
description: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the cryptocurrency market is approaching a major turning point, where real-world utility could become more important than speculation. His latest comments come as institutional XRP infrastructure continues expanding, raising fresh questions about whether XRP could benefit from a more utility-driven market. Speaking with Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin at Singapore FinTech Festival […]
fullContent:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the cryptocurrency market is approaching a major turning point, where real-world utility could become more important than speculation. His latest comments come as institutional XRP infrastructure continues expanding, raising fresh questions about whether XRP could benefit from a more utility-driven market.

Speaking with Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin at Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 on November 19, Garlinghouse predicted that cryptocurrencies would increasingly diverge in performance as investors begin distinguishing between assets supported by genuine demand and those relying primarily on speculation.

The comments arrive during a challenging period for digital assets, with XRP struggling to reflect Ripple’s growing institutional presence in its market valuation.

However, a separate announcement involving the XRP Ledger could strengthen the argument that real-world adoption is becoming an increasingly important part of XRP’s long-term investment narrative.

Ripple CEO Predicts A Major Change In Crypto Markets

During his Bloomberg interview, Garlinghouse explained that cryptocurrencies have historically moved together, particularly during periods of market volatility.

He believes that relationship could gradually change.

According to the Ripple executive, assets with genuine financial applications and sustained demand may begin outperforming tokens whose value depends primarily on speculative trading.

Garlinghouse also acknowledged that 2026 has been difficult for the cryptocurrency market, pointing to capital moving toward major technology IPOs as one possible explanation for recent selling pressure.

Nevertheless, his longer-term outlook remains constructive.

The CEO argued that blockchain technology can improve financial transactions through faster and cheaper settlement, with applications extending beyond payments into tokenization, insurance, and other financial services.

For XRP, the distinction between utility and speculation is particularly important.

Although XRP was developed to facilitate efficient value transfers, its market performance remains heavily influenced by broader cryptocurrency sentiment.

The challenge is determining whether growing institutional use of Ripple’s infrastructure will eventually generate enough XRP-specific demand to influence the token’s valuation.

XRP Ledger Reaches An Important Institutional Milestone

Garlinghouse’s comments coincide with a significant development involving the XRP Ledger.

On November 18, the XRP Ledger Foundation announced that it had completed a self-attestation against the ten principles of the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

Blockchain security firm CertiK independently reviewed the Foundation’s responses under the framework’s Architecture and Resiliency principles.

The development makes XRPL the first public, permissionless Layer 1 blockchain to complete this particular independently verified assessment.

The framework covers areas including governance, settlement finality, operational resilience, cybersecurity, and institutional access.

These considerations are particularly important for banks and asset managers evaluating blockchain infrastructure for tokenized financial assets.

However, the assessment does not constitute regulatory approval, certification, or endorsement by GL1.

Ripple highlighted the milestone through its official X account, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure that financial institutions can evaluate against established standards.

The announcement reinforces the broader institutional narrative surrounding XRP Ledger, although independent verification of specific technical controls does not automatically translate into additional XRP demand.

Why Institutional Adoption Could Become XRP’s Biggest Advantage

Ripple’s growing institutional network provides another important element of Garlinghouse’s argument.

The company recently announced expanded relationships with major financial institutions, including BNY and Robinhood, involving payments, stablecoins, treasury services, and other blockchain-based financial applications.

Meanwhile, Bitcoinist recently reported that Aviva Investors expanded tokenization on XRPL, introducing a tokenized share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund.

These developments demonstrate how traditional financial institutions are increasingly exploring blockchain infrastructure for applications beyond cryptocurrency trading.

Yet an important distinction remains.

Ripple’s corporate expansion, XRP Ledger activity, and demand for XRP are related but separate measures.

A company using Ripple’s software or the RLUSD stablecoin does not necessarily need to acquire large quantities of XRP.

For institutional adoption to support XRP’s market valuation, investors would need evidence of increasing XRP-based settlement activity, liquidity demand, and broader network participation.

Could XRP Benefit From A Utility-Driven Crypto Market?

Garlinghouse’s prediction introduces an interesting possibility for XRP’s long-term investment outlook.

If investors increasingly prioritize digital assets with established financial applications, XRP could benefit from its role as a bridge asset and its connection to an expanding blockchain ecosystem.

Ripple has repeatedly emphasized that XRP remains central to its strategy, even as the company develops stablecoin infrastructure.

However, stablecoins also introduce competition in certain payment scenarios.

Dollar-denominated assets such as RLUSD can provide an alternative when financial institutions want to transfer stable value rather than use a volatile bridge asset.

The opportunity for XRP may therefore depend on whether its liquidity and settlement capabilities provide measurable advantages in specific cross-border payment corridors.

This is particularly relevant as financial institutions explore tokenized deposits, stablecoins, and other digital settlement mechanisms.

XRP Price Analysis: Can Utility Support A Recovery?

Despite Ripple’s expanding institutional relationships, XRP has faced significant selling pressure during November.

Recent market analysis highlighted the importance of the psychological $1 level, with the token struggling to establish a sustained recovery.

From a technical perspective, reclaiming $1 could improve short-term sentiment, but a convincing reversal would require stronger confirmation.

Investors should monitor whether XRP can establish higher lows, improve trading volume, and eventually reclaim its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

A sustained recovery above these indicators would suggest that buying pressure is strengthening.

Conversely, continued weakness below major moving averages would indicate that broader market conditions remain an obstacle.

As Bitcoinist previously examined in its coverage of institutional XRP liquidity, expanding financial infrastructure may create opportunities for the ecosystem without guaranteeing an immediate increase in token prices.

For now, the most constructive scenario would involve improving technical momentum alongside measurable growth in XRP-based transactions.

What Comes Next For Ripple And XRP?

Garlinghouse’s latest comments highlight an important question facing the cryptocurrency industry: will investors continue valuing digital assets primarily through speculation, or will measurable adoption become increasingly important?

Ripple’s expanding institutional relationships and the XRP Ledger’s latest infrastructure assessment suggest that the company is positioning itself for a more utility-focused market.

However, the long-term implications for XRP will depend on actual transaction demand, liquidity, and the extent to which institutional applications require the token.

If cryptocurrencies begin diverging according to their real-world usefulness, XRP’s ability to convert institutional adoption into sustained token demand could become one of the market’s most important developments to watch.
