title: Hill Republicans want to finish the year with a bang. It could be a whimper.
description:
Republicans want to run through the tape in their final weeks in power on Capitol Hill, but they're hitting some major hurdles.
With 17 working days left in the Senate before Democrats take charge, Republicans emerged from hours of meetings Wednesday without a clear path to advance a party-line spending bill the White House desperately wants — just as several of President Donald Trump's nominees hit snags that threaten to keep key roles filled by acting officials for two years.
House Republicans, meanwhile, are simply spinning their wheels. Leaders announced Wednesday they would cut their workweek short because of attendance issues.
It's left some GOP lawmakers openly wondering what their party will get done before the end of the year beyond seating more Trump-appointed judges and, they hope, averting a government shutdown. The Senate is aiming to pass a bipartisan permitting reform bill this week, but it faces a more uncertain path in the House, which is also sitting on a bipartisan college sports bill the Senate passed months ago.
"I don't know if we're going to do anything," Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said after emerging from one of the Senate GOP's closed-door meetings Wednesday. "I think we're going to continue to confirm judges, I'm pretty sure of that. But everything else, I have no idea what we're going to do."
Across the Capitol, one House Republican granted anonymity to speak candidly said there are "very low odds" Republicans will be able to enact any bill through the filibuster-skirting reconciliation process — especially given how many members have stopped coming to work after bruising election defeats.
"It's dereliction of duty," the Republican said, adding leaders would need to "publicly shame" colleagues "by name" into showing up.
The reality check comes as House and Senate Republicans have been under renewed pressure from the White House to use the waning days of their governing trifecta to ram through a swath of stalled GOP priorities.

Republicans want to run through the tape in their final weeks in power on Capitol Hill, but they're hitting some major hurdles.

With 17 working days left in the Senate before Democrats take charge, Republicans emerged from hours of meetings Wednesday without a clear path to advance a party-line spending bill the White House desperately wants — just as several of President Donald Trump's nominees hit snags that threaten to keep key roles filled by acting officials for two years.

House Republicans, meanwhile, are simply spinning their wheels. Leaders announced Wednesday they would cut their workweek short because of attendance issues.

It's left some GOP lawmakers openly wondering what their party will get done before the end of the year beyond seating more Trump-appointed judges and, they hope, averting a government shutdown. The Senate is aiming to pass a bipartisan permitting reform bill this week, but it faces a more uncertain path in the House, which is also sitting on a bipartisan college sports bill the Senate passed months ago.

"I don't know if we're going to do anything," Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said after emerging from one of the Senate GOP's closed-door meetings Wednesday. "I think we're going to continue to confirm judges, I'm pretty sure of that. But everything else, I have no idea what we're going to do."

Across the Capitol, one House Republican granted anonymity to speak candidly said there are "very low odds" Republicans will be able to enact any bill through the filibuster-skirting reconciliation process — especially given how many members have stopped coming to work after bruising election defeats.

"It's dereliction of duty," the Republican said, adding leaders would need to "publicly shame" colleagues "by name" into showing up.

The reality check comes as House and Senate Republicans have been under renewed pressure from the White House to use the waning days of their governing trifecta to ram through a swath of stalled GOP priorities.

But many GOP senators, while publicly supportive, have long been privately skeptical it will come together. For one thing, Republicans still haven't fully agreed on the scope of the hypothetical measure — $350 billion is more than many budget hawks can stomach.

For another, the Senate math gets harder for the GOP next month when incoming Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown of Ohio is sworn in after winning a special election to finish out the term of Vice President JD Vance, lowering the GOP's majority to 52.

"Everybody recognizes it's going to be a herculean effort to try to get the House and the Senate to agree on the scope and the process," Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) said Wednesday.

Besides the GOP-only bill, legislators also need to worry about advancing three other typically bipartisan year-end staples: the annual defense policy bill, the farm bill and a measure to fund the government past a looming Dec. 11 funding deadline.

GOP appropriators made the case during their closed-door meeting Wednesday to hold off on reconciliation for now to allow government funding negotiations to proceed, several senators said after the meeting. Senate Majority Leader John Thune confirmed as much but declined to say how much time Republicans would give the bipartisan government funding talks.

Republican senators are also discussing whether to bring a spending package to the floor that would combine two fiscal 2027 bills: one funding veterans affairs and another funding the Pentagon, according to three GOP senators and aides granted anonymity to describe private conversations.

But Democratic votes will be needed to make this tactic work — and Democrats are not likely to support bankrolling the Pentagon without Iran restrictions and a guarantee that nondefense programs would get a funding increase, too.

Sen. John Hoeven (R-N.D.) said it would put Democrats on the spot: "Are they willing to work with us or not? And this makes them answer that question."

Republicans are having success confirming Trump's judicial nominees, with some vowing not to leave town this week until they have cleared a batch that has been teed up for votes. But some of the president's other nominees are facing less certain prospects.

Committees have until Dec. 1 to advance any nominee they want to have included in a bloc of Trump picks set to be confirmed en masse next month. But there are signs of GOP pushback against the nominations of Eric Ueland to head the Government Accountability Office and Kari Lake to be ambassador to Jamaica, among others, that could keep them out of the package.

The White House also surprised senators by pulling Heidi Overton to lead the FDA, and HELP Chair Bill Cassidy (R-La.) declined to move forward with a top science nominee who was supposed to get a committee vote.

Republican leaders were also struggling to get things done in the House this week, with leaders unable to begin floor debate on two GOP-sponsored bills after 14 House Republicans didn't show up to vote Wednesday. Eleven were nonreturning members.

Those attendance problems aren't expected to get better: Outgoing House members had to vacate their offices and relocate to cubicles this week, further demoralizing defeated GOP incumbents who would just as soon close out their terms back home.

The upshot is that House GOP leaders are unlikely to have the votes to adopt any reconciliation measure that comes over from the Senate. Most House Republicans wanted the Senate to take up a framework they passed before the midterms instead.

title: Binance Hacker Moves Another $248M of Ethereum as the Exchange Pockets $6.5B Court Order
description:

The post Binance Hacker Moves Another $248M of Ethereum as the Exchange Pockets $6.5B Court Order appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
Binance hacker has moved another $248 million in Ethereum as the exchange secures a major legal victory against the attackers. Blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that 137,602 ETH moved across multiple wallets today, extending a three-day distribution spree.

The latest transfers bring the total moved since November 17 to nearly 291,000 ETH, worth more than $500 million. The activity comes as Binance pursues a worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) courts.

The court order covers $6.5 billion in stolen assets and targets unidentified individuals behind the October 29 breach. Binance now has a legal route to pursue frozen funds, but the attackers are still shifting hundreds of millions through Ethereum wallets.

Market Cap

Binance Pockets $6.5B Court Order as Hackers Keep Moving Funds

Binance secured the worldwide freezing injunction yesterday, giving its recovery operation a significant legal boost. The ADGM Court also issued separate orders covering specific stolen assets held by third parties.

Eighteen crypto companies must maintain existing freezes and cannot lend, swap, or mix the affected tokens. They include Circle and World Liberty Financial, neither of which faces allegations of wrongdoing.

JUST IN: Binance says it secured a court order in Abu Dhabi to help recover crypto frozen after last month’s $6.3 billion hack, per Reuters.

Binance previously said third parties had frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion, roughly 45% of the stolen crypto.

The court order… pic.twitter.com/Dx4wI7jlI5

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) November 18, 2026

Binance’s lawyers have identified 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets. The exchange says around $2.85 billion has already been frozen or intercepted, or 45% of the original theft.

Tether has separately frozen $1.5 billion linked to the attack. Although the stablecoin issuer was not named in the court order, it is working directly with Binance on returning the funds.

The legal offensive comes as Binance tries to recover assets that investigators have traced across multiple blockchains. The exchange has already reimbursed affected customers and covered the financial loss. This leaves billions worth of crypto still moving through wallets controlled by the attackers.

DISCOVER: 15+ Best Crypto IPO to Watch in 2026

Binance Hacker’s Ethereum Transfers Reach Nearly 291,000 ETH in Three Days

The movement involved 12 transfers to 12 separate recipient addresses. Eleven transactions carried 12,000 ETH each, while the final transfer contained 5,602 ETH.

The transfers followed two large movements earlier this week. Hack-linked wallets redistributed 74,880 ETH on November 17 and another 78,415 ETH on November 18.

Combined, the three batches account for approximately 290,898 ETH. The latest $248.23 million transfer represents the largest daily movement identified during this period.

The Binance hacker has moved another 137,602 $ETH ($248.23M) for laundering.https://t.co/jKWvcOSJCB pic.twitter.com/ZcIoZLlAhA

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 19, 2026

The FBI attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor operation. Its October 31 alert identified Ethereum addresses operated by or closely connected to the attackers.

Some of the earlier transfers have already entered Bitcoin. Blockchain intelligence firm Elliptic identified 2,100 ETH converted into BTC from the November 17 movement. Much of that Bitcoin subsequently entered CoinJoin transactions, which complicate transaction tracing.

The latest batch consisted of wallet-to-wallet transfers. Splitting the funds across new addresses gives investigators more wallets to track as the laundering operation progresses.

Binance’s legal team is building a constantly updated list of suspect addresses. The court orders can be served through blockchain transactions, allowing exchanges and other service providers to identify affected funds.

The next major milestone arrives on December 1, when the ADGM Court will consider if the proprietary injunction should continue. Meanwhile, every new transfer gives investigators another opportunity to identify where the stolen Ethereum goes.

title: PayPal’s Stablecoin Users Can Disappear Inside Custody
description:
Key Takeaways Only 2% of PYUSD sits in small wallets Paxos custody holds $789M for customers and partners Lending and […]
The post PayPal’s Stablecoin Users Can Disappear Inside Custody appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Only 2% of PYUSD sits in small wallets
  • Paxos custody holds $789M for customers and partners
  • Lending and yield products account for 28%
  • Checkout payments settle to merchants in dollars

Bitquery’s holder investigation, published November 19 with balances verified a day earlier, traced $2.33 billion of the token’s roughly $2.46 billion supply across Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum and Polygon.

Where the $2.33 Billion Sits

Bitquery sorted every measured balance into nine categories. The one closest to everyday users, unlabelled wallets holding less than $1 million, accounts for $49 million.

Measured PYUSD supply by holder type

Paxos custody $789M · 34%
DeFi lending $493M · 21%
Unlabelled wallets, $1M+$313M · 13%
Trading firms $268M · 12%
Yield products $159M · 7%
Exchanges $140M · 6%
Trading pools $83M · 4%
Ordinary wallets, under $1M$49M · 2%
Bridges $35M · 1%

Source: Bitquery. Balances verified November 18, 2026, on Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum and Polygon. Shares are rounded.

The $1 million cutoff decides a great deal. An unlabelled wallet holding $1.2 million falls into a bucket more than six times larger than the ordinary category, while a $900,000 wallet run by a small fund still counts as ordinary. Bitquery assigns labels from known addresses and from how wallets transact with each other, so its categories describe on-chain behaviour rather than verified identities.

The snapshot also runs on two clocks. Ethereum balances were read at midnight UTC on November 18 and Solana balances at 16:21 UTC, so tokens bridged between those chains in the gap could be counted twice or missed. The shares are close approximations of a supply that kept moving during the measurement.

One Custody Bucket, Many Possible Owners

Paxos Trust Company issues PYUSD for PayPal, and its custody wallets hold $789 million, the largest single category. Bitquery says those wallets keep coins for Paxos’s customers and partners, including people who hold PYUSD inside an app, and that the chain does not show which coins belong to PayPal or Venmo users.

PayPal’s own setup explains the blind spot. Its US cryptocurrency terms say it combines customers’ crypto in omnibus accounts, meaning pooled accounts that hold assets for many customers at once, directly or through a service provider, and keeps a separate record of each customer’s interest. Under those terms, customers do not own specific tokens, and the PYUSD balance shown in the app is not tied to a particular blockchain.

Take a hypothetical pool of 1,000 customers holding 100 PYUSD each. The provider’s books show 1,000 owners and 100,000 tokens. On-chain, the same money could sit in a handful of addresses, and a holder chart would file all of it under custody.

Bitquery did find one trace of the people behind the pool. Over the past year, Paxos custody sent payments to 141,617 unlabelled Ethereum wallets, and 68% of those payments were under $100. Bitquery reads the pattern as users moving coins out of apps, while noting that the chain does not show who requested each transfer. One person can control several receiving wallets, so the number is no user count, but it shows small-ticket withdrawals leaving custody at scale.

Lending Protocols Hold 14 Times More Than Small Wallets

DeFi lending and yield products together hold 28% of measured supply. On Ethereum, Spark holds $304 million, Morpho $103 million and Maple $65 million. Bitquery says these protocols lend PYUSD out or use it to back other dollar tokens. On Arbitrum, a single protocol, USD.AI, holds roughly four in five of the coins on that chain.

Trading follows the same pattern. Bitquery found that 95% of Ethereum PYUSD trading over the past year was against USDS, the dollar token of the Sky ecosystem that includes Spark, and was concentrated in a few pools. The firm describes this as money moving between two DeFi systems and says buyers acquiring the coin to spend make up a small part of it.

A lending contract is another pooled holder. The address belongs to the protocol, while the economic interest belongs to depositors and borrowers the balance never names. The 28% shows where PYUSD earns a return, and the number of depositors behind it stays off the chart.

READ MORE:

Ant, DBS Use Blockchain Cash to Buy Tokenized Funds

Checkout Payments End in Dollars

Payments leave even fewer marks. Under PayPal’s Pay with Crypto terms, a shopper at an eligible merchant is connected to Mesh Connect, a third-party provider that acts on the shopper’s instructions. Mesh moves PYUSD from the shopper’s wallet to PayPal, first converting another supported cryptocurrency into PYUSD if needed.

After risk and compliance checks, PayPal converts the PYUSD to US dollars at $1.00 per token and credits the merchant’s business balance, net of fees. Refunds run the other way: the merchant enters the amount in dollars, and PayPal sends PYUSD back to the shopper’s wallet.

The merchant never holds the token, so a snapshot taken after the sale shows no PYUSD on the business side. A company that keeps stablecoins as working capital would appear on-chain, and one using PayPal’s checkout would not, even if both serve the same customers. The terms set out the mechanics but give no figure for how often the route is used. Coindoo’s guide to how crypto payments reach merchants covers the wider settlement process.

What a User Count Would Require

PYUSD has been available in 70 markets since PayPal’s March expansion, which describes how far the product reaches. Measuring how many people use it takes records that only PayPal and Paxos hold.

Who holds it?

Deduplicated account records, with the apps and regions they cover stated

Who pays with it?

Completed checkouts, separated from withdrawals and wallet-to-wallet transfers

Who comes back?

Repeat-payment cohorts tracked over fixed periods

Even provider numbers would need definitions. An account with a few cents left over is not an active payer, and someone who pays monthly may hold nothing on the day of a snapshot. Counting both as users would blur the behaviour an adoption figure is meant to capture.

On the evidence available, the 2% figure supports neither a weak nor a strong reading of PayPal’s retail audience. Small wallets hold little, yet custody has paid out to more than 140,000 wallets in mostly small amounts, and checkout leaves no balance behind. Paxos already publishes reserve reports and attestations on what backs PYUSD. Comparable figures on funded accounts and completed payments would answer the question a wallet chart cannot.

title: My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
description: Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 19th November 2026, Chainwire
fullContent:
[PRESS RELEASE – Dubai, United Arab Emirates, November 19th, 2026]

My Wallet users can now receive a different stablecoin on another blockchain at a fixed 1:1 token rate on eligible routes, with no spread, slippage or swap fee charged by the wallet

My Wallet, a self-custodial, open-source crypto wallet serving more than 10 million users, has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe and USDS across supported blockchains. On eligible routes, users can switch both stablecoins and networks within a single in-app flow, with the amount they will receive fixed before confirmation.

The launch follows My Wallet’s listing at the top of WalletConnect’s WalletGuide. The wallet is also WalletConnect Certified and connects users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Simplifying Stablecoin Transfers Across Blockchains

According to research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research, organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins operate across multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction when users need a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right network, users may still hold the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade or application.

My Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator, powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges resulting in the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet is the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

How the 1:1 Stablecoin Swaps Work

The fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether users switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another blockchain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same rate applies when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

The 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes. There is no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination token amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may have different rates and fees.

“Stablecoins are supposed to make moving money simpler, but users still have to think about which token they hold and which blockchain it’s on,” said Alexander Zinchuk, founder of My Wallet. “We’re removing that friction. If you hold USDT and need USDC on another network, you should be able to make that change in one step, know exactly how many tokens you’ll receive, and not pay an additional swap commission to your wallet.”

Native Bitcoin and Gasless EVM Transfers

The stablecoin launch follows the introduction of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Users can hold, send, receive and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON and other networks, as well as buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

My Wallet now supports gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Optimism, adding to the existing support on Solana and TON. For these EVM transfers, the network fee is deducted from the tokens being sent, so users do not need to acquire a separate native token for gas. Supported assets are USDC on all five EVM networks, USDT on Ethereum and BNB Chain, bridged USDT on Base and Optimism, and USDT0 on Arbitrum. There is no minimum transfer amount or daily limit on the number of transactions.

Together, these innovative features advance My Wallet’s broader “All You Need to Enjoy Crypto” vision, combining asset management, seamless trading, and ease of use into one self-custodial app.

The new features are already available in My Wallet. Swap availability is subject to the selected assets, networks and routes.

About My Wallet

My Wallet is a self-custodial, open-source multichain wallet for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Hyperliquid, TON, TRON, BNB, Base, Robinhood, Monad, Arbitrum, Polygon, and more. Founded in 2022, My Wallet serves over 10 million users across mobile, desktop, web and its Telegram Mini App. The wallet has been audited by CertiK and ranks among the top-5 wallets on CertiK’s Wallet Leaderboard.

My Wallet is WalletConnect Certified and currently listed 1st in WalletConnect’s WalletGuide, connecting users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Staking inside My Wallet is powered by Stakee, its own staking protocol, ranked among the top-2 TON DeFi protocols by TVL on DefiLlama.

For more details, users can visit mywallet.io and try My Wallet at mywallet.io/get.

Join the community on Telegram, X, and Discord.

fullContent:
Solana is attracting fresh attention from traditional finance after Zelle, one of America’s largest payment networks, demonstrated a $1.25 million confidential stablecoin transfer on the blockchain. The development adds another layer to the growing discussion around Solana’s institutional adoption, particularly as financial companies explore blockchain infrastructure for international payments.

The demonstration took place during Solana Breakpoint 2026 in London, where Zelle showcased its ZelleUSD (ZLUSD) stablecoin and confirmed plans to use Solana for cross-border transactions.

Although the demonstration did not involve a live production payment, it highlighted an important development: major financial institutions are increasingly exploring public blockchains for payment infrastructure.

For SOL investors, the bigger question is whether growing institutional adoption could eventually translate into stronger network demand and a sustainable price recovery.

Zelle Brings A $1.25 Million Payment Demonstration To Solana

According to the Solana Foundation’s official announcement, Zelle completed its first confidential transfer using ZelleUSD during the Breakpoint conference.

The transaction demonstrated how financial institutions could transfer tokenized dollars while keeping sensitive transaction information private.

The demonstration reportedly used Solana’s Token-2022 confidential transfer functionality, which allows token amounts to remain encrypted while transactions are verified.

This distinction is particularly important for banks, which must balance payment transparency with customer confidentiality and regulatory requirements.

Solana’s official X account highlighted the demonstration, emphasizing Zelle’s ambitions to expand internationally.

However, the demonstration was conducted on Solana’s development network rather than its production mainnet. It therefore represents a technical milestone, not evidence that ZelleUSD is already processing live consumer payments.

Why Zelle’s Decision Could Matter For SOL

Zelle’s interest in Solana could have implications beyond a single stablecoin transfer.

The payment network processed more than $1.2 trillion in domestic transactions in 2025, making it one of the largest payment platforms in the United States.

Even a relatively small portion of future international payment activity moving onto Solana could create additional transaction demand.

However, this does not mean Zelle’s existing payment volume will automatically migrate to the blockchain.

The more important factor is whether Solana can attract sustained activity from financial institutions, stablecoin issuers, and payment providers.

The trend is already becoming visible across the industry. As Bitcoinist previously reported, Polygon expanded its payments infrastructure to Solana, allowing businesses to access banking services, stablecoin transfers, and global payouts through integrated systems.

For SOL holders, network adoption matters because transactions require fees paid in SOL, while broader ecosystem growth could increase demand for blockchain infrastructure.

Still, Solana’s low transaction fees mean that large payment volumes do not necessarily translate into equally large token demand.

Can Institutional Adoption Help Solana Recover?

The announcement arrives during a challenging period for SOL, with cryptocurrency markets experiencing renewed volatility.

However, price weakness and improving network fundamentals can occur simultaneously.

Solana’s growing involvement in payment infrastructure suggests that institutional interest may continue developing even when speculative trading activity slows.

The key question is whether investors will eventually begin pricing in this expanding real-world utility.

Recent market developments provide an interesting comparison. Bitcoinist’s analysis of Solana’s recovery toward $80 highlighted the importance of buyers defending support near $68–$70 while attempting to reclaim higher resistance levels.

A stronger recovery would likely require improving overall cryptocurrency market conditions, sustained stablecoin growth, and evidence that institutional partnerships are generating meaningful on-chain activity.

From a technical perspective, investors should watch whether SOL can establish a higher low, reclaim important moving averages, and demonstrate improving momentum.

A sustained move above the 50-day moving average could provide an early indication of strengthening short-term momentum. However, a more convincing trend reversal would require broader confirmation, including stronger trading volume and improving market structure.

Until those signals appear, institutional announcements should be viewed as potential long-term catalysts rather than guarantees of immediate price appreciation.

What Comes Next For Solana And ZelleUSD?

Zelle’s international expansion plans could provide an important test of Solana’s ability to support financial applications beyond cryptocurrency trading.

The company’s initial cross-border ambitions include payments between the United States and India, although the exact timing and availability of live Solana-based transfers remain uncertain.

If successful, the initiative could encourage additional payment companies to explore similar infrastructure.

For Solana, the opportunity extends beyond the $1.25 million demonstration itself.

The real significance lies in whether major financial institutions begin using the blockchain consistently for payments, settlement, and tokenized financial products.

While SOL’s short-term performance will continue depending on broader market conditions, developments such as ZelleUSD suggest that Solana’s long-term adoption story is still evolving.

And if institutional payment activity begins translating into measurable network growth, the market may eventually have another reason to reassess SOL’s valuation.

title: Bitcoin’s 28% Decline Before Anthropic IPO Mirrors Pre-SpaceX Crash: Here’s What Happened Next
description: The latest Bitcoin sell-off has revived comparisons with June, when BTC recovered from around $59,000 following a similar pre-IPO decline.
fullContent:
Bitcoin (BTC) has fallen by approximately 28% from its September peak ahead of Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut on November 19.

That is an almost identical dip the OG crypto recorded around the time of the SpaceX IPO in June, and given that it then went on a run that took it above $80,000, some market watchers are wondering whether the same can happen again.

Bitcoin Repeats Its Pre-SpaceX Decline Ahead of Anthropic IPO

The comparisons were made in a November 19 post on X by CryptosRus, who shared a chart measuring peak-to-trough losses across the weeks before each company’s stock market debut.

It showed that before SpaceX went public around June 12, BTC’s price had dropped by almost 29% from a peak close to $83,000 in early May to near $59,000 in the first week of June. After that, the asset made a recovery, eventually going as high as  $87,000 in September.

Something similar is also happening ahead of the Anthropic listing. After Bitcoin went to $87,400 on September 21, it started a steady decline that has it changing hands just above $63,000 at the time of writing, representing a drawdown of nearly 28% across 8 weeks.

“Same setup, same opportunity,” CryptosRus wrote, suggesting that the earlier recovery could offer a reference point for the current market.

That BTC drop near $63,000 triggered liquidations approaching $500 million, with positions worth more than $100 million wiped out in one hour.

Data from CoinGecko shows the asset is nearly 2% lower than 24 hours ago, with the losses stretching to just over 14% across seven days and 21% in the last two weeks. In the previous month, the number one cryptocurrency has seen its price drop by almost 23%, while the plunge year-on-year stands at around 30%.

The timing of the asset’s weakness and the Anthropic IPO prompted speculation that investors may have been moving their capital into AI companies.

Anthropic Bags $81 Billion

Anthropic has now raised $81.3 billion through the sale of 980 million Class A common shares, giving it a $1.5 trillion valuation. That’s a fair few bucks above its original target range, reported to have been around $1.4 trillion, from selling at least 825 million shares at between $70 and $78.

For comparison, SpaceX raised about $75 billion from its own event, which involved the sale of 555.56 million shares and valued the company at $1.77 trillion.

That investor interest in Anthropic also extended to tokenized exposure, with an IPO token sale by Binance Wallet reportedly reaching its $500 million subscription cap in just four hours. That forced the exchange to close subscriptions early, with unsuccessful applicants set to receive a refund.

title: Solana Tokenized Stock Hits $1.2B as Wall Street Moves Equities Onchain
description:
Solana tokenized stock reaches $1.22 billion as Ondo, xStocks and DTCC expand blockchain-based equity infrastructure.
The post Solana Tokenized Stock Hits $1.2B as Wall Street Moves Equities Onchain appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Solana (SOL)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Solana’s tokenized stock market has reached $1.22 billion in circulating value, nearly doubling in less than a month as demand for blockchain-based equities accelerates.

Growth has been driven by platforms including Ondo Finance, xStocks and Backpack Securities, which are bringing exposure to major US companies onto Solana. Apple, Nvidia, Tesla and other household names are increasingly appearing in crypto wallets and decentralized trading platforms.

The expansion is also attracting traditional financial infrastructure. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) plans to connect its tokenization service to Solana in 2027, potentially opening another route for established securities to enter blockchain markets.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Ondo and xStocks Push Solana Tokenized Equities Beyond $1 Billion

Ondo Finance has become one of the biggest contributors to Solana’s tokenized stock market. The platform brought more than 200 tokenized US stocks and ETFs to the network in January, covering companies such as Nvidia, Apple, and Meta.

Its expansion has continued through additional trading and wallet integrations. According to the Solana Foundation’s October ecosystem report, Ondo’s tokenized assets on Solana surpassed $500 million.

Meanwhile, xStocks has accumulated $7.5 billion in trading volume on Solana, while Backpack Securities has processed more than $6 billion in tokenized asset trading volume.

Securitize is also expanding its presence. The company added 13 US equities to its Solana-based offering on November 2, bringing its total catalogue to 25 stocks. Its products include shares in Exxon Mobil, Disney, Salesforce, and GameStop. Unlike purely synthetic products, Securitize says its tokens are backed one-to-one by underlying shares and provide security entitlements with applicable economic and ownership rights.

DTCC Brings Solana Closer to Traditional Financial Markets

The biggest institutional development came on November 12, when DTCC announced plans to connect its Tokenization Service to Solana during the second half of 2027. The integration would allow eligible securities held through its Depository Trust Company subsidiary to become available in tokenized form on Solana.

DTCC is one of the most important pieces of infrastructure in US financial markets. Its subsidiaries processed $4.7 quadrillion in securities transactions during 2025, while its depository provided custody and asset servicing for $114 trillion in securities.

The initial tokenization service launched on October 28, with support for Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network. Solana will become another destination as the company expands its blockchain integrations.

Twenty financial institutions signed agreements to access the service at launch, including JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, Morgan Stanley and UBS. DTCC says tokenized securities distributed through its service will retain the ownership rights, investor protections and regulatory safeguards associated with traditionally held securities.

This gives Solana a potential connection to established securities infrastructure rather than relying exclusively on crypto-native issuers and trading platforms. But the integration is still planned for 2027.

As of now, the $1.22 billion milestone reflects a relatively small market compared with traditional equities. But the combination of expanding stock offerings, billions in cumulative trading activity, and growing institutional involvement suggests tokenization is becoming a more serious part of Solana’s financial ecosystem.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Bitcoin Hyper Eyes Solana Tokenized Stock Boom With Bitcoin Liquidity

Solana is attracting billions in tokenized stock trading, but Bitcoin Hyper is betting that the next opportunity lies in bringing Bitcoin liquidity into a faster, more flexible blockchain environment.

Bitcoin Hyper ($HYPER) is developing a Bitcoin Layer 2 powered by the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM). The architecture aims to combine Bitcoin’s enormous liquidity base with the speed and programmability associated with Solana.

Users will be able to bridge BTC into the Layer 2, where they can access faster transactions, decentralized exchanges, staking, and other DeFi applications. Its design also uses zero-knowledge proofs and periodic state commitments to Bitcoin for settlement.

That combination could open an interesting route for tokenized financial markets. Solana has already demonstrated demand for bringing traditional equities onchain. Bitcoin Hyper is targeting a different pool of capital: Bitcoin holders who want access to applications beyond simply holding BTC.

The project has already attracted more than $33 million during its presale, while its testnet infrastructure is taking shape. Its wallet, explorer, faucet, and testnet bridge are among the components being rolled out ahead of the next development phase.

The HYPER token currently costs just $0.0136, with presale staking offering an advertised 35% APY. That yield gives early participants another incentive to hold their tokens while the network develops. For comparison, conventional SOL staking yields are considerably lower than that offered by the presale rate. Bitcoin Hyper is using staking rewards to attract early participation before its wider ecosystem goes live.

The fundraising milestone also puts the project on a defined timeline. Bitcoin Hyper’s presale is scheduled to conclude on November 26, leaving buyers with a shrinking window before the next stage.

Gain Access to New Bitcoin Layer 2 Early Before the Presale Window Ends In Less Than 2 Weeks

title: Bitcoin Staking Could Be Replaced By A New Lending Model — Here’s What It Means For BTC
description: Bitcoin could be approaching an important turning point in decentralized finance as Babylon, one of the largest Bitcoin staking protocols, considers replacing its existing staking model with a new system built around Bitcoin-backed lending. The development comes as institutional Bitcoin lending continues gaining attention across traditional financial markets. The proposal comes from Babylon co-founder Fisher […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin could be approaching an important turning point in decentralized finance as Babylon, one of the largest Bitcoin staking protocols, considers replacing its existing staking model with a new system built around Bitcoin-backed lending. The development comes as institutional Bitcoin lending continues gaining attention across traditional financial markets.

The proposal comes from Babylon co-founder Fisher Yu, who suggested ending Bitcoin staking before the end of 2026 to concentrate on Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV). The new infrastructure would allow BTC holders to borrow stablecoins without selling their Bitcoin, wrapping it, or transferring custody to a centralized intermediary.

The development raises an interesting question: Could borrowing against Bitcoin become more attractive than earning staking rewards?

Why Babylon Wants To Move Beyond Bitcoin Staking

In a November 17 governance proposal, Fisher Yu explained that Babylon’s next phase could focus on making native Bitcoin more useful across decentralized financial applications.

The proposal follows Aave’s November 9 governance approval of an initial plan to support Bitcoin collateral through Babylon’s Trustless Bitcoin Vaults.

Under the proposed transition, Babylon would discontinue new Bitcoin staking registrations, reduce staking rewards to zero, and disable staking finality. Existing participants would retain the ability to withdraw their BTC under the protocol’s established rules.

Yu also suggested reducing BABY token inflation from 5.5% to 2%, potentially changing the project’s long-term token economics.

However, the proposal remains under discussion. No final governance vote or implementation date has been announced.

Could Bitcoin-Backed Lending Change Investor Behavior?

The most interesting aspect of Babylon’s proposal is how it could change the way long-term Bitcoin holders access liquidity.

Traditionally, investors looking to raise capital from their Bitcoin holdings have faced several choices: sell BTC, borrow through a centralized lender, or use wrapped Bitcoin in decentralized lending protocols.

Babylon’s proposed system introduces another possibility.

Through Trustless Bitcoin Vaults, users would lock native BTC on the Bitcoin blockchain while borrowing assets such as USDC or USDT through Aave V4.

Unlike traditional wrapped Bitcoin lending, the underlying BTC would remain on its original blockchain.

The approach resembles other developments in decentralized finance, including Aave’s Bitcoin collateral proposal, which explores allowing institutions to borrow against Bitcoin held with regulated custodians.

This could become particularly attractive to long-term investors who believe Bitcoin will appreciate but still need access to capital.

Instead of selling their holdings, they could potentially borrow against them while maintaining exposure to Bitcoin’s future price movements.

Nevertheless, borrowing introduces interest costs and liquidation risk. If Bitcoin falls significantly, borrowers may need to add collateral or repay debt to avoid losing their positions.

What Happens To The Bitcoin Already Staked?

Babylon currently has approximately 41,000 BTC committed to its staking infrastructure, representing billions of dollars in Bitcoin.

The proposed transition would not automatically transfer those holdings into lending vaults.

Instead, participants could withdraw their Bitcoin under existing rules and independently decide whether to use the new lending applications.

That distinction matters because a successful transition would depend on how many existing stakers actually choose to become borrowers.

What This Could Mean For Bitcoin’s Long-Term Demand

From a broader market perspective, the potential transition represents another step toward expanding Bitcoin’s financial utility.

Bitcoin has traditionally been viewed primarily as a store of value. However, developments in collateralized lending are creating additional ways to use BTC without immediately selling it.

Similar developments are already emerging across blockchain ecosystems, with projects such as Sui’s Hashi Bitcoin lending initiative exploring how Bitcoin can support new financial applications.

If more investors begin using Bitcoin as collateral, it could encourage longer holding periods among participants who would otherwise sell assets to access liquidity.

The effect would not necessarily be immediate. Borrowing demand, interest rates, security, and liquidation conditions would all influence adoption.

There is also an important distinction between locking Bitcoin as collateral and permanently removing it from circulation. Collateral can eventually be released or liquidated, meaning lending activity does not automatically reduce market supply.

Still, the development highlights a potentially significant evolution in Bitcoin’s role within decentralized finance.

With Babylon targeting a restricted launch in late 2026 and broader access expected in early 2027, the coming months could reveal whether native Bitcoin-backed lending becomes a meaningful alternative to traditional staking.

For long-term Bitcoin supporters, the bigger story may be that BTC is gradually becoming more than an asset investors simply buy and hold.

title: My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
description: My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
fullContent:
Dubai, United Arab Emirates, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

My Wallet users can now receive a different stablecoin on another blockchain at a fixed 1:1 token rate on eligible routes, with no spread, slippage or swap fee charged by the wallet

My Wallet, a self-custodial, open-source crypto wallet serving more than 10 million users, has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe and USDS across supported blockchains. On eligible routes, users can switch both stablecoins and networks within a single in-app flow, with the amount they will receive fixed before confirmation. 

The launch follows My Wallet’s listing at the top of WalletConnect’s WalletGuide. The wallet is also WalletConnect Certified and connects users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Simplifying Stablecoin Transfers Across Blockchains

According to research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research, organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins operate across multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction when users need a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right network, users may still hold the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade or application.

My Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator, powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges resulting in the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet is the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

How the 1:1 Stablecoin Swaps Work

The fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether users switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another blockchain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same rate applies when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

The 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes. There is no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination token amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may have different rates and fees.

“Stablecoins are supposed to make moving money simpler, but users still have to think about which token they hold and which blockchain it’s on,” said Alexander Zinchuk, founder of My Wallet. “We’re removing that friction. If you hold USDT and need USDC on another network, you should be able to make that change in one step, know exactly how many tokens you’ll receive, and not pay an additional swap commission to your wallet.”

Native Bitcoin and Gasless EVM Transfers

The stablecoin launch follows the introduction of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Users can hold, send, receive and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON and other networks, as well as buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

My Wallet now supports gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Optimism, adding to the existing support on Solana and TON. title: LIVE – Bitcoin Price, Gold and Oil Fall: Should the US Repeat Its $2.2T 2020 Rescue?
description:
Bitcoin price, gold and oil fall as hawkish Fed minutes fuel rate hike fears. Should Washington repeat its $2.2T rescue from 2020?
The post LIVE – Bitcoin Price, Gold and Oil Fall: Should the US Repeat Its $2.2T 2020 Rescue? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Bitcoin price is getting hammered in the aftermath of the FOMC minutes. Gold isn’t doing much better; oil and stocks have joined the sell-off. The markets are already nervous about the Federal Reserve’s next decision, and yesterday’s FOMC minutes gave us another reason to worry: policymakers are still talking about raising interest rates.

Almost all officials saw further hikes as appropriate under their baseline outlook. Two even floated the possibility of a bigger increase if inflation refuses to cool.

This is a nasty combination for markets. Bitcoin fell around 3.2% over 24 hours, gold futures dropped more than 3%, and WTI crude lost around 3%. The dollar climbed to a 19-month high. Wall Street was mixed, though, with the Nasdaq finishing higher while the Dow and S&P 500 slipped.

Here’s the comparison. In March 2020, the Fed was slashing rates, buying bonds and throwing emergency liquidity at a financial system under immense pressure. Congress approved a $2.2 trillion rescue package to keep households and businesses afloat.

Today, we are watching markets fall while the Fed is possibly making money more expensive.

Bitcoin Price Under Pressure as the Fed Flags Leverage Risks

Bitcoin (BTC)
24h7d30d1yAll time

October’s FOMC minutes weren’t exactly what markets wanted to hear. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% during its October meeting, but almost all participants believed further increases would likely be appropriate. Two officials also said a hike larger than the usual 25 basis points could be considered if inflation data came in hotter than expected.

And there was more in those minutes than just interest rates. Officials raised concerns about hedge fund leverage and the growing debt tied to artificial intelligence investments. Some financing arrangements could become a problem if investors start questioning enormous AI spending, and whether it will generate the returns companies expect.

The risk is forced selling. Leveraged funds facing losses or investor withdrawals may have to dump assets quickly, potentially pushing prices down further.

Gold has its own problem. A stronger dollar and higher interest rates make it less attractive to investors who can earn a return elsewhere. Bitcoin price, meanwhile, remains vulnerable when traders cut exposure to speculative assets.

The Fed hasn’t declared a financial emergency. Its minutes actually describe the banking system as resilient. But officials are clearly paying attention to risks that could amplify a market shock.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Remember March 2020? The Fed Cut Rates to Zero and Washington Spent $2.2T

March 2020 was brutal. COVID-19 lockdowns brought businesses to a standstill. Investors rushed for cash, stocks collapsed, and Bitcoin briefly slipped below $4,000 after sitting near $10,000 just weeks earlier.

The Federal Reserve didn’t wait around. It cut rates by 50 basis points on March 3, then delivered another 100-basis-point cut on March 15. The federal funds target range dropped to 0%–0.25%.

On March 23, the Fed announced unlimited purchases of Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities, promising to buy whatever amounts were necessary to support market functioning. It also introduced emergency lending programmes to keep credit flowing.

President Donald Trump signed the $2.2 trillion CARES Act on March 27. The package included direct payments to eligible Americans, expanded unemployment benefits, and assistance for businesses struggling to survive lockdowns. The Paycheck Protection Program gave small businesses access to loans designed to help them keep employees on payroll.

The response was enormous, but the economy was facing an extraordinary shutdown. Millions of Americans had lost their jobs, businesses were closing, and normal economic activity had practically disappeared.

Markets eventually bounced back. The S&P 500 recovered its pre-pandemic record by August 2020. Bitcoin climbed above $12,000 during the same month.

Should Washington Pull Off Another $2.2T Rescue?

The current US economy isn’t in the same position as it was during the pandemic. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, and policymakers are discussing rate increases rather than cuts.

Slashing rates to zero and flooding markets with liquidity might help asset prices. It could also make inflation worse. Another multitrillion-dollar spending package would face an entirely different argument in Congress, especially without a pandemic-style economic shutdown.

The Fed doesn’t have to choose between doing nothing and repeating the 2020 rescue. If banks struggle to fund themselves or credit markets start freezing, it can step in with emergency lending and liquidity operations. That’s a much narrower response than another round of unlimited bond purchases.

The Fed’s concerns about leveraged hedge funds and AI financing could become more relevant if investors start selling indiscriminately. A market correction is one thing. Forced selling spreading through the financial system is another.

At the moment, there’s no evidence that we’re facing another March 2020. The banking system remains resilient, and falling Bitcoin prices alone won’t trigger a government bailout.

But the Fed has a problem that didn’t exist in quite the same way during the pandemic. It may need to protect financial stability without giving up its fight against inflation. In 2020, Washington opened the taps. This time, we wait and see, and Bitcoin price will survive.

title: From Bitcoin to AI: A $1.2 Billion Bet That Could Backfire
description: One question is very interesting: does AI represents a lifeline for struggling Bitcoin miners—or simply a more expensive gamble?
fullContent:
As you may already know, the race to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom is pushing former Bitcoin miners into new territory, and for some companies, this bet is seemingly becoming increasingly risky.

Hyperscale Data (GPUS), a well-known Bitcoin miner, has completely emptied its BTC reserves, selling approximately 1,113 BTC for $74 million since July. The goal is to reinvent its Michigan mining facility as an AI data center and potentially unlock a $1.2 billion revenue opportunity.

There’s a catch, though. The firm may not have enough money to get there, even after completely depleting its Bitcoin stash.

According to the latest regulatory filing, Hyperscale Data still needs another $74.8 million by March to complete the infrastructure. At the end of September this year, it held just $17 million in unrestricted cash, while also facing a staggering $231 million in current liabilities.

The financial pressure is now raising serious questions about whether its ambitious AI pivot can even succeed.

And that impressive $1.2 billion, headline-grabbing deal isn’t exactly a given. It depends on a customer extending an initial 10-year agreement twice and Hyperscale successfully delivering the promised computing capacity.

Now, this situation highlights something important: a dilemma across the crypto mining industry of a sort. Companies are pivoting from Bitcoin mining in pursuit of AI infrastructure contracts, attracted by potentially profitable long-term revenues.

However, transforming mining facilities into AI computing hubs demands, as you can imagine, serious upfront capital, reliable financing, and flawless execution.

For Hyperscale, the irony is rather difficult to ignore, because the firm sold all of its Bitcoin to chase the AI hype but is now facing a liquidity crunch that could threaten its entire transformation.

title: Ant, DBS Use Blockchain Cash to Buy Tokenized Funds
description:
Summary Cash stays locked until fund tokens move Pilot ran under Singapore’s MAS-led BLOOM initiative Builds on DBS-Ant Treasury Tokens […]
The post Ant, DBS Use Blockchain Cash to Buy Tokenized Funds appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Summary

  • Cash stays locked until fund tokens move
  • Pilot ran under Singapore’s MAS-led BLOOM initiative
  • Builds on DBS-Ant Treasury Tokens from 2024
  • Values, timings and fees remain undisclosed

Ant International announced the Whale Orchestration Protocol, which connects tokenized deposits and money market funds through its WhaleRTP wholesale settlement platform, and published a whitepaper explaining how the link works.

The deposit rail already existed. The fund leg is new

Ant and DBS have been building toward this since August 2024, when DBS launched a Treasury Tokens pilot with Ant International for round-the-clock treasury and liquidity management. Those tokens run on DBS’s permissioned, EVM-compatible blockchain, which is wired into the bank’s core payments engine and connected to Ant’s Whale treasury platform. The original aim was internal: moving Ant’s own money between its entities in seconds rather than days.

The new pilot points that rail outward. The partners completed transactions linking DBS Treasury Tokens with Franklin Templeton’s tokenized money market fund solutions. The cash leg is a bank deposit token; the asset leg is a fund unit recorded on a separate system.

The work sits under BLOOM, an initiative the Monetary Authority of Singapore launched in October 2025 to support settlement in tokenized bank liabilities and well-regulated stablecoins. Corporate treasury management is one of its named wholesale use cases, and Ant International co-leads BLOOM’s work on programmable compliance controls.

The two assets carry different legal claims. A tokenized deposit is a claim on DBS; a tokenized fund unit is an interest in a fund. Recording both on blockchains gives them a common format but leaves them on separate ledgers, and that separation is the problem the protocol sets out to solve.

A lien replaces “you go first”

Securities markets handle this with delivery versus payment, or DvP. BIS research describes it as tying delivery to payment so that neither happens without the other. That removes principal risk: paying and never receiving the asset, or delivering it and never being paid.

Inside one ledger, DvP can run as a single transaction. Across two, something has to hold one side still while the other moves. The whitepaper’s answer is a lien on the deposit tokens. The owner keeps legal ownership, but the cash can’t be spent elsewhere while it is committed to the trade. Once the fund side’s issuance or cancellation of tokens is verified, the payment is released.

The protocol itself validates and relays transaction states between the two systems. The paper describes it as neither an asset bridge nor a settlement ledger: deposit tokens stay on DBS’s chain, fund units stay with the fund, and nothing is wrapped into a third token. The fund keeps its own eligibility, compliance, transfer-agency and operational controls.

For a treasury, that means no new bridged asset to hold or value. The design relies instead on each ledger reporting its state accurately and on the protocol reading it correctly.

Following $1 million in and out of a fund

Take a treasury with $1 million it won’t need for several weeks. It wants to earn money market yield on the balance and recover the cash before its next supplier payment run. The amount is illustrative, not a figure from the pilot.

Going in: subscription

  1. Lock. $1 million of the treasury’s DBS Treasury Tokens goes under lien. The treasury still owns it.
  2. Issue. After its own checks, the fund issues units to the treasury as tokens.
  3. Release. The protocol confirms issuance, and the locked cash is paid to the fund.

Coming out: redemption

  1. Lock. The cash that will pay the redemption goes under lien.
  2. Cancel. The fund cancels the treasury’s fund tokens.
  3. Release. Cancellation is confirmed, and proceeds arrive as DBS Treasury Tokens.

Based on the workflow in the partners’ whitepaper.

The interval that counts is the one between instruction and confirmation. During it, the $1 million still belongs to the treasury but can’t cover payroll or a supplier invoice. A shorter window means less cash sitting frozen, yet the public material gives no figure for how long that window lasted in the pilot.

The redemption leg also ends somewhere specific: a DBS Treasury Token balance. Whether that’s the end of the journey depends on whom the treasury needs to pay next.

Settlement liquidity isn’t spending liquidity

Treasurers deal with three kinds of liquidity. Investment liquidity is the ability to exit a holding on the fund’s terms. Settlement liquidity is having cash and assets ready at the moment of exchange. Operational liquidity is having usable money in the right account when a payment falls due.

The pilot addresses the second. It makes the swap itself safer and removes the need for either side to trust the other with the first move. The other two kinds of liquidity are left where they were.

Investment liquidity still depends on the fund. Eligibility approval, dealing cut-offs and the price at which units are issued or cancelled are set by the fund’s terms, and those steps come before the final exchange. A treasury that misses a dealing window gains nothing from a faster swap at the end.

Operational liquidity depends on where the proceeds land. A DBS Treasury Token balance can pay a counterparty on the same network. A supplier that banks elsewhere, or invoices in another currency, needs a further transfer or conversion, which the pilot material leaves out. Coindoo’s coverage of the JPMorgan-DBS tokenized-dollar service deals with that next step: moving tokenized dollars between two banks’ networks around the clock.

READ MORE:

Tether’s Payments Bet Goes Beyond Sending USDT

What the pilot hasn’t shown

The announcement leaves out transaction values, measured completion times, fees, which customers can use the service and the exact fund share class. The pilot runs between regulated institutions, and nothing in the material points to purchases through public crypto wallets.

Three figures would show whether the design helps a working treasury: how long a typical lien stays in place, how often instructions fail or need correcting, and how quickly redemption proceeds can settle a payment outside the DBS network. The last of those decides whether a fund holding can stand in for cash on a payment day.

title: Anthropic Hits $1.5 Trillion Valuation: What It Means for IPO Investors Today?
description: Ultimately, Anthropic's IPO represents both the extraordinary potential of artificial intelligence and the growing challenge of determining how much that potential is worth.
fullContent:
Anthropic’s pricing is through, and the initial public offering (IPO) that will take place today now has a starting point of $83 per share. This gives the company a valuation of around $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

As we reported earlier, the initial price target was between $70 and $78 per share, meaning that there is strong investor demand for the AI company. But what does this mean for IPO investors?

What Does This Mean for Investors?

The offering, which seeks to be worth approximately $81 billion, ranks amongst the largest IPOs in history, but that was relatively expected. We always knew that the valuation would be staggering. Now that the firm is set to start trading on Nasdaq under the ANT ticker, let’s examine what implications the pricing carries.

First things first, the $1.5 trillion valuation reflects massive expectations for the future growth of the company. Investors are clearly betting that enterprise adoption of artificial intelligence, rising demand for Claude, and continued advances in AI capabilities will translate into substantial long-term revenue growth.

However, there is one more thing that needs to be said out loud – such a high valuation leaves very little room for disappointment.

Anthropic already faces serious competition by the likes of OpenAI, Google, and other tech giants. Meanwhile, developing and operating advanced AI models requires tremendous investments in computing infrastructure, putting pressure on profitability and cash flow.

What this means for IPO investors is that the key question will be whether Anthropic can grow fast enough to justify this tremendous valuation.

Strong demand could potentially push the shares signficantly above the $83 offering price during early trading, but a higher entry price would also naturally increase the valuation risk.

title: Tether’s Payments Bet Goes Beyond Sending USDT
description:
Key takeaways Tether and Further added roughly $10 million MetaComp’s router can bypass stablecoins entirely 24-hour settlement claim lacks a […]
The post Tether’s Payments Bet Goes Beyond Sending USDT appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key takeaways

  • Tether and Further added roughly $10 million
  • MetaComp’s router can bypass stablecoins entirely
  • 24-hour settlement claim lacks a stated endpoint
  • Conversion costs can outweigh blockchain fees

MetaComp disclosed the funding in an announcement that extends its Pre-A round to about $45 million.

What Tether and Further are paying for

The new money builds on a $35 million Pre-A and Pre-A+ round that MetaComp completed in March, backed by investors including Alibaba, Sky9 Capital and Noah. The release does not say how the latest $10 million splits between its two investors.

Further Asset Management is an Abu Dhabi-based firm that invests in financial infrastructure and digital assets. Managing partner Faisal Al Hammadi said MetaComp fits its focus on the infrastructure behind institutional adoption.

Tether’s stated reasons are more specific. CEO Paolo Ardoino pointed to the payment corridors linking Asia, the Middle East and Africa, saying “regulated stablecoin infrastructure can change that.” He described those corridors as places where Tether sees room for USDT and its gold-backed XAUT token. The company frames the investment as part of building infrastructure in emerging markets, where faster and cheaper settlement matters most. That fits the broader push of stablecoins into cross-border payments.

MetaComp says the capital will go to licenses, compliance and additional payment channels in priority markets. Singapore’s MAS directory lists it as a Major Payment Institution licensed for cross-border money transfer and digital payment token services. That license covers its Singapore activity, not every market where a supplier might be paid, which helps explain why licenses top the spending list. The company says it already connects with more than 60 financial institutions and 170 payment service providers and supports 60 currencies.

A router that doesn’t have to pick USDT

The product at the center of the deal is StableX. Its product page says an intelligent routing engine chooses between stablecoin and US dollar rails based on cost, speed and settlement certainty, and it names USDT and USDC among the supported tokens. A payment through MetaComp can therefore travel as USDT, as USDC or as a conventional dollar transfer, without the customer holding a crypto wallet.

That makes Tether’s return harder to read than the headline figure suggests. Whenever the engine picks USDC or a bank rail, Tether’s token never moves. Whatever the route, the investment does buy a stake in a licensed firm that controls the parts of a payment USDT cannot handle alone: the bank connections, the currency conversion and the compliance checks, in corridors Tether has named as priorities.

MetaComp’s volume figure does not show how often USDT wins. The company reports more than $1 billion in monthly processing volume as of October 30, but it also runs wealth products and reports more than $600 million in assets under management. The release gives no breakdown by product, payment rail or stablecoin, so USDT’s share of that billion is not public.

Where each side starts and finishes also shapes whether USDT helps. A sender that already holds USDT skips a purchase, and a supplier willing to keep stablecoins skips a bank payout. A supplier that wants local currency in its bank account needs both ends handled. Coindoo’s guide to crypto payments covers how each of those legs works.

Where a stablecoin payment can stall

When a business pays an overseas supplier in local currency, the token transfer is only the middle of five stages, and each stage has its own sources of delay and cost.

1. Funding

Can delay: wire timing at the sender’s bank, onboarding and identity review

Can cost: outgoing bank fees

2. Fiat to stablecoin

Can delay: sanctions and transaction screening

Can cost: conversion spread or fee

3. On-chain transfer

Can delay: network confirmations, Travel Rule data exchange between providers

Can cost: network fee, usually the smallest item

4. Local conversion

Can delay: sourcing liquidity in less-traded currencies

Can cost: spread against the market rate

5. Bank payout

Can delay: local banking hours, cut-off times, receiving-bank checks

Can cost: payout and receiving-bank fees

Only the third stage runs purely on a blockchain. The other four depend on banks, liquidity providers and compliance teams, the same areas MetaComp says the new funding will strengthen.

The 24-hour claim has no stated finish line

According to the release, MetaComp’s hybrid model cuts settlement from 2–7 days to within 24 hours on corridors connecting Asia, the Middle East and Africa. It does not say when that clock starts or stops: when the receiving provider gets the tokens, when local conversion completes or when the supplier’s bank credits the account. It also does not say which conventional route the 2–7 day baseline describes.

No per-corridor results are published, and the release does not say how it counts payments held for extra review or sent over a weekend. StableX advertises round-the-clock foreign exchange, but the final credit still depends on the receiving country’s payment system, and not all of those run around the clock.

READ MORE:

Crypto Traders Can Get 3x Equity Exposure Through Spot Tokens

On a $10,000 transfer, the chain fee is the small number

A BIS working paper published on October 19 by Wenxin Du, Catherine Huang and David Scharfstein compares bank, fintech and stablecoin routes. The authors find that converting between fiat and stablecoins runs through exchanges and other intermediaries whose trading, conversion and withdrawal fees can substantially raise the total cost. They also find liquidity between dollar stablecoins and non-US currencies is generally very thin. Where stablecoins offered better exchange rates on some transfers into emerging markets, the paper attributes the gap to capital controls rather than to the technology. The paper does not assess MetaComp.

It does give benchmarks for the alternatives. In a small sample, bank wires carried exchange-rate markups of roughly 2% to 4.7% before explicit wire fees. Fintech money transfer operators charged a median of about $40 to $60 to send $10,000 from the US into developed-market currencies. In both cases, the currency conversion drives the cost, not the transfer itself.

The same holds inside a stablecoin route. On a hypothetical $10,000 payment, a 0.50% conversion spread costs $50. Cutting the network fee from $5 to $1 saves $4, while trimming that spread to 0.20% saves $30. These are illustrative inputs, not MetaComp’s prices.

MetaComp labels the rates it displays as indicative and non-binding, subject to market conditions at execution. The figure that matters is the firm quote a customer accepts, measured as the amount debited against the amount the supplier receives, using the same reference rate for every route being compared.

Tether has bought into the parts of a payment that USDT cannot complete on its own: the licenses, bank links and currency conversion at each end. MetaComp has not disclosed how often its own router decides USDT is the best way through. That number would say more about the value of Tether’s stake than the size of the check.
